translation.title: Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries

translation.quality: The source edition describes its English as machine-assisted and post-edited and cautions that errors may remain. These passages were extracted from the al-Tabari-labeled sections; they have not been independently checked against the Arabic.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Prophet, fear God by obeying Him, performing His obligations, fulfilling His rights upon you, refraining from what He has forbidden, and violating His limits. And do not obey the disbelievers who say to you: Drive away from you your followers from among the weak believers in you so that we may sit with you. “And the hypocrites” who show you faith in God and sincere advice to you, but they spare no effort in ruining you, your companions, and your religion. So do not accept their opinion, and do not consult them, seeking their advice, for they are your enemies. Indeed, God is Knowing and Wise. He says: God is All-Knowing, All-Wise in managing your affairs, your companions’ affairs, your religion, and other matters of managing all of His creation.
h
And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord

. He says: And do what God sends down to you of His revelation, and the verses of His Book. Indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Knowing. He says: Indeed, God is ever, with what you and your companions do of this Qur'an, and other matters of yours and the matters of His servants, Knowing: that is, He is All-Aware, nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He will reward you for that with what He promised you of recompense. And in a manner similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement,
h
And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord
, he said: People of interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord
meaning this Qur’an. Indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Knowing.

x: God Almighty says: And entrust your affair to God, O Muhammad, and trust in Him. And sufficient is God as a Disposer of affairs. He says: And sufficient for you is God in what He commands you as a Disposer of affairs and a Guardian of your affairs.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of God’s statement,
h
God has not made for any man two hearts within him

Some of them said: He meant by that to refute a group of hypocrites who described God’s Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as having two hearts, so God denied that about His Prophet and called them liars.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Nufayl narrated to us, saying: Zuhair ibn Muawiyah narrated to us, on the authority of Qabus ibn Abi Dhibyan, that his father narrated to him, saying:
m: “We said to Ibn Abbas: ‘Have you seen the statement of God, ‘
h
God has not made for any man two hearts within him

,’ what does He mean by that?’ He said: One day the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and prayed, and a thought crossed his mind, so the hypocrites who were praying with him said: ‘He has two hearts, one heart with you and one heart with them.’ So God revealed, ‘
h
God has not made for any man two hearts within him

x: Others said: Rather, he meant by that: a man from Quraish who was called the two-hearted because of his cunning.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
God has not made for any man two hearts within him
. He said: There was a man from Quraysh who was called, because of his cunning, the one with two hearts, so God revealed this about him.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, God has not made for any man two hearts in his body. He said: A man from Banu Fihr said: There are two hearts in my body, and I have a better mind with each one of them than the mind of Muhammad and he lied.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
God has not made for any man two hearts within him

, Qatada said: There was a man during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who was called the one with two hearts, so God revealed about him what you hear. Qatada said: Al-Hasan used to say: There was a man who used to say: I have a soul that commands me, and a soul that forbids me. So God revealed about him what you hear.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: There was a man called Dhu al-Qalbain, so the verse was revealed:
h
God has not made for any man two hearts within him

x: Others said: Rather, he meant Zayd ibn Haritha because the Messenger of God, may God bless him Surat al-Ahzab 33:4
h
God has not made for any man two hearts within him

, nor has He made your wives of whom you declare to be divorced your mothers, nor has He made your adopted sons your sons. That is only your statement with your mouths, and God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. and grant him peace, had adopted him, so God used that as an example.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri,
m: regarding his statement,
h
God has not made for any man two hearts within him

, he said: We have been informed that this was in the case of Zayd bin Haritha, God struck an example for him, saying: The son of another man is not your son. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of those who said: That is a denial from God Almighty of the saying of the one who said about a man who has two hearts in his chest with which he can reason, in the manner narrated from Ibn Abbas. It is possible that this is a denial from God of the one who described the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with that, and that it is a denial of the one who called the Qurayshite who was mentioned to have been called the one with two hearts because of his cunning. Whichever of the two matters it is, it is a denial from God that His men created him would have that characteristic. And His statement,
h
And He has not made your wives of whom you say

, ‘You are like the backs of our mothers,’ your mothers. God Almighty says: And God has not made, O men, your wives of whom you say, ‘You are like the backs of our mothers,’ your mothers. Rather, He made that of what you said a lie, and imposed upon you a punishment as expiation. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And He has not made your wives of whom you declare to be divorced your mothers means He has not made her your mother
. So if a man declares to be divorced from his wife, then God has not made her his mother, but He has made expiation for her. And His statement,
h
And He has not made your adopted sons your sons

, means: God did not make the one you claimed to be your son, who is someone else’s son, your son by your claim. It was mentioned that this was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because of his adoption of Zayd ibn Haritha. The narration mentioned that:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Your adopted sons are your adopted sons
, he said: This verse was revealed about Zayd ibn Haritha.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And He has not made your adopted sons your sons

, he said: Zayd ibn Haritha, when God and His Messenger bestowed His favor upon him, was called: Zayd ibn Muhammad, he was a prophet, so God said, Muhammad is not the father of any of your men (al-Ahzab 33:40). He said: He is mentioning wives and sisters, so He informed him that wives were not your mothers, nor were your adopted sons your sons.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
And He has not made your adopted sons your sons
, and And He has not made your adopted son your son, he says: If a man claims a man who is not his son,
h
That is your statement with your mouths
... the verse, and he mentioned to us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: Whoever claims a father other than his own deliberately, God will forbid him Paradise.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Zaydah narrated to us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Amir, who said:
m: There is no Zayd among the claimants. His statement,
h
That is your statement with your mouths

, means that the Almighty says this statement, which is the man’s statement to his wife: You are to me like my mother’s back, and his claiming that someone who is not his son is his son. It is only your statement with your mouths and has no reality. The lineage of the one whose son you claim is not proven by this claim, and the wife does not become a mother by the man’s statement to her: You are to me like my mother’s back. “And God speaks the truth,” means: God is the Truthful One who speaks the truth, and by His statement the lineage of the one whose lineage he has established is proven, and by it the woman becomes a mother to the child if He rules thus. And He guides to the way, means the Almighty says: And God makes clear to His servants the path of truth, and guides them to the path of right conduct.

x: God the Almighty says: Ascribe your adopted sons, whose lineage you have traced back to you, to your fathers. He says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Ascribe Zayd’s lineage to his father Haritha, and do not call him Zayd ibn Muhammad. And His statement,
h
It is more just in the sight of God

, means that calling them by their fathers is more just in the sight of God, and more truthful and correct than calling them by other than their fathers and attributing them to those who adopted them and claimed them even though they were not his sons.

c: Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Call them by the names of their fathers
h
it is more just in the sight of God
. That is, more just in the sight of God. And His statement,
h
But if you do not know their fathers

, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients. God, the Exalted, says: If you, O people, do not know who the fathers of your adopted sons are, so that you attribute them to them, and you do not know them, so that you associate them with them, then they are your brothers in religion. He says: They are your brothers in religion, if they are from the people of your religion, and your clients if they are your freedmen and not your sons. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Call them by the names of their fathers
h
it is more just in the sight of God
. That is, more just in the sight of God.
h
But if you do not know their fathers
, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients. But if you do not know who his father is, then he is only your brother and client.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Uyaynah ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, he said: Abu Bakra said:
m: God said: “
h
Call them by the names of their fathers
h
it is more just in the sight of God
h
But if you do not know their fathers

, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients.” So we are among those whose fathers are not known, and I am one of your brothers in religion. He said: My father said: By God, I think that if he had known that his father was a donkey, he would have claimed to be his father. And His statement,
h
And there is no blame upon you for that in which you have erred

, means: There is no blame upon you or sin for a mistake you may make in attributing some of those you attribute to his father, while you see him as the son of the one to whom they attribute him, while he is the son of someone else. But what your hearts intended, means: But the sin and blame are upon you for attributing him to someone other than his father, while you know that he is the son of someone other than the one to whom you attribute him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And there is no blame upon you for that in which you have erred

meaning: If you call a man by someone other than his father, and you think that is the case, but [it is] what your hearts intended God says: Do not call him by someone other than his father intentionally. As for the mistake, God will not hold you accountable for it but He will hold you accountable for what your hearts intended.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Your hearts deliberately did it. He said: Deliberate is what comes after clarification and prohibition in this and other things, and the ma in his statement, but what your hearts deliberately did is in the accusative case in response to the ma in his statement, in what you erred in. That is because the meaning of the statement is: There is no blame upon you for what you erred in, but for what your hearts deliberately did. And His statement,
h
And God is Forgiving and Merciful

, God Almighty says: And God is the One who conceals the sin of one who divorces his wife and speaks falsehood and lies, and the sin of one who claims that someone else’s child is his own, if they repent and return to God’s command, and stop saying falsehood after their Lord forbade them from it, out of mercy towards them, that He does not punish them for that after they repent from their sin.

x: God Almighty says: The Prophet Muhammad is more deserving of the believers, meaning: He is more deserving of the believers in him than they are of themselves, that he may rule over them as he wishes, and that is permissible for them.

c: Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibn Zayd said:
m: The Prophet is closer to the believers than they are to themselves, just as you are closer to your servant. Whatever you decide concerning them is permissible, just as whatever you decide concerning your servant is permissible.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, The Prophet is closer to the believers than they are to themselves. He said: He is a father to them. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated: Uthman ibn Umar narrated: Falih narrated: Hilal ibn Ali narrated: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Umrah narrated: Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no believer but that I am closer to him in this world and the Hereafter. Read, if you wish, ‘The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves.’ And any believer who leaves behind wealth, it goes to his heirs and relatives, whoever they may be. But if he leaves behind a debt or a loss, let him come to me, and I will be his protector.”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Hasan bin Ali told us, on the authority of Abu Musa Isra’il bin Musa, who said:
m: Al-Hasan recited this verse: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves,
h
and his wives are their mothers

. He said: Al-Hasan said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am closer to every believer than his own self. Al-Hasan said: In the first recitation: Nearer to the believers than their own selves, and he is a father to them.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said
m: in some of the readings The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves and he is a father to them and he mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Any man who leaves behind a loss, I have more right to it, and if he leaves behind wealth, it is for his heirs. His saying,
h
And his wives are their mothers

, means: The sanctity of his wives is the same as the sanctity of their mothers for them, in that it is forbidden for them to marry them after his death, just as it is forbidden for them to marry their mothers. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves,
h
and his wives are their mothers
. He thus magnifies their right, and in some readings: And he is a father to them.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, and their wives are their mothers, they are forbidden to them. And His statement,
h
And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the Book of God than the believers and the emigrants

, God Almighty says: And those of kinship who inherit from one another are nearer to the inheritance of one another than the believers and the emigrants, by migration and faith rather than by kinship. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the ordinance of God than the believers and the emigrants

. The Muslims remained for a period of time inheriting from one another through emigration, and the Muslim Bedouin did not inherit anything from the emigrants, so God revealed this verse, and the believers mixed with one another, so inheritances became by religions.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the ordinance of God than the believers and the emigrants

, unless you do to your relatives a kindness, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had established brotherhood between the emigrants and the helpers when the emigration began, and they inherited from each other based on that. God said, “And for each We have appointed heirs from that which parents and near relatives leave, and those with whom you have made a covenant. So give them their share”
r
(An-Nisa’: 33)

. He said: If there is no kinship, this prevents them. He said: This was the first, then God said, Unless you do to your relatives a kindness, meaning: Unless you make a bequest to them. That was written in the ordinance, that those of kinship are nearer to each other in the ordinance of God. He said: And the believers and the emigrants did not inherit from each other if they were relatives, until they emigrated to Madinah. And he recited, God said, And those who believed but did not emigrate - you have no share in their guardianship until they emigrate
r
(Anfal: 72)

until His saying, and great corruption. (al-Anfal 8:73), and they did not inherit from one another, until the year of the conquest came, and migration ceased and Islam became widespread. No one was accepted to be on the same path as the Prophet and those with him unless he migrated. He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to those he sent: Go out in the name of God, do not transgress and do not turn away. Invite them to Islam. If they respond, then accept and invite them to migrate. If they migrate with you, then they have what you have and are subject to what you are subject to. If they refuse and do not migrate and choose their homes, then leave them there. They are like the Bedouins, and the rulings of Islam apply to them, and they have no share in this booty. He said: When the conquest came and migration ceased, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no migration after the conquest.” Islam became widespread, and people inherited from their kin wherever they were. That which had been between the believers and the emigrants was abrogated, and they had a share in the booty, even if they stayed and refused. Their right in Islam was one, the emigrant and the non-emigrant, the non-emigrant, the Bedouin and everyone, when the conquest came. The meaning of this interpretation is: Those who are related to one another are more deserving of inheritance than the believers and emigrants are of one another, due to their emigration. The apparent meaning of this statement may be that those who are related to one another are more deserving of inheritance than those who did not believe and did not emigrate. And His statement,
h
Except that you do to your relatives a kindness
, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation.

x: Some of them said: The meaning of that is: Except that you make a bequest to your relatives who are not people of faith and emigration.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Ibn al-Hanafiyyah:
m: Unless you do good to your relatives. They said: He makes a will for his relatives from among the polytheists. He said: Abda told us, he said: I read on the authority of Ibn Abi Arubah, on the authority of Qatada, Unless you do good to your relatives. He said: Relatives of polytheists have a will, but they do not have an inheritance.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, Except that you do good to your allies, he said: To your allies from the people of polytheism, a will, and they have no inheritance.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri and Yahya Ibn Adam told us, on the authority of Ibn Al-Mubarak, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Yahya Ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: To your guardians be kind. He said: A will.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: I said to Ata’: What is His statement, except that you do to your allies a kindness,? He said: The gift. So I said to him: The believer is related to the unbeliever, between them is a kinship. He said: Yes, his gift to him is a gift and a bequest to him.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: unless you adhere to what is right among you through the right of faith, migration, and alliance, then you give them their right of support and blood money.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asam told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, except that you do to your allies a kindness, he said: Your allies among whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was allied, from among the Muhajireen and the Ansar, by holding fast to what is right, reason, and support among them.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: that you should make a will to your guardians from among the immigrants.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: Except that you do good to your guardians meaning: Except that you make a will for them. The most correct of the sayings on this matter, in my opinion, is to say: The meaning of this is that you should do to your allies, whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, established brotherhood with you, from among the Muhajireen and Ansar, what is known by giving them a will, supporting them, paying blood money for them, and the like, because all of that is from the good that God has urged His servants to do. Rather, I have chosen this statement and said: It is more correct than what was said by those who said: Surat al-Ahzab 33:6 The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves,
h
and his wives are their mothers

. And those of kinship are closer to one another in the ordinance of God than the believers and the emigrants, unless you do to your relatives a kindness. That is already written in the Book. What is meant by that is the will for relatives from the polytheists, because the relative of the polytheist, even if he is related, is not a client, and that is because polytheism severs the guardianship between the believer and the polytheist, and God has forbidden the believers to take them as allies in His saying:
h
Do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies
Al-Mumtahanah 66:1. It is not permissible for Him to forbid them from taking them as allies, and then He, the Most High, describes them as their allies. The position of that in His saying:
h
unless you do so

is in the accusative case of exception. The meaning of the statement: And those of kinship are closer to one another in the Book of God than the believers and the emigrants, unless you do to your allies who are not of kinship from you a kindness. And his saying,
h
That was written in the Book

, means: Those of kinship were more deserving of one another in the Book of God: that is, in the Preserved Tablet, written: that is, written, as the rajaz poet said: In the first newspapers that were written And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
That was written in the Book
, meaning that relatives are closer to one another in the Book of God.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: It was written in the book: The polytheist does not inherit from the believer.

evidence.text: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Hasan bin Ali told us, on the authority of Abu Musa Isra’il bin Musa, who said: Al-Hasan recited this verse: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers.
Al-Hasan said: In the first recitation: Nearer to the believers than their own selves, and he is a father to them.

Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said in some of the readings The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves and he is a father to them and he mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Any man who leaves behind a loss, I have more right to it, and if he leaves behind wealth, it is for his heirs.

x: God Almighty says: That was written in the Book, as We wrote everything that is in the Book. And when We took from the prophets their covenant That was also written in the Book, and what is meant by the covenant is the promise, and We have explained that with its evidence in what came before. And from you O Muhammad and from Noah and Abraham and Moses and Jesus, the son of Mary,
h
and We took from them a firm covenant
He says: And We took from all of them a firm covenant that they would believe one another.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And when We took a covenant from the prophets

, and from you and from Noah, he said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say, I was the first of the prophets in creation, and the last of them in the mission, “and Abraham and Moses and Jesus, the son of Mary,
h
and We took from them a firm covenant
,” a covenant that God took from the prophets, specifically that some of them would believe in others, and that some of them would follow others.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Sulayman told us: Abu Hilal told us:
m: When Qatada recited this verse,
h
And when We took a covenant from the prophets
, and from you and from Noah, he said: “The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was among the first of the prophets in creation.”

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, From the prophets is their covenant, and from you and from Noah, he said: On the back of Adam.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We took from them a firm covenant
, he said: The firm covenant is the pledge.

evidence.text: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Sulayman told us: Abu Hilal told us: When Qatada recited this verse, And when We took a covenant from the prophets, and from you and from Noah, he said: “The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was among the first of the prophets in creation.”

x: God Almighty says: We took a covenant from these prophets so that I might ask the messengers about what their nations answered them with, and what their people did with the message they conveyed to them from their Lord. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: To ask the truthful about their truthfulness. He said: The messengers who conveyed the message.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, That He may ask the truthful about their truthfulness, he said: The messengers who conveyed the message.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: To ask the truthful about their truthfulness. He said: The messengers who carry out and convey the message.

x: God Almighty says,
h
O you who have believed

, remember the favor of God upon you, which He bestowed upon your community when the Muslims were besieged with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during the Battle of the Trench.
h
When there came to you armies
: the armies of the confederates: Quraysh, Ghatafan, and the Jews of Banu Nadir.
h
So We sent upon them a wind
, which is, according to what was mentioned, the north wind.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abd Al-A’la told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: “The south side said to the north side on the night of the Confederates: Go, let us support the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The north side said: A free woman does not travel at night. He said: So it was the wind that sent down upon them.”

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Amir told us: Al-Zubayr told us,
m: meaning Ibn Abdullah, who told us: Rabih bin Abi Saeed told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abi Saeed, who said: “We said on the day of the Trench: O Messenger of God, hearts have reached the throats, so is there anything you can say? He said: Yes, say: O God, cover our faults and calm our fears. So God struck the faces of His enemies with the wind, and God defeated them with the wind.”

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Abdullah bin Amr told me, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: “My uncle Uthman bin Maz’un sent me on the night of the Trench in intense cold and wind to Madinah, and he said: Bring us food and a blanket. I asked permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he gave me permission and said: ‘Whoever you meet of my companions, tell them to return.’ So I went and the wind was blowing everything away, and I did not meet anyone except that I told them to return to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Not one of them turned his neck. He said: I had a shield with me, and the wind was hitting it on me, and it had iron in it. He said: The wind hit it until some of the iron fell on my hand and penetrated it to the ground.” Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated: Yazid ibn Ziyad narrated: Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi narrated: “A young man from Kufa said to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman: ‘O Abu Abdullah, did you see the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and accompany him?’ He said: ‘Yes, O my nephew.’ He said: ‘Then how did you act?’ He said: ‘By God, we were struggling.’ The young man said: ‘By God, if we had caught up with him, we would not have let him walk on the ground. We would have carried him on our shoulders.’ Hudhayfah said: ‘O my nephew, by God, I saw us with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) at the Trench, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) prayed a part of the night, then he turned to us and said: ‘Who is the man who will stand and see for us what the people did?’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) stipulated that if I return, God will admit me into Paradise.’ But no one got up. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) prayed a part of the night, then he turned to us and said the same thing, but no one of us got up. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) prayed a part of the night, then he turned to us and said: ‘Who is the man who will stand and see for us what the people did?’ The people, then he returns - the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stipulated for him to return - I ask God to be my companion in Paradise. No man got up from the intensity of fear, the intensity of hunger, and the intensity of cold. When no one got up, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called me, and I had no choice but to get up when he called me. He said: O Hudhayfah, go and enter among the people and see what they do, and do not say anything until you come to us. He said: So I went and entered among the people, and the wind and the soldiers of God were doing to them what they were doing, leaving them no pot, no fire, and no building. Abu Sufyan said: O people of Quraysh, let a man look at who is sitting with him. Hudhayfah said: So I took the hand of the man next to me and said: Who are you? He said: I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so. Then Abu Sufyan said: O people of Quraysh, by God, you have not become in a permanent place. The hooves and hoofs have been destroyed, and Banu Qurayzah have differed, and we have heard from them what we dislike. We have experienced from this wind what you see. By God, our pots will not be reassured, our fire will not be able to stand, and our buildings will not hold together. So depart, for I am departing. Then he went to his camel, which was tied up, and sat on it, then struck it, and it jumped on three occasions. It did not release its halter to me while I was standing. Had it not been for the covenant of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that I should not do anything until I came to you, if I wished, I would have killed it with an arrow. Hudhayfah said: So I returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was standing praying in a cloak belonging to one of his wives. When he saw me, he brought me between his legs and threw the edge of the cloak over me. Then he bowed and prostrated while I was wrapped in it. When he had finished, I told him the report. Ghatafan heard what Quraysh had done, so they turned and returned to their country.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, “
h
When there came to you armies
,” he said: The confederates: Uyaynah ibn Badr, Abu Sufyan, and Qurayza. And His statement,
h
So We sent upon them a wind

, he said: The north wind was sent upon the confederates on the day of the Trench, until it tipped their pots over onto their mouths, and tore down their tents until it drove them away. And His statement, and soldiers you did not see, he said: The angels, and they did not fight that day.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
O you who have believed

, remember the favor of God upon you when there came upon you armies, and We sent upon them a wind and armies you did not see, he said: He meant the angels. He said: “This verse was revealed on the Day of the Confederates, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had been besieged for a month, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had dug a trench, and Abu Sufyan came with the Quraysh and those who followed him from the people until they encamped at the place of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Uyaynah ibn Hisn, one of the Banu Badr, and those who followed him from the people came until they encamped at the place of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Jews wrote to Abu Sufyan and supported him, so he said, where God, the Most High, says, “When they came upon you from above you and from below you,” so God sent terror and a wind upon them. It was mentioned to us that whenever they lit a fire, God would extinguish it, until it was mentioned to us that the master of every tribe would say, ‘O sons of so-and-so, come to me,’ until when they had gathered at his house, he said, ‘Escape, escape. You have come to what God has sent.’” They are terrified.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
O you who have believed
, remember the favor of God upon you... the verse, he said: The day of Abu Sufyan was the day of the Confederates.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid bin Ruman told me,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
O you who have believed
, remember the favor of God upon you
h
when there came to you armies

and We sent against them a wind and armies you did not see. The armies were Quraysh, Ghatafan, and Banu Qurayzah, and the armies that God sent against them with the wind were the angels. And His statement, And God is All-Seeing of what you do, God Almighty says: And God was All-Seeing of your deeds on that day, and that was their patience in the face of the effort and hardship they were in, and their steadfastness against their enemy, and other than that of their deeds, and nothing of that was hidden from Him, and He recorded it for them, in order to reward them for it.

x: God Almighty says: And God was Seeing of what you did, when the armies of the confederates came upon you from above you and from below you. And it was said: Those who came upon them from below them were Abu Sufyan in Quraysh and those with him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, When they came upon you from above you, he said: Uyaynah ibn Badr among the people of Najd, and from below you, he said: Abu Sufyan. He said: And the Qurayza confronted them.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abda told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwa, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha:
m: I mentioned the Day of the Trench and recited:
h
When they came upon you from above you and from below you
, and when eyes turned away and hearts reached to the throats. She said: It is the Day of the Trench.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman,
m: a client of the family of Az-Zubayr, on the authority of Urwah ibn Az-Zubayr, and on the authority of someone I do not accuse, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Kaʿb ibn Malik, on the authority of Az-Zuhri, on the authority of ʿAsim ibn ʿUmar ibn Qatadah, on the authority of ʿAbd God ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Hazm, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Kaʿb Al-Qurazi, and on the authority of others among our scholars: It was from the Hadith of the Trench that a group of Jews, including Salam ibn Abi Al-Haqiq An-Nadri, Huyayy ibn Akhtab An-Nadri, Kinanah ibn Ar-Rabiʿ ibn Abi Al-Haqiq An-Nadri, Hudhahah ibn Qays Al-Waʿili, and Abu ʿAmmar Al-Waʿili, with a group of Banu An-Nadir and a group of Banu Waʿil, and they were the ones who formed the confederates against the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), went out until they reached Mecca to the Quraysh, and they called them to war against the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and they said: We will be with you against him until we eradicate him. The Quraysh said to them, "O Jews, you are the people of the first Scripture, and you know what we and Muhammad are disagreeing about. Is our religion better or his?" They said, Rather, your religion is better than his, and you are more deserving of the truth than he. He said: They are the ones about whom God revealed:
h
Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They believe in jibt and taghut and say of those who disbelieve, These are better guided than those who believe in a way
r
(An-Nisa’: 51)
... until His saying:
h
And sufficient is Hell as a Blaze
r
(An-Nisa’: 55)

. So when they said that to the Quraysh, they were pleased with what they said and were encouraged to fight the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So they gathered for that and prepared for it. Then those Jews went out until they came to Ghatafan from Qays Ailan, and they called them to fight the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They informed them that they would be with them in it, and that the Quraysh had followed them in that. So they gathered for it and responded to them. So the Quraysh went out with their leader Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and the Ghatafan went out with their leader Uyaynah ibn Hisn ibn Hudhayfah ibn Badr in the company of Nabi Fazara, and Al-Harith ibn Awf ibn Abi Haritha Al-Murri in the company of Banu Murrah, and Mis’ar ibn Rakhila ibn Nuwayrah Ibn Tarif Ibn Sahmah Ibn Abdullah Ibn Hilal Ibn Khalawah Ibn Ashja Ibn Rayth Ibn Ghatafan, with those who followed him from his people from Ashja. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of them and what they had gathered for him in the matter, he dug the trench around Medina. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished digging the trench, the Quraysh advanced until they encamped at the place where the streams of Ruma met, between al-Jurf and al-Ghaba, with ten thousand of their Abyssinians and those who followed them from Banu Kinanah and the people of Tihamah. The Ghatafan advanced and those who followed them from Najd, until they encamped at Dhaban Nuqma to one side. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out until they turned their backs to Sala’ with three thousand Muslims. He pitched his army there, with the trench between him and the people, and he ordered the children and women to be raised up on the roofs. The enemy of God, Huyayy Ibn Akhtab al-Nadri, went out until he came to Ka’b Ibn Asad al-Qurazi, the one who had made a treaty with Banu Qurayzah, and he had made a truce with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he greeted his people, and made a covenant with him on that, and when Kaʿb heard of Huyayy ibn Akhtab, he closed his fortress to him, and asked permission to enter, but he refused to open it for him. Huyayy called out to him: O Kaʿb, open it for me. He said: “Woe to you, O Huyayy! You are an ill-omened man. I have made a covenant with Muhammad, and I will not break what was between me and him. I have seen nothing from him but loyalty and truthfulness.” He said: Woe to you, open it for me so I may speak to you. He said: I will not do it. He said: By God, if you close it for me, I will fear for your greedy people and eat from them with you. So, be careful of the man, and he opened it for him. He said: “O Kaʿb, I have come to you with the glory of the age and with a vast sea. I have come to you with the Quraysh and their leaders and chiefs, until I have brought them down at the meeting place of the torrents of Rome, and with Ghatafan and their leaders and chiefs, until I have brought them down at the base of the raging rivers near Uhud. They have made a covenant with me and made a covenant with me that they will not leave until they have exterminated Muhammad and those with him.” Kaʿb ibn Asad said to him: By God, you have come to me at the height of time, and in a place whose water has been poured out, thundering and lightning, with nothing in it, so leave me and Muhammad and what I am doing. I have seen nothing from Muhammad but truthfulness and loyalty. My tribe kept attacking Ka’b on the peaks and the lowlands until he allowed him to give them a covenant from God and a pact that if Quraysh and Ghatafan return and do not harm Muhammad, I will enter with you into your fortress until what harms you happens to me. Ka’b bin Asad broke his covenant and disavowed what he had done between himself and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When the report reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Sa’d bin Mu’adh bin An-Nu’man bin Imru’ Al-Qais, one of the Banu Al-Ashhal, who was at that time the chief of the Aws, and Sa’d bin Ubadah bin Daylam, the brother of the Banu Sa’idah bin Ka’b bin Al-Khazraj, who was at that time the chief of the Khazraj, and with them Abdullah bin Rawahah, the brother of Bilharith bin Al-Khazraj, and Khawat bin Jubayr, the brother of the Banu Amr bin Awf. He said: Go. So that you may see whether what we have heard about these people is true or not? If it is true, then be gentle with me with a tune I know, and do not weaken the people’s resolve, even if they are faithful to what is between us and them, then announce it to the people. So they went out until they came to them, and they found them in the worst state of what had been reported about them, and they spoke ill of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: There is no covenant or contract between us and Muhammad. So Saad ibn Ubadah cursed them and they cursed him, and he was a man of sharpness, so Saad ibn Muadh said to him: Stop cursing them, for there is nothing between us and them more severe than cursing. Then Saad and Saad and those with them came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and greeted him, then they said: Adal and al-Qara, meaning like the treachery of Adal and al-Qara against the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the companions of al-Raji’ Khubayb ibn ‘Adi and his companions. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God is Great, be happy, O group of Muslims. And at that time the calamity became great, and fear became intense, and their enemy approached them from above them, and from below them, until the Muslims had every suspicion, and hypocrisy appeared. From some of the hypocrites, until Mu'tab bin Qushair, the brother of Banu Amr bin Awf, said: Muhammad promised us that we would eat the treasures of Chosroes and Caesar, and one of us is not able to go to the toilet. And until Aws bin Qayzi, one of Banu Haritha bin Al-Harith, said: O Messenger of God, our houses are vulnerable to the enemy, and that was from a group of men from his people, so give us permission to return to our home, and it is outside the city. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stayed for twenty-some nights, close to a month, and there was no war between the people except for shooting arrows and siege.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman told me,
m: regarding his statement,
h
When they came upon you from above you and from below you
, those who came upon them from above them were Qurayzah, and those who came upon them from below them were Quraysh and Ghatafan. His saying,
h
And when the eyes turned away
, means: When the eyes turned away from their place and stared aimlessly. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And when the eyes turned away
means stared. His saying,
h
And the hearts reached the throats
, means: The hearts grew out of their places of terror and fear, and reached the throats.

c: As Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: Suwaid bin Amr told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
And the hearts reached the throats
. He said: From fear. And His statement,
h
And you think false thoughts about God
, means:
h
And you think false thoughts about God

, such as the thought of one of them who thought that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would be victorious, and that the victory that God promised him would not happen, and similar false thoughts that were thought by one of those who were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his army.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Hudhahah ibn Khalifa told us, he said: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: And you think about God various thoughts. He said: Different thoughts: The hypocrites thought that Muhammad and his companions would be exterminated, and the believers were certain that what God had promised them was true, that He would make Him prevail over all religions, even if the polytheists hated it. Surat al-Ahzab 33:10
h
When they came upon you from above you and from below you
h
and when the eyes turned away

and the hearts reached to the throats, and you thought about God [various] assumptions. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, And you think about God suspicions. The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the Kufians read it as suspicions with the alif, and likewise, And we obeyed the Messenger, and they led us astray from the path (al-Ahzab 33:66-67) in both connected and paused readings. The weakness of the one who said that was the case for them, was that it is in all the copies of the Qur’an of the Muslims with the alif in all of these letters.

x: Some of the Kufic reciters would keep the alif in them when pausing and delete it when connecting, because they were weak in their reading of the rhymes of poetry and their openings, so they add the alif in the place of the fatha when pausing, but they do not do that in the filling of the verses, because it is good to keep the alifs in these letters, because they are the heads of the verses, representing them with the rhymes.

Some of the readers of Basra and Kufa read it by deleting the alif from all of them in both pause and connection, arguing that this does not exist in the speech of the Arabs except in the rhymes of poetry and not in other speech, and that they only do that in the rhymes in order to complete the meter of the poem, because if they did not do that in them the poem would not be correct. This is not the case in the Qur’an, because there is nothing that compels them to do that in the Qur’an. They said: They are, however, in the copy of Abdullah without the alif. The most correct reading in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of those who read it without the alif in connected and paused recitations, because this is the well-known speech of the Arabs, with the recitation being well-known in this way among the reciters of the two cities: Kufa and Basra. Then the reading with the alif in both cases in pause and connected recitations, because the reason for those who included it in pause is that it is also in the scripts of the Muslim copies of the Qur’an.

If the reason for including the alif in some cases is that it is fixed in the Muslim copies of the Qur’an, then the reading must be fixed in all cases, because it is fixed in their copies. It is not permissible for the reason that necessitates reading this way in some cases to be present in other cases, and the recitation is different, and this is not similar to the rhymes of poetry, because the rhymes of poetry only add alifs in places of fat-ha, ya’ in places of kasra, and waw in places of damma in order to complete the meter. If this was not done in this way, it would be invalidated as it would be impossible to follow its meter. There is nothing that compels the reciter of the Qur’an to do this in the Qur’an.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, And you think about God suspicions.

The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the Kufians read it as suspicions with the alif, and likewise, And we obeyed the Messenger, and they led us astray from the path (al-Ahzab 33:66-67) in both connected and paused readings.

Some of the Kufic reciters would keep the alif in them when pausing and delete it when connecting, because they were weak in their reading of the rhymes of poetry and their openings, so they add the alif in the place of the fatha when pausing, but they do not do that in the filling of the verses, because it is good to keep the alifs in these letters, because they are the heads of the verses, representing them with the rhymes.

Some of the readers of Basra and Kufa read it by deleting the alif from all of them in both pause and connection, arguing that this does not exist in the speech of the Arabs except in the rhymes of poetry and not in other speech, and that they only do that in the rhymes in order to complete the meter of the poem, because if they did not do that in them the poem would not be correct.

The most correct reading in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of those who read it without the alif in connected and paused recitations, because this is the well-known speech of the Arabs, with the recitation being well-known in this way among the reciters of the two cities: Kufa and Basra.

Then the reading with the alif in both cases in pause and connected recitations, because the reason for those who included it in pause is that it is also in the scripts of the Muslim copies of the Qur’an.
If the reason for including the alif in some cases is that it is fixed in the Muslim copies of the Qur’an, then the reading must be fixed in all cases, because it is fixed in their copies.

It is not permissible for the reason that necessitates reading this way in some cases to be present in other cases, and the recitation is different, and this is not similar to the rhymes of poetry, because the rhymes of poetry only add alifs in places of fat-ha, ya’ in places of kasra, and waw in places of damma in order to complete the meter.

x: And His saying,
h
There the believers were tested

, means: At that time the faith of the believers was tested, the people were purified, and the believer was distinguished from the hypocrite. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
There the believers were tested
, he said: They were tested. His saying,
h
And they were shaken with a severe shaking
, means: They were shaken with a severe shaking, and they were tested and tried.

x: And His statement,
h
And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease say

, doubting their faith and weakness in their belief in it: God and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion, and that is according to what was mentioned in the statement of Mu’tab bin Qushair. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: Yazid bin Ruman told me,
m: h
And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said
, ‘God and His Messenger have promised us nothing but delusion.’ He said: Mu’tab bin Qushair, when he said what he said on the day of the Trench.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease will say
, he said: They will speak of hypocrisy on that day, and the believers in God and faith will speak, they will say: This is what God and His Messenger promised us.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said

, ‘God and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion.’ He said: Some of the hypocrites said that: Muhammad had promised us the conquest of Persia and Rome, but he has trapped us here, so that not one of us can even go out to relieve himself. God and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: A man said to a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the Day of the Confederates: O so-and-so, have you seen when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, says: “If Caesar perishes, there will be no Caesar after him, and if Khosrau perishes, there will be no Khosrau after him. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you will surely spend their treasures in the way of God.” How does this compare to that, while one of us cannot even go out to urinate out of fear? God and His Messenger have promised us nothing but delusion. So he said to him: You have lied. I will surely inform the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of your report. So he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. Then he called him and said: What did you say? He said: He lied about me, O Messenger of God. I did not say anything. This never came out of my mouth. God says: They swear by God that they did not say it, but they did say the word of disbelief... (al-Tawbah 9:74) until he reached: And they will have on the earth neither protector nor helper (al-Tawbah 9:74). He said: So this is the saying of God: (If we pardon On behalf of a group of you, We will punish another group. (al-Tawbah 9:66) Ibn Bashar told us:

c: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Uthma told us: Kathir ibn Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Auf al-Muzani told us: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, drew the line of the trench in the year the Confederates were mentioned, from Ahmar al-Shaykhayn, the edge of Banu Haritha, until he reached al-Madhdh. Then he made a distance of forty cubits between every ten. The Muhajirun and the Ansar differed about Salman al-Farsi, and he was a strong man. The Ansar said: Salman is from us, and the Muhajirun said: Salman is from us. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Salman is from us, the people of the house. Amr ibn Auf said: So I, Salman, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, al-Nu’man ibn Muqrin al-Muzani, and six of the Ansar were in a distance of forty cubits. We dug under Dubar until we reached al-Sarra. God brought out from the bottom of the trench a white, marbled rock, which broke our iron and made it difficult for us. We said: O Salman, go up to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and tell him the report of this rock. Either…” Either we turn away from them, for the right path is near, or he orders us to do what he says about it, for we do not like to go beyond his line. So Salman climbed until he came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who had built a Turkish dome over him. He said, “O Messenger of God, may our father and mother be sacrificed for you, a white rock, a marble, came out of the bottom of the trench, and it broke our iron and made it difficult for us, so that neither little nor much could come out of it. So order us to do what you say about it, for we do not like to go beyond your line.” So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) descended into the trench with Salman, and the nine of us climbed the edge of the trench. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) took the pickaxe from Salman and struck the rock with a blow that split it, and a flash of lightning from it illuminated what was between its two lava plains, meaning the two lava plains of Madinah, until it was as if a lamp were in the interior of a dark house. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said the takbir of victory, and the Muslims said the takbir. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) struck it a second time, and it split, and a flash of lightning from it lit up what was between its two lava plates, as if it were a lamp in the interior of a dark house. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said the Takbir of Victory, and the Muslims said the Takbir of Victory. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) struck it a third time, and it broke, and a flash of lightning from it lit up what was between its lava plates, as if it were a lamp in the interior of a dark house. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said the Takbir of Victory. Then he took Salman and his two sons, and Salman said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of God, I have seen something I have never seen before. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) turned to the people and said: Did you see what Sulayman was saying? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God, may our father and mother be sacrificed for you! We saw you strike, and lightning came out like waves. We saw you grow, so we grew, and we saw nothing else. He said, “You have spoken the truth. I struck my first strike, and the lightning that you saw lit up for me the palaces of Al-Hirah and the cities of Kisra, as if they were the fangs of dogs. Gabriel, peace be upon him, informed me that my nation will prevail over them. Then I struck my third strike, and the lightning that you saw lit up for me the palaces of Sana’a, as if they were the fangs of dogs. Gabriel, peace be upon him, informed me that my nation will prevail over them. So rejoice, victory will reach them. Rejoice, victory will reach them. Rejoice, victory will reach them. So the Muslims were filled with joy and said, ‘Praise be to God, a promise that has come true, for He promised us victory after the siege.’ So the confederates closed in, and the Muslims said, ‘This is what God and His Messenger promised us…’… the verse. The hypocrites said, ‘Are you not amazed?’ He talks to you, gives you false hopes and promises you falsehood. He tells you that he sees from Yathrib the palaces of Al-Hirah and the cities of Kisra, and that they will be conquered for you, while you are digging the trench out of fear and are unable to emerge. And the Qur’an was revealed: “
h
And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said
, ‘God and His Messenger have promised us nothing but delusion.’”

x: God Almighty means by His saying,
h
And when a party of them said
, ‘O people of Yathrib,
h
there is no place for you to stay

,’ and when some of them said: O people of Yathrib, and Yathrib is the name of a land, so it is said that the city of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is in a part of Yathrib. And His saying
h
There is no place for you to stay

, so go back with the opening of the m from maqam. He says: There is no place for you to stand in, as the poet said: Whatever evil there is, it will be taken to the place where it will not be seen. His saying,
h
Then go back

, means: Go back to your homes. He ordered them to flee from the army of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to escape from him, and to leave the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said that this was done by Aws ibn Qayzi and those who agreed with him.
Who said that?
Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who narrated:

c: Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me:
m: h
And when a party of them said

, ‘O people of Yathrib…’ to fleeing. He said: Aws ibn Qayzi and whoever among his people shared that opinion. The reading with a fatha on the meem in the phrase You have no standing place, means: you have no place to stand, and it is the reading that I do not permit a reading other than it, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it. It was mentioned on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami that he read it as You have no standing place, with a damma on the meem, meaning: you have no place to stay. And His statement:
h
And a party of them ask permission of the Prophet
, saying, ‘
h
Our houses are exposed

,’ but they are not exposed. God Almighty says: And some of them ask permission of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to leave him and go to his home, but he wants to flee and escape from the army of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And a party of them ask permission of the Prophet… to his statement
, except to flee, he said: They are Banu Haritha, they said: Our houses are empty because we fear thieves.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Our houses are exposed
, he said: We fear theft from them.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And a party of them asked permission of the Prophet
, saying, ‘
h
Our houses are exposed

, but they are not exposed,’ and that they are close to the enemy, and we fear thieves in them. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, but he did not find an enemy in them. God said, They only wanted to flee, meaning that their saying,
h
Our houses are exposed
, was only to flee.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan Al-Qazzaz told us: Ubaidullah bin Hamran told us: Abd Al-Salam bin Shaddad Abu Talut told us on the authority of his father
m: regarding this verse:
h
Our houses are exposed
, but they are not exposed. He said: They are lost.

evidence.text: The reading with a fatha on the meem in the phrase You have no standing place, means: you have no place to stand, and it is the reading that I do not permit a reading other than it, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.
It was mentioned on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami that he read it as You have no standing place, with a damma on the meem, meaning: you have no place to stay.

x: And his saying, And if you entered upon them from its corners, he says: And if you entered the city upon these people who say, Our houses are exposed, from its corners, meaning: from its sides and regions, the singular of which is: qatr, and there is another language for it: qatr, and aqtar, and from it is the saying of the rajaz poet: If you want to apply oil or dates, then give them to the people who left the bad. His statement,
h
Then they were asked about the trial

, means: Then they were asked to return from faith to polytheism. They would have done it, means: They would have done it and returned from Islam and committed polytheism. His statement, And they did not remain in it except for a little while, means: They did not remain in it except for a little while from responding to polytheism, and they would have hastened to do that. And in a manner similar to what we said in what the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And if it were to enter upon them from its regions

meaning if it were to enter upon them from the outskirts of Medina and they were asked for the trial meaning polytheism they would give it meaning: they would give it, and they would not remain in it except for a little while meaning: except that they would give it willingly, what they would withhold.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement,
h
And if it were to enter upon them from its regions

, he said: If the city were to enter upon them from its outskirts, and then they were asked to disbelieve, they would have disbelieved. He said: And these hypocrites, if armies were to enter upon them, and those who want to fight them were asked to disbelieve, they would have disbelieved. He said: And the fitnah is disbelief, and it is what God says, Perversion is worse than killing (al-Baqarah 2:191), meaning disbelief. He says: Fear of them, and the evil of the persecution that they are in from hypocrisy, drives them to disbelieve in it. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement la-atuha. The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the reciters of Mecca read it as la-atuha with a shortened alif, meaning they came to her.

x: Some of the Meccans and the majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it as la-atuha with a long alif, meaning they would have given it, based on His statement:
h
Then they were asked about the trial
. They said: If it was a question, then it was a giving. The long reading is more pleasing to me for what I have mentioned, even though the other reading is permissible.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of His statement la-atuha.
The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the reciters of Mecca read it as la-atuha with a shortened alif, meaning they came to her.

Some of the Meccans and the majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it as la-atuha with a long alif, meaning they would have given it, based on His statement: Then they were asked about the trial.
The long reading is more pleasing to me for what I have mentioned, even though the other reading is permissible.

x: God Almighty says: And indeed, those who asked permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to leave him, and said, Our houses are exposed, had pledged to God before that, that they would not turn their backs to their enemy, for their saying was in the presence of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but they did not fulfill it after that. And the covenant of God will be questioned about. He says: So God asks that of whomever gave it to Him from himself. It was mentioned that this was revealed about Banu Haritha because of what they did at the Trench after what they did at Uhud.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: Yazid bin Ruman told me:
m: And they had already made a covenant with God not to turn their backs, and the covenant with God will be questioned about. They were Banu Haritha, and they were the ones who intended to fail on the day of Uhud with Banu Salamah when they intended to fail on the day of Uhud, then they made a covenant with God that they would not return to such a thing, so God mentioned to them those who had given Him of themselves.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And they had already made a covenant with God before that they would not turn their backs

, and the covenant with God will be questioned about. He said: There were people who were absent from the Battle of Badr, and they saw the honor and virtue that God had given the Companions of Badr, so they said: If God lets us witness a fight, we will fight. So God drove that to them until it was in the outskirts of Medina.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who ask your permission to leave you and say: Our homes are exposed, Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing. He says: Because that, or what God has decreed of them, will reach you in every situation, whether you hate it or like it. And then you will not enjoy it except for a little. He says: And if you flee from death or killing, your flight will not increase your lifespans and terms, rather you will only enjoy it in this world until the time that has been decreed for you, then what has been decreed for you and against you will come to you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: “Say: Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing. And then you will not enjoy [yourselves] except for a little.” Indeed, the whole world is little.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin, on the authority of Rabi’ ibn Khaitham:
m: And then you will not enjoy [yourselves] except for a little. He said: Except for their appointed terms.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Razin, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Khaitham,
m: similarly, except that he said: What is between them and their appointed times. Ibn Al-Muthanna narrated: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated: Shuʿbah narrated: Mansur narrated: Abu Razin said: Concerning this verse, So let them laugh a little and weep much (al-Tawbah 9:82), he said: Let them laugh a little in this world and weep much in the Fire. And he said concerning this verse, And then you will not enjoy [yourselves] except for a little, he said: Until their appointed times. One of these two hadiths traces it back to Rabiʿ ibn Khaitham. Ibn Wakee’ narrated: My father narrated to me, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Razin, on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khaitham: And then you will not enjoy yourself except for a little He said: The term. And his statement you will enjoy yourself is raised and not placed in the accusative case by permission of the waw that is with it. That is because if there is a waw before it, the meaning of if is to delay it after the verb, as if it was said: And if they fled, they would not enjoy themselves except for a little. And sometimes it is placed in the accusative case by it, even if there is a waw with it, because the verb is left out, so it is as if it is at the beginning of the sentence.

x: And His statement, Say, 'Who is it that can protect you from God if He intends to do you harm or intends to have mercy on you?' God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to those who ask your permission and say, Our houses are vulnerable, escaping from being killed: Who is it that can protect you from God if He intends to do you harm in yourselves, whether by killing or calamity or something else, or by well-being and safety? Is whatever harm or mercy befalls you in yourselves anything but from Him?

c: As Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: Yazid bin Ruman told me,
m: “Say: Who is it that can protect you from God if He intends to harm you or intends to have mercy on you?” That is, the matter is nothing but what I have decreed. And His statement,
h
And they will not find for themselves besides God any protector or helper

, God Almighty says: And these hypocrites will not find, if God intends evil for them in themselves and their wealth, besides God, any protector to take care of them sufficiently, nor any helper to aid them from God and repel from them what God intends for them of evil in that.

x: God Almighty says: God knows those among you who hinder people from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and turn them away from him and from witnessing the war with him, out of hypocrisy and to discourage Islam and its people. And those who say to their brothers, ‘Come to us,’ meaning, come to us and leave Muhammad alone, so that you do not witness his battle with him, for we fear for your own destruction by his destruction. And they do not come to battle except a little, meaning, they do not witness the war and fighting, if they witness it, except as an excuse and to defend themselves, the believers. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
God knows those among you who hold back and those who say to their brothers

, he said: These are people from the hypocrites who used to say to their brothers: Muhammad and his companions are nothing but a morsel of food, and if they were meat, Abu Sufyan and his companions would have devoured them. Leave this man alone, for he is doomed. His saying, And they do not come to battle except a little means that they do not witness the fighting, they are absent from it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman told us:
