m: God knows those among you who hold back: meaning the hypocrites and those who say to their brothers, “Come to us and do not come to battle except a little”: meaning only to repel and excuse.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
God knows those among you who hold back and those who say to their brothers… to the end of the verse

, he said: This is the Day of the Confederates. “A man returned from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and found his brother before him with roast meat, a loaf of bread, and wine. He said to him, ‘You are here with roast meat, a loaf of bread, and wine, while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is among spears and swords?’ He said, ‘Come to this, for you and your companion have reached the point of ruin. By the One by whom he swears, Muhammad will never encounter it.’ He said, ‘You have lied, by the One by whom he swears.’ He said, ‘And he was his brother from his father and mother. By God, I will inform the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of your affair.’ He said, and he went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to inform him. He said, ‘He found that Gabriel, peace be upon him, had come down with his report, “
h
God knows those among you who hold back and those who say to their brothers
, “Come to us,” and they do not come to battle except a little.’”

x: And His saying, stingy with you, the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning with which God described these hypocrites, in this instance of stinginess.
Some of them said: He described them as stingy with them regarding the spoils.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: They are stingy with you regarding the spoils.

x: Others said: Rather, he described them as being stingy with goodness.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told me, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, They are stingy with you, he said: with good, the hypocrites. Another one said: It means: They are stingy with spending on the weak believers among you. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that God described these hypocrites as cowardly and miserly, and He did not specify their description with one meaning or another. They are, as God described them, miserly with the believers in terms of spoils, goodness, and spending in the way of God, and with the poor Muslims. The accusative of His statement, miserly with you, is in the state of the noun mentioned in His statement, and they do not come to battle, as if it was said: They are cowards in battle, miserly when dividing the spoils, with the spoils. It may be possible that it is definitely from His statement, God knows those among you who hold back, so its interpretation would be: God knows those who hold people back from fighting and are miserly with the spoils when they conquer. It may also be definitely from His statement,
h
Come to us

, miserly, and they are miserly like that. And He, the Most High, described them with what He described them of miserliness towards the believers, because of the enmity and resentment in their souls towards them.

c: As Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: Yazid bin Ruman told me,
m: They are stingy with you, meaning with the grudge in their souls. And His statement,
h
So when fear comes

... to His statement, of death, the Most High says: So when the battle is present and the fighting comes, they fear destruction and being killed. You see them, O Muhammad, looking to you, seeking refuge with you, their eyes rolling, fearing death and fleeing from it. Like one who faints from death: He says: Like the rolling of the eyes of one who faints from the death that has befallen him. So when the fear has gone: He says: Then when the war is over and they are at peace,
h
they will smite you with sharp tongues
. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So when fear comes
, you will see them looking at you, their eyes rolling from fear.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid bin Ruman told me:
m: h
So when fear comes
, you will see them looking at you, their eyes rolling like one who has fainted from death: meaning, out of awe and fear of it. As for his saying,
h
They bit you with sharp tongues
, he is saying,
h
They bit you with sharp tongues

. And a man with a sharp tongue is called a sharp orator or a slashing orator or a slashing orator or a slashing orator. The commentators differed about the meaning of what God Almighty described of these hypocrites as boiling the believers in Him.

x: Some of them said: That is their boiling them when they take the spoils, by asking for a share for them.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And when the fear has gone, they will lash you with sharp tongues. As for when it comes to spoils, they are the most miserly people and the worst at sharing. Give us, give us, for we were present with you. As for when it comes to battle, they are the most cowardly and abandon the truth.

x: Others said: Rather, it is their inflicting harm upon them. This was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas.

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
They will smite you with sharp tongues
, he said: They will confront you.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: They slandered you with sharp tongues, he said: They spoke to you.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that they force them to say what you like, out of hypocrisy.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: Yazid ibn Ruman told me:
m: And when the fear has gone, they will lash out at you with sharp tongues, in saying whatever you like, because they do not hope for an afterlife, nor are they motivated by a reward, so they fear death with the fear of one who does not hope for what comes after it. The most similar of these statements to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the Qur’an is the statement of the one who said: They slapped you with sharp tongues, being miserly with good.

c: So He informed us that
m: their slapping the Muslims was due to their miserliness with regard to spoils and good. So it is known that if that was the case, it was to seek spoils. And if that was on their part to seek spoils, then that includes the statement of the one who said: The meaning of that is: They slapped you with harm, because their action was like that, and there is no doubt that it was harm to the believers. His statement, stingy with good, means: stingy with spoils, when the believers are victorious. His statement, they did not believe,
h
so God rendered their deeds worthless
, means the Almighty says: These people whose description I have described to you in these verses did not believe in God and His Messenger, but they are people of disbelief and hypocrisy,
h
so God rendered their deeds worthless
, meaning: God took away the rewards for their deeds and nullified them. He mentioned that the one who was described with this characteristic was a Badri, but God nullified his deeds.

x: Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
So God rendered their deeds worthless
h
and that was easy for God
, he said: My father told me that he was a Badri, and that His statement,
h
God rendered their deeds worthless
, means that God rendered worthless his deeds on the day of Badr. And His statement,
h
And that was easy for God
, means that God Almighty says: And the nullification of their deeds that they had done before their apostasy and hypocrisy was easy for God.

x: God Almighty says: These hypocrites think they are the parties, and they are Quraysh and Ghatafan.

c: As Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: Yazid bin Ruman told me,
m: They think that the parties have not gone away Quraish and Ghatafan. His saying, They did not go, means they did not turn away, even though they turned away out of fear and cowardice. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, They think that the confederates have not gone away, he said: They think that they are close. He mentioned that this is in Abdullah’s reading: They think that the confederates have gone, but when they find them not gone, they wish that they were still among the desert dwellers. And His statement,
h
And if the confederates come to you

, they would wish that they were nomads among the desert dwellers. God the Most High says: And if the believers come to the confederates - and they are the group, and the singular is party - wish means: they wish out of fear and cowardice that they were absent from you in the desert with the bedouins for fear of being killed. That is because His statement, If they were nomads among the bedouins you say: So-and-so has gone into the desert, so he is nomad, and he is a nomad. As for the bedouins, they are the plural of bedouin, and the singular of Arab is Arab. It is only said that a bedouin is for the people of the deserts, to differentiate between the people of the deserts and the cities, so he made the bedouins for the people of the desert, and the Arabs for the people of the cities. And His statement,
h
They ask about your report

, means: These hypocrites, O believers, ask people about your report, meaning about your report of the desert. Did Muhammad and his companions perish? He says: They wish to hear report of your perishing, that they would not witness your battles with you. And if they had been among you, they would not have fought except a little. God Almighty says to the believers: And if they had also been among you, they would not have benefited you, and they would not have fought the polytheists except a little. He says: Except as an excuse, because they do not fight them for the sake of God or hoping for reward. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
They ask about your report
, he said: Your report. And all the reciters of the regions, except for Asim Al-Jahdary, read
h
They ask about your report

, meaning they ask whoever came to them from the people about the report of your army and your report. And it was mentioned on the authority of Asim Al-Jahdary that he used to read that yas’alun with a shaddah on the seen, meaning they ask each other about that. The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is what the reciters of the regions say, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.

evidence.text: And all the reciters of the regions, except for Asim Al-Jahdary, read They ask about your report, meaning they ask whoever came to them from the people about the report of your army and your report.
And it was mentioned on the authority of Asim Al-Jahdary that he used to read that yas’alun with a shaddah on the seen, meaning they ask each other about that.
The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is what the reciters of the regions say, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.

x: The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement an example. The majority of the reciters of the regions read it as aswah with a kasrah on the alif, except for Asim bin Abi Lunjud, who read it with a damma as aswah. Yahya bin Waththab used to read this with a kasrah, and he would read His statement Indeed, in them you have a good example to follow (al-Mumtahanah 60:6) with a damma, and these are two dialects. It was mentioned that the kasrah is among the people of Hijaz, and the damma is among Qays, who say: aswah and akhwah. This is a rebuke from God to those who stayed behind from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his army in Madinah, from among the believers in him. God, the Most High, says to them: Indeed, in the Messenger of God you have a good example to follow, that you follow his example, and be with him wherever he is, and do not stay behind him.

For him whose hope is in God means: For he who hopes for God's reward and mercy in the hereafter does not desire himself, but rather he will have an example in being with him wherever he is. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman told me:
m: Then he turned to the believers and said: There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of God an excellent pattern for anyone whose hope is in God and the Last Day that they should not prefer themselves over himself, or over a place he is in. And remember God often that is: And remember God often in fear, hardship, and ease.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement an example.
The majority of the reciters of the regions read it as aswah with a kasrah on the alif, except for Asim bin Abi Lunjud, who read it with a damma as aswah.
Yahya bin Waththab used to read this with a kasrah, and he would read His statement Indeed, in them you have a good example to follow (al-Mumtahanah 60:6) with a damma, and these are two dialects.

x: And His statement,
h
And when the believers saw the parties

, means: And when the believers in God and His Messenger saw the groups of the unbelievers, they said, submitting to God’s command, and believing that this was the fulfillment of His promise to them, which He promised them in His statement, Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such [thing] has not yet come to you as came to those who passed on before you? ... until His statement,
h
Nearby Al-Baqarah (214 This is what God and His Messenger promised us

, and God and His Messenger spoke the truth, so God praised them for that from their certainty and their submission to His command, and He said: And the gathering of the parties against them only increased their faith in God and their submission to His judgment and command, and He granted them victory and triumph over the enemies. And what we said about that was said by the people of interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And when the believers saw the confederates… the verse

. He said: That is because God said to them in Surat Al-Baqarah, Or do you think that you will enter Paradise? (al-Baqarah 2:214)… until His statement, Indeed, the victory of God is near. (al-Baqarah 2:214). He said: So when the calamity befell them when they joined the confederates in the trench, the believers interpreted that, and it only increased their faith and submission.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: Yazid ibn Ruman told me:
m: Then he mentioned the believers and their truthfulness and their belief in what God promised them of trials with which He would test them: “They said, ‘This is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger spoke the truth. And it only increased them in faith and submission.’” That is, patience in the face of trials, submission to fate, and belief in the fulfillment of what God and His Messenger had promised them.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And when the believers saw the confederates

, they said, ‘This is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger spoke the truth.’ And God had promised them in Surat Al-Baqarah, when He said: “Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such [trial] has not yet come to you as came to those who passed on before you? They were afflicted with poverty and hardship and were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, ‘We are not worthy of worship.’” (al-Baqarah 2:214) By God, this is a severe trial and deficiency. When the companions of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) saw the hardship and trial that befell them, they said, ‘This is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger spoke the truth.’ And it only increased them in faith and submission, and in belief in what God had promised them and in submission to God’s decree.

x: God Almighty says, “Among the believers” in God and His Messenger, are men true to what they pledged to God meaning: they fulfilled what they pledged to Him of patience in times of hardship and distress, and in times of battle.
h
And among them is he who has fulfilled his vow

meaning: among them is he who finished the work that he vowed to God and made obligatory for himself, so he was martyred some on the day of Badr, some on the day of Uhud, and some in other situations. And among them is he who awaits his fulfillment and completion of it, just as those of them who have passed on fulfilled their pledge to God, and victory from God, and triumph over his enemy. And wailing is a vow in the speech of the Arabs.

i: And wailing also has other meanings in their speech, including death, as the poet said:
x: He died at the Hooper meeting place.

i: Meaning: his death and his soul, and from it the great danger, as Jarir said:
x: With a light fist, the kings fought us, and our horses, in the evening, were green on the ground.
That is, in great danger. And from it is wailing. It is said: We wailed in his path all day long: when he extended and did not stop all day and night.

i: And from it is wailing, which is danger, as the poet said:
x: If a dog wails on people, which of them is more deserving of the crown of glory?
And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yazid ibn Ruman told me:
m: Among the believers are men true to what they pledged to God meaning they fulfilled what they pledged to God.
h
And among them is he who has fulfilled his vow

meaning he finished his work and returned to his Lord, like the one who was martyred on the day of Badr and the day of Uhud. And among them is he who awaits what God has promised of victory and martyrdom for what his companions have done.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And among them is he who has fulfilled his vow
he said: his covenant and was killed or lived and among them is he who awaits a day in which there is jihad, so he will fulfill his vow and covenant and be killed or believed in the meeting thereof.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And among them is he who has fulfilled his vow

He said: His covenant And among them is he who awaits He said: A day in which there will be fighting, so he will be truthful in the encounter. He said: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mujahid, And among them were those who fulfilled their vow. He said: He died during the covenant. He said: Abu Usama told us, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Fulan he named him, but his name escaped me, on the authority of his father, And among them was he who fulfilled his vow. He said: His vow.

c: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Talha ibn Yahya, on the authority of his uncle Isa ibn Talha:
m: “A Bedouin came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him: ‘Who are those who have met their fate?’ He turned away from him. Then he asked him again, and he turned away from him. Talha entered through the door of the mosque wearing two green garments, and he said: ‘This is one of those who have met their fate.’”

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Hudha told us: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And among them is he who has fulfilled his vow
, he said: His death is while being truthful and faithful. And among them is he who awaits death in the same manner, and among them is he who has changed completely.

c: Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Masruq, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
And among them is he who has fulfilled his vow
, and among them is he who awaits. He said: The vow is the covenant.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: “Among the believers are men true to what they pledged to God. Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow” in truthfulness and loyalty and among them is he who awaits from himself truthfulness and loyalty.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And among them is he who has fulfilled his vow
, he said: He died in the state of belief and faith, and among them is he who awaits that.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Bakr told us: Sharik ibn Abdullah told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And among them is he who has fulfilled his vow

He said: Death is according to what he had pledged to God. And among them is he who awaits death according to what he had pledged to God. It was said: This verse was revealed about a people who did not witness Badr, so they made a covenant with God that they would fulfill their pledge to fight the polytheists with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Some of them fulfilled their pledge and met their fate, some of them changed their pledge, and some of them fulfilled their pledge but did not meet their fate, and they were waiting, based on the characteristics God described them with in this verse.

Who said that? Amr ibn Ali narrated: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated: Thabit narrated: Anas narrated: Anas ibn al-Nadr was absent from the Battle of Badr, and he said: I was absent from the first battle witnessed by the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). If I see fighting, God will see what I will do. Then, on the day of Uhud, when the people were defeated, he met Saʿd ibn Muʿadh and said: By God, I smell the fragrance of Paradise. So he advanced and fought until he was killed, and this verse was revealed concerning him: “Among the believers are men true to what they pledged to God. Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow [to the death], and among them is he who awaits [his chance].”

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abdullah bin Bakir told us: Humaid told us:
m: Anas bin Malik claimed that Anas bin An-Nadr was absent from the battle on the day of Badr, and he said: I was absent from the battle of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) against the polytheists. If God allows me to witness a battle, God will see what I will do. When the day of Uhud came, the Muslims fled, and he said: O God, I disavow before You what these polytheists have brought, and I apologize to You for what these people have done, meaning the Muslims. So he walked with his sword and met Saʿd bin Muʿadh, and he said: O Saʿd, I smell the fragrance of Paradise before Uhud. Saʿd said: O Messenger of God, I could not do what he did. Anas bin Malik said: We found him among the dead, with eighty-odd wounds on him, between sword blows, spear thrusts, and arrow wounds. We did not recognize him until his sister recognized him by his fingertips. Anas said: We used to say that this verse is: “Among the believers are men true to what they pledged to God.
h
And among them is he who has fulfilled his vow
.” It was revealed about him and his companions.

c: Suwar bin Abdullah told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us:
m: I heard Humayd narrating, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, that Anas bin Al-Nadr was absent from the Battle of Badr, and then he mentioned something similar. Abu Kurayb narrated: Yunus ibn Bakir narrated: Talhah ibn Yahya narrated: Musa and Isa ibn Talhah narrated: Talhah said: “A Bedouin came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). They did not dare to ask him a question, so they said to the Bedouin: ‘Ask him about one who has fulfilled his vow. Who is he?’ He asked him, but he turned away from him. Then he asked him again, but he turned away from him. Then I entered through the door of the mosque wearing green clothes. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw me, he said: ‘Where is the one who will ask about one who has fulfilled his vow?’ The Bedouin said: ‘I will, O Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘This is one of those who have fulfilled his vow.’”

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Abdul Hamid Al-Hammani told us, on the authority of Ishaq bin Yahya Al-Talhi, on the authority of Musa bin Talha, who said:
m: Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan stood up and said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Talha is among those who have fulfilled their vow.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Tamam al-Kalbi told me: Sulayman ibn Ayoub told us: My father told me: Ishaq told us: Yahya ibn Talhah told us: His uncle Musa ibn Talhah told us: His father Talhah told us:
m: “When we returned from Uhud and arrived in Madinah, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ascended the pulpit, addressed the people, consoled them, and informed them of the reward they would receive for it. Then he recited: ‘Men who have been true to what they pledged to God’… the verse. A man stood up and said: ‘O Messenger of God, who are these?’ He turned around, wearing two green garments, and said: ‘O questioner, this is one of them.’” And His saying,
h
And they did not change

: They did not change the covenant that they made with their Lord, as the obstructionists changed it, saying to their brothers: Come to us, and saying: Our houses are exposed. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And they did not Surat al-Ahzab 33:23 Among the believers are men true to what they promised God. Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow [to the death], and among them is he who awaits [his chance]. And they did not alter [the terms of their commitment] by any alteration. change at all, meaning: they did not doubt or hesitate about their religion, nor did they replace it with something else.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And they did not change
at all: They did not change their religion as the hypocrites did.

x: And His statement,
h
That God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness
, God Almighty says, Among the believers are men true to what they pledged to God. “
h
That God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness

” means: That God may strengthen the people of truthfulness through their truthfulness to God in what they pledged to Him, and their fulfillment of it. And He may punish the hypocrites if He wills, for their disbelief in God and their hypocrisy, or He may accept their repentance from their hypocrisy, and guide them to faith. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And He will punish the hypocrites
if He wills or forgive them. He said: If He wills, He will bring them out of hypocrisy and into faith.

x: What is the point of the condition in His statement,
h
And He will punish the hypocrites
, with His statement, if He wills, and the hypocrite is a disbeliever? Is it permissible for Him not to will the punishment of the hypocrite, so it is said, And He will punish him if He wills?
The meaning of that is not what you imagined. Rather, the meaning of that is:
h
And He will punish the hypocrites

by not granting them success in repenting from their hypocrisy until they die in their disbelief, if He wills, and thus they deserve the punishment. So the exception is from success, not from the punishment if they die in their hypocrisy. What we have said about this is explained by His statement,
h
Or He forgives them
. The meaning of the statement then is: He punishes the hypocrites because He does not guide them to repentance, so He surpasses them in it,
h
or He forgives them
and does not punish them.
His saying, Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, means that God conceals the sins of those who repent, and is merciful to those who repent, and does not punish them after their repentance.

God Almighty says, And God repelled those who disbelieved in Him and in His Messenger from among the Quraysh and Ghatafan in their fury meaning: in their distress and grief, for missing out on what they had hoped for of victory, and their disappointment in what they had hoped for of supremacy they did not attain any good meaning: they did not obtain any wealth or captivity from the Muslims and God sufficed the believers in fighting with soldiers of angels and the wind that He sent against them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
And God repelled those who disbelieved in their fury
, and they did not attain any good. Al-Ahzab.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And God repelled those who disbelieved in their fury

, they did not attain any good, and that was on the day of Abu Sufyan and the Confederates. God repelled Abu Sufyan and his companions in their fury, they did not attain any good. And God sufficed the believers in fighting, with the soldiers from Him and the wind that He sent against them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: Yazid bin Ruman told me,
m: h
And God repelled those who disbelieved in their fury
, and they did not attain any good: meaning Quraysh and Ghatafan.

c: Al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sada’i told me: Shababah told us: Ibn Abi Dhi’b told us, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Abi Sa’id al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa’id al-Khudri, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: We were prevented from praying on the day of the Trench, so we did not pray the noon prayer, nor the afternoon prayer, nor the sunset prayer, nor the evening prayer, until after the evening prayer, with the palms of our hands bent, and God revealed: And God sufficed the believers in fighting, and God is Powerful and Exalted in Might. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered Bilal to call the prayer, and he prayed the noon prayer, and he prayed it well, just as he used to pray it on time. Then he prayed the afternoon prayer in the same way, then he prayed the sunset prayer in the same way, then he prayed the evening prayer in the same way. He made the iqamah for each prayer, and that was before the fear prayer was revealed: But if you fear, then on foot or riding (al-Baqarah 2:239).

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Hakam told me: Ibn Abi Fadik told us: Ibn Abi Tha’lab told us, on the authority of al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa’id, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, who said:
m: We were detained on the day of the Trench, and he mentioned something similar. And His statement,
h
And God is All-Powerful
, All-Mighty, means:
h
And God is All-Powerful

to do whatever He wills to do with His creation, so He gives victory to whomever He wills among them over whomever He wills to abandon. No one can overcome Him. All-Mighty: meaning: He is severe in His vengeance against whoever He takes vengeance against from among His enemies.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And God is Powerful and Exalted in Might: Powerful in His command, Exalted in His punishment.

x: God Almighty says: And God sent down those who supported the confederates from Quraysh and Ghatafan against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, and that is their support for him, and he meant by that Banu Qurayzah, and they are those who supported the confederates against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. His statement, from the People of the Scripture, means: from the People of the Torah, and they were Jews. His statement, from their fortresses, means from their strongholds. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And He brought down those who supported them from among the People of the Scripture he said: Qurayza. He says: He brought them down from their fortresses.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And those who supported them from among the People of the Scripture - they are Banu Qurayzah

. They supported Abu Sufyan and corresponded, so they broke the covenant that was between them and the Prophet of God. He said: “While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was with Zaynab bint Jahsh washing his head, and she had washed his side, Gabriel, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him and said: May God pardon you. The angels have not laid down their weapons for forty nights. Go to Banu Qurayzah, for I have cut their strings, opened their doors, and left them in an earthquake and confusion. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took his leave, then he took the path of Banu Ghanm, and the people followed him, and he had bound his eyebrow with dirt. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them and besieged them and called out to them: O brothers of the monkeys. They said: O Abu al-Qasim, you were not obscene. So they submitted to the judgment of Ibn Muadh, and there was between them and His people shaved their heads, so they hoped that he would take them into consideration, and he or Lubaba signaled to them that it was slaughter, so God revealed:
h
O you who have believed, do not betray God and the Messenger or betray your trusts while you know [the consequence]

(al-Anfal 8:27), so he ruled that their fighters should be killed, their children should be taken captive, and that their property should go to the Muhajireen without the Ansar. His people and clan said: You have given preference to the Muhajireen over us in your property. He said: You were people with property, and the Muhajireen had no property. And it was mentioned to us that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) grew up and said: He ruled regarding you according to the judgment of God.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned back from the Trench and returned to Medina, and the Muslims laid down their weapons, when it was noon, Gabriel came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us,
m: on the authority of Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri - “Wrapped in a turban of brocade, riding a mule with a saddle on it, and over it was a velvet of brocade. He said: Have you laid down your weapons, O Messenger of God? He said: Yes. Gabriel said: The angels have not laid down their weapons yet. I have only just returned from pursuing the people. God commands you, O Muhammad, to march to Banu Qurayzah, and I am heading towards Banu Qurayzah. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered a crier to announce to the al-Nas 114:Whoever listens and obeys should not pray the afternoon prayer except in Banu Qurayzah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, with his banner to Banu Qurayzah, and the people rushed to it. Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, marched until he approached the fortresses, and he heard from them an ugly statement to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he returned until he met the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” On the way, he said: O Messenger of God, there is nothing wrong with you unless you come close to these wicked people. He said: Why? I think you heard them insulting me. He said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: If they had seen me, they would not have said anything like that. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came close to their fortresses, he said: O brothers of monkeys, has God disgraced you and brought down His vengeance upon you? They said: O Abu al-Qasim, I was not ignorant. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by his companions at the two mountains before he reached Banu Qurayzah, and he said: Did anyone pass by you? Surat al-Ahzab 33:26 And He caused those of the People of the Scripture who supported them to come down from their fortresses and cast terror into their hearts. Some you killed and some you took captive. They said: O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Dihya bin Khalifah Al-Kalbi passed by us on a white mule with a saddle on it and a brocade velvet saddle. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That was Gabriel sent to Banu Qurayzah to shake their fortresses and cast terror into their hearts. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, reached Qurayzah, he dismounted at one of their wells in a part of their property called Birana. The people followed him, and some men came to him after the last evening prayer, and they had not prayed the afternoon prayer because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had said: No one should pray the afternoon prayer except in Banu Qurayzah. So they prayed the afternoon prayer, and God did not criticize them for that in His Book, nor did His Messenger rebuke them for it. And the hadith on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Ma’bad bin Ka’b bin Malik Al-Ansari, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, besieged them for twenty-five nights until the siege was exhausting them and God cast terror into their hearts. Huyayy bin Akhtab had entered upon Banu Qurayzah in their fortress when the Quraysh and Ghatafan had withdrawn from them, in fulfillment of the covenant Ka’b bin Asad had made with him. When they were certain that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not leave them until he had fought them, Ka’b bin Asad said to them: ‘O group of Jews, what you see has befallen you, and I present to you three options, so take whichever one you choose.’ They said: ‘What are they?’ He said: ‘We will pledge allegiance to this man and believe him, for by God it has become clear to you that he is a prophet sent, and that he is the one you found in your book, so you will be safe regarding your blood, your wealth, your children, and your women.’ They said: ‘We will never depart from the rule of the Torah, nor will we replace it with anything else.’ He said: ‘If you refuse this to me, then come and let us kill our children.’” And our women, then we will go out to Muhammad and his companions, men with drawn swords, and we will not leave behind us anything that concerns us until God judges between us and Muhammad. If we perish, we will perish, and we will not leave behind us anything that we fear for, and if we are victorious, then by my life we will take the women and children. They said: We will kill these poor people, for what good is life after them? He said: If you refuse this to me, then tonight is the night of the Sabbath, and perhaps Muhammad and his companions have felt secure, so come down so that we may take Muhammad and his companions by surprise. They said: Shall we spoil our Sabbath and do on it what those before us did not do? As for those you know, they have been transformed in a way that is not hidden from you. He said: Not a single man among you has slept a single night in his life with determination since his mother gave birth to him. He said: Then they sent to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Send to us Abu Lubabah ibn Abd al-Mundhir, the brother of Banu Amr ibn Awf, who were among the caliphs of the Aws, so that we may consult him about our affair. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him. When they saw him, the men stood up to him, and the women and children cried out to him, crying in his face. He felt sorry for them and said to him: O Abu Lubabah, do you think we should submit to the judgment of Muhammad? He said: Yes, and he pointed with his hand to his throat, that is the slaughter. Abu Lubabah said: By God, my feet did not move until I knew that I had betrayed God and His Messenger. Then Abu Lubabah went on his way, and did not come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until he was tied to one of its pillars in the mosque and said: I will not leave my place until God accepts my repentance for what I have done, and I swear by God that I will never step on Banu Qurayzah again, and God will never see me in a land where I betrayed God and His Messenger again. When the report of him reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he had been slow to respond, he said: If he had come to me, I would have asked forgiveness for him. But since he did what he did, I am not the one who will release him from his place until God accepts his repentance. Then Thaʿlaba ibn Saʿiyah, Asid ibn Saʿiyah, and Asad ibn ʿUbayd, who were a group of Banu Hudhayl who were not from Banu Qurayzah or al-Nadir, their lineage was above that, they were the paternal cousins of the people, converted to Islam that night in which the Qurayzah submitted to the judgment of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. That night, Amr ibn Sa'di Al-Qurazi went out and passed by the guards of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who were led by Muhammad ibn Maslama Al-Ansari that night. When he saw him, he said, Who is this? He said, Amr ibn Sa'di. Amr had refused to join Banu Qurayzah in their treachery against the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he said, I will never betray Muhammad. When Muhammad ibn Maslama recognized him, he said, O God, do not deprive me of the ability to forgive the mistakes of the noble. Then he was released. He went out on his way until he spent the night in the mosque of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in Madinah. He then went away, and it is not known where he went from God’s earth to this day. His affair was mentioned to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he said, That was a man whom God saved through his loyalty.

x: Some people claimed that he was the most trustworthy of those among Banu Qurayzah when they submitted to the judgment of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), but his arrow lay scattered, and it is not known where he went. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said that statement, and God knows best. When morning came, they submitted to the judgment of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Aws jumped up and said: O Messenger of God, they are our clients, not the Khazraj. I did to the clients of the Khazraj yesterday what you know. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had besieged the Banu Qaynuqa’ before Banu Qurayzah, and they were allies of the Khazraj. They submitted to his judgment. Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul asked him for them, and he gave them to him. When the Aws spoke to him, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Are you not satisfied, O people of the Aws, that a man from among you should rule over them?

They said: Yes. He said: That is up to Saʿd ibn Muʿadh. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had placed Saʿd ibn Muʿadh in the tent of a woman from the tribe of Aslam called Rufaydah in his mosque. She used to treat the wounded and herself serve those Muslims who were poor. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had said to his people when he was struck by an arrow in the trench: Put him in Rufaydah’s tent until I return soon! When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had given him authority over Banu Qurayzah, his people came to him and carried him on a donkey, making him sit on a leather cushion. He was a large man. Then they came with him to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they were saying: O Abu ʿAmr, be kind to your clients, for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appointed you to that position because you were kind to them.

When they complained to him, he said: It is time for Saʿd not to be blamed for the sake of God. Some of his people who were with him returned to the home of Banu ʿAbd al-Ashhal, and the men of Banu Qurayzah informed them of the report of his death before he arrived. Saad bin Muadh came to them from his statement that he had heard from him. When Saad reached the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Muslims, he said: Rise and go to your master! So they rose and said: “O Abu Amr, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) has appointed your clients to you to judge among them.” Saad said: You have the covenant and pledge of God upon you, that you will judge among them as you have judged? He said: Yes. He said: “And upon those here in the area where the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is?” He turned away from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) out of respect for him.
The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Yes. Saad said: Then I rule among them that the men be killed, the wealth be divided, and the children and women be taken captive.
Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated:

c: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, on the authority of Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, on the authority of Abdur-Rahman ibn Amr ibn Saʿd ibn Muʿadh, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Waqqas al-Laythi, who said:
m: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I have judged them according to the judgment of God from above seven heavens, then they were brought down. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) imprisoned them in the house of the daughter of al-Harith, a woman from Banu al-Najjar. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out to the market place of Medina, which is its market today. He dug trenches there, then he sent for them and struck off their necks in those trenches, taking them out to him in groups. Among them were the enemies of God, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, and Kaʿb ibn Asad, the chief of the people. They were six or seven hundred, and most of them say that they were between eight and nine hundred. They said to Kaʿb ibn Asad as they were taking them to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in groups: O Kaʿb, what do you think about what will be done to us? Kaʿb said: Do you not understand in every situation? Do you not see that the caller does not desist, and that whoever among you takes him does not return? By God, it is death. This was the way of life until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished with them, and Huyayy ibn Akhtab, the enemy of God, was brought, wearing a robe of his that was like a pectoral, which he had torn on every side like the place of a fingertip, fingertip by fingertip, so that it would not be taken away, and his hands were bound around his neck with a rope. When he looked at the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: There is nothing wrong with the command of God, the Book of God and His decree, and a great battle that has been written for the Children of Israel. Then he sat down and his neck was struck off. Jabal ibn Jawal al-Tha’labi said: By God, Ibn Akhtab did not blame himself, but he who lets down God will be let down. I strive to find an excuse for myself, and every anxious person seeks honor. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr narrated: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr narrated: Aishah said: None of their women were killed except one woman. She said: By God, she was sitting with me, talking to me and laughing in the middle of the day, and the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was killing their men in the marketplace. Then a voice called out her name, Where is so-and-so? She said: By God, I am. I said: Woe to you, what is wrong with you? She said: Should I be killed? I said: Why? She said: Because of something I did. He said: “So she was taken away and her head was struck off. Aishah used to say: I will never forget my amazement at her good nature and her constant laughter, even though I knew that she would be killed.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: Yazid bin Ruman told me:
m: And He brought down those who supported them among the People of the Scripture from their fortresses. The fortresses are the fortresses and roofs in which they were.
h
And He cast terror into their hearts

c: Amr ibn Malik al-Bakri told us: Wakee’ ibn al-Jarrah told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: From their fortresses means: From their strongholds.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Rawqa’ told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, from their palaces, he said: He brought them down from their palaces, he said: their palaces. Surat al-Ahzab 33:26 And He caused those of the People of the Scripture who supported them to come down from their fortresses and cast terror into their hearts. Some you killed and some you took captive.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, from their fortresses: meaning from their castles and roofs.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And He brought down those who supported them from among the People of the Scripture from their strongholds

, he said: The strongholds are their fortresses which they thought would protect them from God, the Blessed and Exalted. The root of the word siyasi is the plural of saysa, and what is meant by it here is their fortresses. The Arabs say for the edge of a mountain: saysa, and the root of something is called saysa. It is said: May God reward the stronghold of so-and-so, meaning its root. And the thorns of the thorn are called sayasi, as the poet said: The location of the sciatic nerve in the stretched tissue They are the two forks of the rooster. And His statement,
h
And He cast terror into their hearts
, means: And He cast fear of you into their hearts.

x: A group you kill, means: You kill a group of them, and they are those from whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, killed when he defeated them. And a group you take captive, means: You take captive a group of them, and they are their women and children who were taken captive.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: A group you kill those whose necks were struck, and you take captive a group those who were taken captive.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: Yazid bin Ruman told me:
m: A group you kill and a group you take captive, meaning killing the men and taking the children and women captive.

x: And He made you inherit their land, their houses, and their wealth. He says: And He made you inherit their land after their destruction, meaning their farms, their plantations, and their houses. He says: And their dwellings and their wealth, meaning all the wealth other than the land and the houses. His statement, and a land you have not trodden, has been disputed among the commentators. Which land is this?
Some of them said, It is the Romans and the Persians, and they removed it from the lands that God later conquered for the Muslims.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And a land you have not trodden. He said: Al-Hasan said: It is the Romans and the Persians, and what God opened for them.

x: Others said: It is Mecca.
Others said: Rather, it is Khaybar.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: Yazid bin Ruman told me,
m: And a land which you have not trodden, he said: Khaybar. The correct thing to say about this is that God, the Most High, mentioned that He gave the believing Companions of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) an inheritance of the land of Banu Qurayzah, their homes and their wealth, and a land which they had not trodden on that day. There was neither Mecca nor Khaybar nor the lands of Persia and Rome nor Yemen among what they had trodden on that day, then they trod that later and God gave it to them as an inheritance. All of that is included in His statement, and a land which you have not trodden, because He, the Most High, did not specify some of that over others. And God has power over all things, the Most High says: And God had power to give the believers that inheritance, to grant them victory, and other matters. Nothing He wanted was impossible for Him, and nothing He tried to do was prevented from Him.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say, O Muhammad, to your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornments, then come, I will provide for you.” He says: I will provide for you what God has made obligatory for men for women, namely, provision when they separate from them through divorce, in His words:
h
And give them provision, the wealthy according to his means and the poor according to his means. A provision according to what is acceptable. This is due to those who do good.
(al-Baqarah 2:236). And His words:
h
And release you with gracious release.
He says: And release you for what God has permitted, and taught His servants with it, in His words:
h
When you divorce women, slap them during their waiting period.
And if you desire God and His Messenger. He says: And if you desire the pleasure of God and the pleasure of His Messenger and obedience to them, then obey them.

For indeed, God has prepared for the good-doers among you, meaning those among them who act according to the command of God and the command of His Messenger, a great reward. It was mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) because Aisha asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) something about worldly goods, either an increase in spending money or something else. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) kept away from his wives for a month, as it was mentioned. Then God commanded him to give them the choice between being patient with him, being content with what was allotted to them, and working in obedience to God, or between him enjoying their time and separating from them if they were not content with what was allotted to them. It was said that the reason for this was jealousy that Aisha was jealous of.
The narration was mentioned by someone who said: It was for some expenses and other things.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr,
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not go out for prayers. They said: What is the matter with him? Umar said: If you wish, I will tell you his matter. So he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and began to speak and raise his voice until he was given permission. He said: I began to say to myself, ‘What should I say to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he might laugh?’ Or a word to that effect. So I said: ‘O Messenger of God, if you saw so-and-so and asked me for maintenance, I would rebuke her.’ He said: ‘That is what kept me away from you.’ He said: So he went to Hafsah and said: ‘Do not ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for anything. Whatever you need, come to me.’ Then he followed the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and began to speak to them. He said to Aishah: ‘Does the fact that you are a beautiful woman and that your husband loves you deceive you? Either you stop, or the Qur’an will be revealed concerning you.’ Umm Salamah said: ‘O son of al-Khattab, is there nothing left for you except to intervene between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and His wives, and a woman will not ask except her husband? He said: And the Qur’an was revealed: “O Prophet, tell your wives, if you desire the life of this world and its adornment” ... to His saying: a great reward. He said: So he started with Aisha and gave her the choice and recited the Qur’an to her, and she said: Did you begin with any of your wives before me? He said: No. She said: Then I choose God and His Messenger, and the home of the Hereafter, and do not tell them about that. He said: Then he followed them and began to give them the choice and recite the Qur’an to them, and inform them of what Aisha had done, and they followed one another in that.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, “O Prophet, tell your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornments, then come, I will provide for you and release you with a gracious release” ... to His statement, a great reward. He said: Al-Hasan and Qatada said: He gave them the choice between this world and the Hereafter, Paradise and Hell, in regard to something they desired from this world. Ikrimah said about the jealousy that he committed against Aisha, and that he had nine wives at that time, five from Quraysh 106:Aisha, Hafsa, Umm Habiba bint Abi Sufyan, Sawda bint Zam’a, and Umm Salama bint Abi Umayya. He also had Safiyya bint Huyayy al-Khaibariyya, Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliya, Zainab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyya, and Juwayriyah bint al-Harith from Banu al-Mustaliq. He started with Aisha, and when she chose God, His Messenger, and the Hereafter, joy was seen on the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they all followed suit and chose God, His Messenger, and the Hereafter.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-A’la told us: Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: and this is the opinion of Qatada, regarding the statement of God, “O Prophet, tell your wives: If you should desire the life of this world and its adornment…” until His statement, great, they said: God commanded him to give them the choice between this world and the Hereafter, Paradise and Hell. Qatada said: This was out of jealousy of Aisha for something she wanted from this world, and he had nine wives: Aisha, Hafsa, Umm Habiba bint Abi Sufyan, Sawda bint Zam’a, Umm Salama bint Abi Umayya, Zainab bint Jahsh, Maymuna bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah, Juwayriyya bint al-Harith from Banu al-Mustaliq, and Safiyya bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab. So he started with Aisha, and she was the most beloved of them to him, and when she chose God, His Messenger, and the Hereafter, joy was seen on the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they followed suit in that.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: and this is the statement of Qatada, he said: When they chose God and His Messenger, God thanked them for that and said: It is not lawful for you to take other women after this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty should please you (al-Ahzab 33:52). So God limited it to them, and they are the nine who chose God and His Messenger.

x: Mention of those who said that out of jealousy:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God may God exalt his mention:
h
You may postpone whomever you wish of them, and you may take whomever you wish

(al-Ahzab 33:51)... the verse, he said: His wives had been jealous of the Prophet may God exalt his mention so he had abandoned them for a month. The choice was revealed from God to him concerning them:
h
O Prophet, tell your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornments
, and he recited until he reached:
h
And do not display yourselves like that of the times of the former ignorance

(al-Ahzab 33:33). So he gave them the choice between choosing that he set them free and divorce them, or that they stay if God and His Messenger wanted, on the condition that they were the mothers of the believers and would never be wedded, and that he would take to himself whomever he wished of them, for whoever he gave himself to until he would raise his head to her, and postpone whomever he wished until he would raise his head to her, and whoever desires of those with whom he has a wife, and withdraws, there is no blame upon him. That is more likely that their eyes will be comforted, and he will not grieve, and they will be satisfied if they know that it is from My judgment. They should prefer some of them over others, so that they will be more likely to be satisfied. He said: And whoever I seek from those whom I have isolated, I will get it, and whoever I have isolated will not get it. So he gave them the choice between being satisfied with this or leaving them, and they chose God and His Messenger, except for one Bedouin woman who left. And he was on that and he had stipulated this condition for him, and he continued to be just between them until he met God.

c: Ahmad ibn Abdah al-Dhabi narrated to us, saying: Abu Awana narrated to us, on the authority of Umar ibn Abi Salamah, on the authority of his father, who said: Aisha said:
m: When the choice was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: I want to mention a matter to you, so do not decide anything about it until you consult your parents. She said: “I said: ‘What is it, O Messenger of God?’ He said: ‘So he repeated it to her.’ She said: ‘What is it, O Messenger of God?’ He said: ‘So he recited to them: “O Prophet, tell your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornments…’” to the end of the verse. She said: “I said: ‘Rather, we choose God and His Messenger.’” She said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, rejoiced at that.”

x: Ibn Wakee' narrated: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Aishah, who said: When the verse of choice was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, began with Aishah and said: O Aishah, I am presenting a matter to you, so do not give a verdict about it until you have presented it to your parents, Abu Bakr and Umm Ruman. She said: O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what is it? He said: God said: O Prophet, tell your wives, if you should desire the life of this world and its adornment to something great, so I said: I desire God and His Messenger, and the home of the Hereafter, and I do not consult my parents, Abu Bakr and Umm Ruman, in that. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughed, then he asked the stone to read and said: Aishah said such and such.
They said: We say the same as Aishah said.

c: Saʿid ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to us: My father narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Bakr, on the authority of ʿUmrah, on the authority of ʿAishah,
m: that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went down to his wives, he was commanded to give them a choice. He came to me and said: I will mention something to you, but do not be hasty until you consult your father. I said: What is it, O Prophet of God? He said: I have been commanded to give you a choice, and he recited to her the verse of choice to the end of the two verses. She said: I said: What is it that you say, do not be hasty until you consult your father? For I choose God and His Messenger. He was pleased with that, and he presented it to his wives, and they all followed one another, and they chose God and His Messenger.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Musa bin Ali and Yunus bin Yazid told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said: Abu Salamah bin Abd al-Rahman told me,
m: “Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to give his wives a choice, he started by saying: ‘I am going to mention to you something, so do not hasten until you consult your parents.’ She said: ‘He knows that my parents would not have ordered me to divorce him.’ She said: ‘Then he recited this verse: “O Prophet, tell your wives: If you should desire the life of this world and its adornments, then come, I will provide for you and release you with gracious release.’” She said: I said: ‘For what purpose should I consult my parents? I desire God and His Messenger and the home of the Hereafter.’ Aisha said: ‘Then the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did as I did.’ So that was not the case when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said it to them, and they chose it as a divorce because they chose him.

evidence.text: She said: ‘Then he recited this verse: “O Prophet, tell your wives: If you should desire the life of this world and its adornments, then come, I will provide for you and release you with gracious release.’”

x: God Almighty says to the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality meaning: whoever of you commits a known act of adultery for which God has made the prescribed punishment, her punishment for her immorality in the Hereafter will be doubled for the immorality of other people’s wives, as:

c: Muhammad bin Sa’ told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: The punishment will be doubled for her. He said: He means the punishment of the Hereafter. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of reciters in the regions recited it as yuddaf’a laha al-‘adhab with an alif, except for Abu ‘Amr, who recited it as yuddaf’a with a shaddah on the ‘ayn, interpreting it in his recitation as meaning to double something once, that is, to make something into two. So, according to him, the meaning of the statement is to make the punishment of whoever among the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commits a clear indecency in this world and the hereafter double the punishment of all other women besides them. He says that yuddaf’a means to make a thing twice as big as three, so according to him, the meaning of those who recited yuddaf’a was that her punishment is like that of other women besides the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). That is why he chose yuddaf’a over yuddaf’a. The others who recited it as yuddaf’ denied what he said about that, and they said: We do not know of any difference between yuddaf’a and yuddaf’a. The correct reading in this regard is that of the reciters of the regions, which is yudji’ab doubles. As for the interpretation adopted by Abu ‘Amr, it is an interpretation that we do not know of any scholar who claimed other than him and Abu ‘Ubaydah Mu’ammar ibn al-Muthanna. It is not permissible to go against what has been unanimously agreed upon by the evidence, with an interpretation for which there is no proof from the perspective that must be accepted. And His statement,
h
And that was easy for God
, means that the Almighty says: And the doubling of the punishment for those of them who did that was easy for God, and God knows best.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of this.

The majority of reciters in the regions recited it as yuddaf’a laha al-‘adhab with an alif, except for Abu ‘Amr, who recited it as yuddaf’a with a shaddah on the ‘ayn, interpreting it in his recitation as meaning to double something once, that is, to make something into two.
The others who recited it as yuddaf’ denied what he said about that, and they said: We do not know of any difference between yuddaf’a and yuddaf’a.
The correct reading in this regard is that of the reciters of the regions, which is yudji’ab doubles.

x: God Almighty says: And whoever among you obeys God and His Messenger and does what God has commanded, We will give her her reward twice over meaning: God will give her the reward for her work, twice the reward of the work of other women among mankind. And We have prepared for her a noble provision meaning: And We have prepared for her in the Hereafter a pleasant life in Paradise. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And whoever among you is obedient to God and His Messenger… the verse
, meaning: obeys God and His Messenger. And does righteousness fasts and prays.

c: Salim bin Junada told me: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, who said:
m: I asked Aamer about Qunut. He said: What is it? I said: And stand before God, devoutly obedient (al-Baqarah 2:238). He said: Obedient. I said: And whoever among you is devoutly obedient to God and His Messenger He said: He stabs.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And whoever among you is obedient to God and His Messenger meaning whoever among you obeys God and His Messenger and We have prepared for her a noble provision meaning Paradise. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, and do righteousness. The majority of reciters in Hijaz and Basra read, and do righteousness, with a ta’ in response to the interpretation of from since it came after His statement, from you.

x: Some of them narrated from the Arabs that they would say, How many slave girls were sold to you? and that if they put the slave girl first, they would say, How many slave girls were sold to you? So they feminized the verb after the slave girl. The verb in both versions is for you, not for the slave girl.

i: Al-Farra’ mentioned that some Arabs recited:
x: Oh, Umm Amr, whose home is the atmosphere of Adi, he eats insects His forehead turns black from the scorching heat of the poison, and he becomes naked if he has young children.

He said: And if they were, and he did not say: And if it was, and this is for those who use it in a specific meaning. As for the people of Kufa, the majority of their reciters read it as and he works with a ya’ in apposition to yuqannat, since everyone read it with a ya’. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings and two well-known dialects in the speech of the Arabs, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. This is because the Arabs sometimes use the predicate of man in its pronunciation, so it is singular and mentioned, and sometimes in its meaning, as God Almighty said:
And among them are those who listen to you, so can you make the deaf hear, even though they do not understand? And among them are those who look at you
So He used it in the plural once for the meaning, and used it singular another time for the pronunciation.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, and do righteousness.
The majority of reciters in Hijaz and Basra read, and do righteousness, with a ta’ in response to the interpretation of from since it came after His statement, from you.
As for the people of Kufa, the majority of their reciters read it as and he works with a ya’ in apposition to yuqannat, since everyone read it with a ya’.

x: God Almighty says to the wives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace:
h
O wives of the Prophet
, you are not like any other women of the women of this nation if you fear God and obey Him in what He commands you and what He forbids you.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
O wives of the Prophet
, you are not like any other women, meaning the women of this nation. His saying,
h
Do not speak softly
, means:
h
Do not speak softly
to men in order to please those who commit immorality among you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, “
h
O wives of the Prophet
, you are not like anyone among women. If you fear God, then do not be too soft in speech,” meaning: Do not be soft in speech, and do not be too soft in speech.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
So do not speak in a soft voice
, he said: A soft voice is what is disliked for women to say to men, which enters men’s hearts. His statement,
h
So he in whose heart is disease will covet

, means: So he in whose heart is weakness will covet, and because of the weakness of his faith in his heart, he is either doubtful about Islam and a hypocrite, and because of this he takes God’s limits lightly, or he is lax about committing indecencies. The commentators differed in their interpretation of this.

x: Some of them said that he described him as having a disease in his heart because he was a hypocrite.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: Then he in whose heart is disease will be tempted, he said: Hypocrisy.

x: Others said: Rather, he described it that way because they desire to commit indecencies.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: Then he in whose heart is disease will covet. He said: Ikrimah said: The desire for adultery. And His saying,
h
And speak a suitable word
, means: And speak a word that God has permitted and made permissible for you.

c: As Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement,
h
And speak a good word
, he said: A beautiful, good, and well-known word in goodness.

x: The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement,
h
And abide in your homes
. The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the Kufians read it as, Wa qarna with a fatha on the qaf, meaning:
h
And abide in your homes

. It seems that the one who read it that way deleted the first ra' from iqran, which is fatha, then moved it to the qaf, as it was said, Fazaltum tafkahun (The Sovereignty: 65), meaning Fazaltum You remained amused, so the first lam was dropped, which was kasra, then its kasra was moved to the dhaal. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it as, Wa qarna with a kasra on the qaf, meaning: Be people of dignity and tranquility in your homes. This reading, which is the kasra on the qaf, is more correct in our view, because if it is from dignity, as we have chosen, then there is no doubt that the reading with the kasra on the qaf is better, because it is said that someone was dignified in his home, so he is dignified dignified, so the qaf is kasra in tafaʿala, and if it is a command from it, it is said qar, just as it is said from the weight of yazan, zan, and from waʿad and ʿiʿud, ʿad.

If it is from qarār, then it is more correct to say iqarna, because whoever among the Arabs said: ،وناَنسن بَناَن،َنلنٌة،وناَنسن بَناَن،َنْعَنَن للَناَنٌَنلنomitting the ʿayn of the verb and transferring its vowel to its faʿ in faʿl, faʿlna, and faʿltum, did not do that in the imperative and prohibitive, so he does not say:ونَن َنلنٌة َناًءا،َناًءاٌَنلن. So the one who has been argumentative for the correctness of the reading with the fatha on the qaf in that is not saying the Arabs inواََنتٌَنلنلتت واََنت َنلنwith a reason that necessitates its correctness for what I have described of the reason.

Some of them have narrated from some of the Bedouins that he heard it: ،الجِهَيََن تى مmeaning:يََن تى. If it is correct, then it is closer to being an argument for the proponents of this reading than the other argument. His saying,
h
And do not display yourselves like that of the times of ignorance
. It was said that display in this context means strutting and swaggering.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And do not display yourselves like that of the times of the former ignorance
