: meaning, when you go out of your homes, he said: They had a gait, a graceful and flirtatious manner, meaning the times of the former ignorance, so God forbade them from that.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said:
m: I heard Ibn Abi Nujayh say regarding His statement,
h
And do not display yourselves like that of the times of the former ignorance

, he said: Strutting. It was said that displaying one’s adornment is the display of one’s beauty, and a woman showing off her charms to men. As for his saying, The unveiling of the first pre-Islamic era, the people of interpretation differed regarding the lack of ignorance in the first era.

x: Some of them said: That was what happened between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon him.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Aamer:
m: h
And do not display yourselves like that of the times of the first ignorance
. He said: The first ignorance was between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them.

x: Others said: That was between Adam and Noah.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Hakam:
m: h
And do not display yourselves like that of the times of the first ignorance

. He said: There were eight hundred years between Adam and Noah, and their women were the ugliest of women, and their men were beautiful. So the woman would seek the man for herself, so this verse was revealed:
h
And do not display yourselves like that of the times of the first ignorance

x: Others said: Rather, it was between Noah and Idris.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Zuhair told me: Musa ibn Ismail told us: Dawud told us,
m: meaning Ibn Abi al-Furat, who said: Alba’ ibn Ahmar told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: He recited this verse:
h
And do not display yourselves like that of the times of the former ignorance

. He said: It was between Noah and Idris, and it was a thousand years, and there were two clans of the children of Adam, one of them lived in the plain and the other lived in the mountain. The men of the mountain were bright-eyed, but the women were ugly, and the women of the plain were bright-eyed, but the men were ugly. And Satan came to a man from the Surat al-Ahzab 33:33 And abide in your houses and do not display yourselves like that of the times of former ignorance. And establish prayer and give zakah and obey God and His Messenger. God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification. plain in the form of a boy, and hired himself out to him, and he served him. Satan took something like the one in which the shepherds play the flute, and he came in it with a voice the like of which had never been heard. This reached those around them, and they came to listen to him, and they took a festival to which they would gather throughout the year, and the men would display theirselves like that of the times of the former ignorance.

c: So he came to his companions and informed them
m: of this, so they turned to them and camped with them, and indecency became apparent among them. This is the saying of God:
h
And do not display yourselves like that of the times of the former ignorance

. The most correct of the sayings on this matter, in my opinion, is to say: God Almighty forbade the wives of the Prophet from displaying their beauty in the manner of the first era of ignorance, and it is possible that this was between Adam and Jesus, so the meaning of that would be: Do not display your beauty in the manner of the first era of ignorance that preceded Islam.
b.via: So he came to his companions and

x: Is there ignorance in Islam, such that it could be said that by his saying the first ignorance he meant the one before Islam?
It contains characteristics of ignorance.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And do not display yourselves like that of the times of the first ignorance

, he said: He means that which existed before Islam. He said: And in Islam was there ignorance? He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Darda’, and he said to a man while he was disputing with him: O son of so-and-so, because he used to taunt him about it in the ignorance. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abu Darda’, there is ignorance in you. He said: Ignorance of disbelief or Islam? He said: Rather, ignorance of disbelief. He said: I wished that I had begun my conversion to Islam on that day. He said: And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Three are the deeds of the people of ignorance that people should not abandon: insulting lineage, seeking rain from the stars, and wailing.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, he said: Sulayman ibn Bilal told me, on the authority of Thawr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas, that Umar ibn al-Khattab said to him: Tell me about the statement of God to the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace:
h
And do not display yourselves like that of the times of ignorance

- was there only one? Ibn Abbas said: Was it among the first but had an end? Umar said: May God reward you, Ibn Abbas, how did you say it? He said: O Commander of the Faithful, was it among the first but had an end? He said: Then bring proof of what you say from the Book of God. He said: Ya-Sin 36:And strive in God’s cause with the striving due to Him Al-Hajj 22:78 as you strived the first time. Umar said: Who ordered jihad? He said: Two tribes of Quraysh 106:Makhzum and Banu Abd Shams. Umar said: You have spoken the truth. It is possible that this was between Adam and Noah, and it is possible that it was between Idris and Noah, so the last period of ignorance would be between Jesus and Muhammad. If this is something that is permitted by the apparent meaning of the verse, then it is correct to say about it, as God said: He forbade the unveiling of the days of ignorance. And His statement,
h
And establish prayer and give zakat
, means: And establish the obligatory prayer, and give the zakat that is obligatory upon you from your wealth. And obey God and His Messenger, in what they command you and forbid you.
h
God only desires to remove from you the impurity

, O people of the House, means: God only desires to remove from you evil and immorality, O people of the House of Muhammad, and to purify you from the filth that is in those who disobey God, a thorough purification. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
God only desires to remove from you the impurity
, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification, they are the people of a House whom God purified from evil and singled out for mercy from Him.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
God only desires to remove from you the impurity
, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification, he said: The impurity here is the devil, and other impurity is polytheism.

x: The interpreters differed regarding those meant by his saying the people of the house.
Some of them said: He meant the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Ali, Fatima, Hassan, and Hussein, may God be pleased with them.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me: Bakr ibn Yahya ibn Zaban al-Anzi told us: Mandal told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Atiyyah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “This verse was revealed about five: me, Ali may God be pleased with him, Hasan may God be pleased with him, Husayn may God be pleased with him, and Fatimah may God be pleased with her: ‘
h
God only desires to remove from you the impurity
, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.’”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Muhammad ibn Bishr told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Mus’ab ibn Shaiba, on the authority of Safiyya bint Shaiba, who said: Aisha said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out one morning wearing a black hair cloak. Then al-Hasan came and brought him in with him. Then he said: ‘
h
God only desires to remove from you the impurity
, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.’”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Anas,
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would pass by Fatimah’s house for six months, and whenever he went out to pray, he would say: ‘Prayer, O people of the House!
h
God only desires to remove from you the impurity
, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.’”

c: Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me: Yahya bin Ibrahim bin Suwaid Al-Nakha’i told us, on the authority of Hilal,
m: meaning Ibn Muqlas, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was with me, along with Ali, Fatimah, Al-Hasan, and Al-Husayn. I made a cloak for them, so they ate and slept, and he covered them with a cloak or a velvet blanket, then he said: ‘O God, these are my family. Remove impurity from them and purify them thoroughly.’”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Na’im told us: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq told us: Abu Dawud told me, on the authority of Abu al-Hamra’, who said:
m: I stayed in Medina for seven months during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: “I saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when dawn came, come to the door of Ali and Fatima and say: ‘Prayer, prayer. God only desires to remove from you the uncleanness, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.’”

c: Abdul-A’la bin Wasil told me, he said: Al-Fadl bin Dukayn told us, he said: Yunus bin Abi Ishaq told us,
m: with his chain of transmission on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the same.

c: Abdul A’la bin Wasil told me: Al-Fadl bin Dukayn told us: Abdul Salam bin Harb told us, on the authority of Kulthum Al-Maharbi, on the authority of Abu Ammar, who said:
m: “I was sitting with Wathilah bin Al-Asqa’ when they mentioned Ali, may God be pleased with him, and they cursed him. When they got up, he said: Sit down so I can tell you about the one they cursed. I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when Ali, Fatimah, Hasan, and Husayn came to him. He threw his cloak over them and then said: O God, these are my family. O God, remove impurity from them and purify them thoroughly. I said: O Messenger of God, and what about me? He said: And you? He said: By God, this is the most trustworthy of my deeds to me.”

c: Abdul Karim bin Abi Umair told me: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us: Abu Amr told us: Shaddad Abu Ammar told us:
m: I heard Wathilah bin Al-Asqa’ narrating: “I asked about Ali bin Abi Talib in his house, and Fatimah said: He has gone to bring the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), when he came, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered and I entered, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sat on the bed and made Fatimah sit on his right, and Ali on his left and Hasan and Husayn in front of him, and he wrapped his garment over them and said: ‘God only desires to remove from you the uncleanness, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.’ O God, these are my family, O God, my family is more deserving. Wathilah said: So I said from the side of the house: ‘And I, O Messenger of God, am I among your family?’ He said: ‘And you are among my family.’ Wathilah said: ‘She is among what I hope for most.’”

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to me, he said:
m: Thanawkiʿ, on the authority of ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Fadil ibn Marzuq, on the authority of ʿAtiyyah, on the authority of Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, on the authority of Umm Salamah, she said: “When this verse was revealed: ‘God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification,’ the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called for ʿAli, Fatimah, Hasan, and Husayn, and covered them with a Khaybari cloak and said: ‘O God, these are my family. O God, keep away uncleanness from them and purify them with a thorough purification.’ Umm Salamah said: ‘Are you not one of them?’ He said: ‘You are on the right path.’”

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Musʿab ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, saying: Saʿid ibn Zurbi narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said:
m: “Fatimah came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a pot of hers in which she had made porridge and placed it on a plate. She placed it in front of him, and he said: ‘Where is your cousin and your two sons?’ She said: ‘In the house.’ He said: ‘Call them.’ So she came to Ali and said: ‘You and your two sons, answer the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.’ Umm Salamah said: When he saw them approaching, he reached for a cloak that was on the bed, stretched it out, and made them sit on it. Then he took hold of the four corners of the cloak with his left hand, and brought it over their heads. He gestured with his right hand to his Lord, and said: ‘These are the people of the House, so remove impurity from them and purify them with a thorough purification.’” Abu Kurayb narrated: Hasan ibn Atiyyah narrated: Fadil ibn Marzuq narrated: Atiyyah narrated: Abu Saeed narrated: Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), said: “This verse was revealed in her house: ‘God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.’” She said: “I was sitting at the door of the house, so I said: ‘O Messenger of God, am I not one of the people of the House?’ He said: ‘You are indeed on the right path; you are one of the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him).’ She said: Surat al-Ahzab 33:33 And abide in your houses and do not display yourselves like that of the times of former ignorance. And establish prayer and give zakah and obey God and His Messenger. God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification. ‘And in the house were the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn may God be pleased with them.”

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Khalid bin Mukhallad narrated to us, saying: Musa bin Ya’qub narrated to us, saying: Hashim bin Hashim bin Utbah bin Abi Waqqas narrated to me, on the authority of Abdullah bin Wahb bin Zam’ah, who said:
m: “Umm Salamah informed me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gathered Ali and the two Hassans, then brought them under his garment, then he cried out to God, then he said: These are my family, so Umm Salamah said: O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, bring me in with them, he said: You are from my family.”

c: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi told me: Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih told us: Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Asbahani told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Ubayd al-Makki, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Umar ibn Abi Salamah, who said:
m: This verse was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in the house of Umm Salamah:
h
God only desires to remove from you the impurity

, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification. So he called Hasan, Husayn, and Fatimah and seated them in front of him. He called Ali and seated him behind him. He and they covered themselves with the cloak and then said: These are my family, so remove from them impurity and purify them with a thorough purification. Umm Salamah said: I am with them in your place and you are in good health.

c: Muhammad ibn Amara told me: Ismail ibn Abaan told us: Al-Sabah ibn Yahya Al-Mari told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Al-Daylam, who said:
m: Ali ibn Lahusayn said to a man from the people of Ash-Sham: Have you not read in al-Ahzab 33:God only desires to remove from you the uncleanness, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification. He said: And you are them? He said: Yes.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Bakr Al-Hanafi told us: Bakir bin Mismar told us:
m: I heard Amer bin Saad say: Saad said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when the revelation came down to him, he took Ali, his two sons, and Fatima, and brought them under his garment, then he said: ‘Lord, these are my family and my household.’” Ibn Humayd narrated: Abdullah ibn Abd al-Quddus narrated to us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Hakim ibn Sa’d, who said: We mentioned Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him to Umm Salamah. She said: The verse ‘God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the Household, and to purify you with a thorough purification’ was revealed about him. Umm Salamah said: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to my house and said: ‘Do not allow anyone in.’ Then Fatimah came, and I could not prevent her from entering upon her father. Then al-Hasan came, and I could not prevent him from entering upon his grandfather and mother. Then al-Husayn came, and I could not prevent him from entering upon his grandfather and mother. So al-Husayn came, and I could not prevent him. So they gathered around the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on a carpet. The Prophet of God covered them with a cloak he was wearing, then he said: ‘These are my family, so keep away uncleanness from them and purify them with a thorough purification.’ So this verse was revealed when they gathered on the carpet.” She said: “I said: ‘O Messenger of God, what about me?’ She said: ‘By God, I am not at ease.’ He said: ‘You are indeed heading for good.’”

x: Others said: Rather, he meant the wives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Asbagh told us, on the authority of Alqamah, who said:
m: Ikrimah used to call out in the market:
h
God only desires to remove from you the impurity
, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification. He said: It was revealed specifically about the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, And abide in your homes.
The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the Kufians read it as, Wa qarna with a fatha on the qaf, meaning: And abide in your homes.

It seems that the one who read it that way deleted the first ra' from iqran, which is fatha, then moved it to the qaf, as it was said, Fazaltum tafkahun (The Sovereignty: 65), meaning Fazaltum You remained amused, so the first lam was dropped, which was kasra, then its kasra was moved to the dhaal.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it as, Wa qarna with a kasra on the qaf, meaning: Be people of dignity and tranquility in your homes.

This reading, which is the kasra on the qaf, is more correct in our view, because if it is from dignity, as we have chosen, then there is no doubt that the reading with the kasra on the qaf is better, because it is said that someone was dignified in his home, so he is dignified dignified, so the qaf is kasra in tafaʿala, and if it is a command from it, it is said qar, just as it is said from the weight of yazan, zan, and from waʿad and ʿiʿud, ʿad.

So the one who has been argumentative for the correctness of the reading with the fatha on the qaf in that is not saying the Arabs inواََنتٌَنلنلتت واََنت َنلنwith a reason that necessitates its correctness for what I have described of the reason.
If it is correct, then it is closer to being an argument for the proponents of this reading than the other argument.

Ibn Zuhair told me: Musa ibn Ismail told us: Dawud told us, meaning Ibn Abi al-Furat, who said: Alba’ ibn Ahmar told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: He recited this verse: And do not display yourselves like that of the times of the former ignorance.

x: God Almighty says to the wives of His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And remember the blessing of God upon you, by placing you in houses in which the verses of God and wisdom are recited, so thank God for that and praise Him for it. What He means by His statement,
h
And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God

is: And remember what is read in your houses of the verses of the Book of God and wisdom. What He means by wisdom is: what was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the rulings of God’s religion, and which was not revealed in the Qur’an, and that is the Sunnah. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God and wisdom

, meaning the Sunnah, he said: He bestows upon them that favor. And His saying, Indeed, God is Kind and All-Knowing, God Almighty says: Indeed, God was kind to you, as He placed you in the houses in which His verses and wisdom are recited, and All-Knowing of you when He chose you as wives for His Messenger.

evidence.text: What He means by His statement, And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God is: And remember what is read in your houses of the verses of the Book of God and wisdom.

Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God and wisdom, meaning the Sunnah, he said: He bestows upon them that favor.

x: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who are humble before God in obedience, men and women, and those who believe in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he brought them from God,
h
and the obedient men and women
h
and the obedient men and women

to God in what he commanded them and forbade them, and the truthful men and women in what they pledged to God, and the truthful women in that, and the patient men and women who are patient before God in poverty and hardship, steadfast in His religion, and during battle, and the patient men and women, and the humble ones whose hearts are humble before God, fearing Him and His punishment, and the humble ones, and the charitable men and women who fulfill the rights of God from their wealth, and the fasting men and women, and the fasting men and women who guard their private parts except from their wives or those their right hands possess, and the women who guard that except from their husbands if they are free, or from their property if they are slaves, and the men who remember God with their hearts, tongues, and limbs, and the women who remember—thus has God prepared for them forgiveness for their sins.
h
And a great reward
: meaning a great reward in the Hereafter for their deeds, which is Paradise. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: Some women entered upon the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: God has mentioned you in the Qur’an, but we have not been mentioned at all. Is there nothing in us that should be mentioned? Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the obedient men and obedient women - meaning the obedient men and obedient women, and the humble men and humble women - meaning the fearful men and fearful women - God has prepared for them forgiveness for their sins
h
and a great reward
in Paradise.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And a great reward
, he said: Paradise. And regarding His statement,
h
And the obedient men and women
, he said: The obedient men and women.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Jarir told us, he said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Amer, he said:
m: The obedient ones are the obedient ones.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Muammil told us, he said:
m: Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: “Umm Salamah said: O Messenger of God, men are mentioned but we are not, so ‘Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women’ was revealed.”

c: Abu Kurayb told us, she said: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, that Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Hattab told him, on the authority of Umm Salamah, she said:
m: “I said: O Messenger of God, are men mentioned in everything, and we are not? So God revealed, ‘Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women’... the verse.”

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Sayyar bin Muzahir Al-Anzi told us: Abu Kudayna Yahya bin Muhallab told us, on the authority of Qabus bin Abi Dhibyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant Surat al-Ahzab 33:35 Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the obedient men and obedient women, the truthful men and truthful women, the patient men and patient women, the humble men and humble women, the charitable men and charitable women, the fasting men and fasting women, the men who guard their private parts and the women who guard them, and those who remember God And for those who remember God, God has prepared forgiveness
h
and a great reward
. him peace, said: Why does he mention the believing men and not the believing women? Then God revealed: Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women... the verse.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, he said: Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Why are women not mentioned with men in righteousness? Then God revealed this verse.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Mu'ammar told me: Abu Hisham told us: Abd al-Wahid told us: Uthman ibn Hakim told us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Shaibah told us:
m: I heard Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “I said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘O Messenger of God, why are we not mentioned in the Qur’an as men are? ’ She said: ‘One afternoon, nothing startled me except his call from the pulpit while I was combing my hair. So I wrapped my hair and went out to one of their rooms, and I listened by the palm frond. Then he said from the pulpit: O people, God says in His Book: “Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women...” until His saying:
h
God has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward

x: God Almighty says: It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a decision concerning themselves, that they should choose any other decision for themselves other than that which they have decided, nor should they disobey the command of God and the command of His Messenger and their decision, and disobey them. And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger in what they have commanded or forbidden, has certainly strayed into clear error. That is, he has deviated from the straight path and taken a path other than that of guidance and right conduct. It was mentioned that this verse was revealed about Zainab bint Jahsh when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, proposed to her for his servant Zaid bin Haritha, but she refused to marry him.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman

, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter ... to the end of the verse, that “the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to propose marriage to his young servant Zayd ibn Haritha, and entered upon Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah and proposed marriage to her, but she said, ‘I will not marry him.’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Then marry him.’ She said, ‘O Messenger of God, am I being guided by my own desires?’ While they were talking, God revealed this verse to His Messenger, “
h
And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman

” ... to His statement, clear error. She said, ‘O Messenger of God, have you chosen him as my wife?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ She said, ‘Then I will not disobey the Messenger of God, I have married myself to him.’”

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, that they should have the choice in their affair, he said: Zaynab bint Jahsh and her dislike of marrying Zayd ibn Haritha when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered her to do so.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman

, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any option in their decision. He said: “This verse was revealed about Zaynab bint Jahsh, who was the cousin of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, proposed to her, and she accepted. She thought that he was proposing to her for himself, but when she learned that he was proposing to her for Zayd ibn Haritha, she refused and denied it. So God revealed, “And it is not for a believing man or a Surat al-Ahzab 33:36
h
And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman

, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any option in their decision. And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error. believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any option in their decision.” He said: I followed him after that and was satisfied.

c: Abu Ubaid Al-Wasafi told me: Muhammad bin Hamir told us: Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Umrah, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, proposed marriage to Zaynab bint Jahsh for Zayd bin Haritha, but she refused him and said: I am better than him in lineage. She was a woman who had a sharp temper, so God revealed: ‘
h
And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman

, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any [any] choice about their affair…’”… the entire verse. It was said: It was revealed about Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt, because she offered herself to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he married her to Zayd ibn Haritha.

x: Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman

, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter ... to the end of the verse, he said: It was revealed about Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt, and she was one of the first women to emigrate. She offered herself to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he married her to Zayd ibn Haritha. She and her brother were dissatisfied and said: We only wanted the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so we married him to his slave. He said: Then the Qur’an was revealed,
h
And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman

, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any option in their decision ... to the end of the verse. He said: And a more comprehensive order than this came: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves (al-Ahzab 33:6). He said: That is specific, and this is consensus.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a rebuke from God to him: And remember, O Muhammad, when you said to the one whom God had blessed with guidance and whom You had blessed with emancipation, meaning Zayd ibn Haritha, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Keep your wife and fear God. (This is because Zayd bint Jahsh, as it was mentioned, was seen by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was pleased with her while she was in the lap of his freed slave. So he cast aversion to her in Zayd’s soul because God knew what had happened in the soul of His Prophet, so he wanted to separate from her. So Zayd mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Keep your wife, and he, may God bless him and grant him peace, loved for her to have separated from him so that he could marry her.

And fear God and fear God in what is due to Him over you regarding your wife. And conceal in yourself what God is going to reveal. He says: And conceal in yourself the love of his separation from her so that you can marry her if he separates from her, and God is going to reveal what You hide that in yourself, And you fear people, while God has more right to be feared. God Almighty says: “And you fear that people will say: He ordered a man to divorce his wife and married her when he divorced her, while God has more right to be feared than people.” And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And when you said to him upon whom God had bestowed favor - that is, Zayd, upon whom God had bestowed Islam, and I had bestowed favor: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had set him free: Keep your wife for yourself and fear God, while you concealed within yourself that which God is to bring to light. He said: And he was concealing within himself that he wished he had divorced her. Al-Hasan said: No verse was revealed to him that was more difficult for him than its statement: And you concealed within yourself that which God is to bring to light. If the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him Surat al-Ahzab 33:37 And when you said to him upon whom God had bestowed favor and you had bestowed favor, "Keep your wife to yourself and fear God," while you concealed within yourself that which God was to disclose, and you feared the people, while God has more right that you should fear Him. So when Zaid had no longer any need of her, We married her to you so that there would be no discomfort upon the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons. When they have satisfied their desire for them, and the command of God is to be done. peace, had concealed any of the revelation, he would have concealed it. And you fear the people, while God has more right that you should fear Him. He said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, feared what the people would say.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had married Zayd ibn Haritha to Zaynab bint Jahsh, his cousin. One day the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out wanting to see her, and there was a curtain of hair at the door. The wind lifted the curtain and it was revealed, and she was in her room, unveiled. Her admiration fell into the heart of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and when that happened, he disliked her to another. He came and said: ‘O Messenger of God, I want to leave my wife.’ He said: ‘What is the matter with you? Does anything about her worry you?’ He said: ‘No, by God, nothing about her worries me, O Messenger of God, and I have only seen good in her.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘Keep your wife and fear God.’ This is what God Almighty said: ‘And when you said to him whom God has bestowed favor upon and you have bestowed favor, “Keep your wife to yourself and fear God,” while you concealed within yourself that which God is to reveal. ’ You concealed within yourself that if he divorced her, you would marry her.”

c: Muhammad bin Musa Al-Jarashi told me: Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Abu Hamza, who said:
m: This verse, And you conceal within yourself what God is to reveal, was revealed about Zaynab bint Jahsh.

c: Khallad bin Aslam told us: Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zayd bin Jud’an, on the authority of Ali bin Hussein, who said:
m: God Almighty informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that Zaynab would be one of his wives. When Zayd came to him complaining about her, he said: Fear God and keep your wife. God said: And you conceal within yourself that which God is to reveal.

c: Ishaq bin Shaheen told me: Dawud told us, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Aisha, who said:
m: If the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had concealed anything of what was revealed to him from the Book of God, he would have concealed and you conceal within yourself that which God is to reveal, and you fear people, while God has more right that you should fear Him. And His saying, And when Zaid had no longer any need for her, We married her to you, God Almighty says: When Zaid bin Haritha had no longer any need for her, and that was his desire, from this comes the saying of the poet: And he said goodbye to me before I said goodbye to him, as he had spent much of our youth We married her to you means: We married Zaynab to you after Zayd divorced her and she became separated from him. so that there will be no blame upon the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons meaning: in marrying women whom they adopted who are not their sons or children, even if they divorced them and became sons of them. when they have had their pleasure in them means: when they have had their pleasure in them and separated from them and they have become lawful for others, and that was not a case of them giving them up for divorce. And the command of God is to be done means: whatever God decreed was to be done, meaning it was to come to pass. What is meant by this is that God’s decree concerning Zaynab, that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) would marry her, was past, done, and would come to pass. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
So that there will be no blame upon the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have no longer any need for them
, meaning: if they divorce them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had adopted Zayd ibn Haritha.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement, And when Zayd had no longer any need for her... to his statement, And the command of God was to be carried out, if that was from him and not for you, then that is the statement of God, And the wives of your sons who are from your loins
r
(An-Nisa’: 23)

c: Muhammad bin Uthman Al-Wasiti told me: Jaafar bin Awn told us, on the authority of Al-Mualla bin Irfan, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Jahsh, who said:
m: Aisha and Zainab boasted. Zainab said: I am the one whose marriage was revealed.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: Zainab, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: I can prove you by three things that no other woman can prove you by: My grandfather and your grandfather are one, God has married you to me from heaven, and the ambassador is Gabriel, peace be upon him.

x: God Almighty says: There was no blame on the Prophet for committing any sin in marrying the wife of his adopted son after he had separated from her.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: There is no blame upon the Prophet for what God has enjoined upon him: meaning what God has made permissible for him. And his statement,
h
The way of God

with those who passed on before, means: God Almighty would not have made His Prophet follow in what He permitted him, an example of what He did with the messengers who came before him, in that He did not make them sin by what He permitted them. His Prophet would not have feared people in what He commanded him to do or permitted him to do. And the accusative of His statement,
h
The way of God
, is in the sense of: a right from God, as if He said: We did that as a way of ours. And his saying,
h
And the command of God was a decreed fate
, means: And the command of God was a decreed judgment. Ibn Zayd used to say about this:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And the command of God is a predestined decree

, that God had His knowledge with Him before He created all things, so He completed it in His knowledge to create creation, command them and forbid them, and make a reward for those who obey Him and a punishment for those who disobey Him. Then when that command was decreed, He decreed it, and when He decreed it, it was hidden from Him. So He called it the Unseen and the Mother of the Book. And He created creation based on that book their provisions, their life spans, and their deeds, and whatever things befall them of ease and hardship from the book that He wrote would befall them. And he recited, Those will receive their portion of the Book until - when that is exhausted - there come to them Our messengers to take them in death (al-A’raf 7:37). And the command of the one who was decreed was decreed when He decreed it, so nothing will happen except what is in that, and what is in that Book, and in that decree. He decreed a command, then decreed it, then created based on it. So He said: The command of God that passed and was completed, and He created creation based on it was a predestined decree. He willed His decree, then created upon it, so He said: It was the command of God that was carried out and completed, and He created upon it the creation a predestined decree. He willed a command to carry out His command and decree, and He willed a command that He would be pleased with from His servants in their obedience to Him. So when what He willed of His servants’ obedience was for Him, He was pleased with it for them, and when what He willed was, He wanted to implement His command, plan, and decree in it. He recited:
h
And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind
(al-A’raf 7:179). So He willed that these be from the people of Hell, and He willed that their deeds be the deeds of the people of Hell, so He said:
h
And thus We have made pleasing to every nation their deeds
(al-An’am 6:108). And He said:
h
And thus have We made pleasing to many of the polytheists the killing of their children, their partners, to lead them astray and to confuse them with their religion
(al-An’am 6:137). These are the deeds of the people of Hell.
h
And if God had willed, they would not have done it
(al-An’am 6:137). He said:
h
And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy - devils
(al-An’am 6:112). These are the deeds of the people of Hell.
h
And if God had willed, they would not have done it
r
(Al-Anʿam: 137)
, he said And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy - devils
r
(Al-Anʿam: 112)
... to His saying And if your Lord had willed, they would not have done it
r
(Al-Anʿam: 112)
and he recited And they swore by God their most solemn oaths
r
(Al-Anʿam: 109)
... to everything before that they would not believe unless God willed
r
(Al-Anʿam: 111)
that they would believe in that, he said: So they removed it from the name by which he was called, he said: He is the Doer of what He wills, so they claimed that it was not what He willed.

x: God the Almighty says: This is the way of God with the messengers who came before Muhammad, who convey God's messages to those to whom they were sent, and fear God in not conveying that to them, and fear no one but God, for it is Him they fear if they fall short in conveying God's message to those to whom they were sent. He says to His Prophet Muhammad: So who are those messengers who have this description, so be and do not fear anyone before God, for God will protect you from all of His creation, and no one of His creation will protect you from Him, if He intends evil for you. And those in His statement, those who convey God's messages is in the accusative case in response to those in His statement, This is the way of God with those who came before, and His statement,
h
And sufficient is God as a Reckoner
, Allāh the Almighty says: And sufficient for you, O Muhammad, is God as a guardian of the deeds of His creation, and as a reckoner for them.

God Almighty says: O people, Muhammad was not the father of Zaid bin Haritha, nor was he the father of any of your men who were not born of Muhammad, so it would be forbidden for him to marry his wife after separating from her. But he is the Messenger of God and the Seal of the Prophets, who sealed prophethood and sealed it, so it will not be opened to anyone after him until the Day of Resurrection. And God has knowledge of everything of your deeds and your words and other than that, and nothing is hidden from Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Muhammad is not the father of any of your men

, he said: It was revealed about Zayd, he was not his son, and by my life, male children were born to him, he is the father of al-Qasim, Ibrahim, al-Tayyib, and al-Mutahar. But he is the Messenger of God and the Seal of the Prophets, meaning the last of them. And God is Knowing of all things.

c: Muhammad ibn Amara told me: Ali ibn Qadam told me: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Naseer ibn Dhaluq, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Husayn,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Muhammad is not the father of any of your men

, he said: It was revealed about Zayd ibn Haritha. The accusative in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, means repeating was the Messenger of God, and the nominative means resuming, but he is the Messenger of God. The reading in our view is the accusative. The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement and the Seal of the Prophets. The reciters of the regions, except for Al-Hasan and Asim, recited it with a kasra on the ta’ of Khatam Al-Nabiyyin, meaning that he is the seal of the prophets. It was mentioned that in the recitation of Abdullah but a prophet who sealed the prophets, this is evidence of the correctness of the recitation of the one who recited it with a kasra on the ta’, meaning that he is the one who sealed the prophets, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him and them. Al-Hasan and Asim recited it with a fatha on the ta’, meaning that he is the last of the prophets, as they recited makhtum with a seal of musk, meaning: its last is musk. Whoever recited it like that.

evidence.text: The reading in our view is the accusative.
The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement and the Seal of the Prophets.
The reciters of the regions, except for Al-Hasan and Asim, recited it with a kasra on the ta’ of Khatam Al-Nabiyyin, meaning that he is the seal of the prophets.

It was mentioned that in the recitation of Abdullah but a prophet who sealed the prophets, this is evidence of the correctness of the recitation of the one who recited it with a kasra on the ta’, meaning that he is the one who sealed the prophets, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him and them.
Al-Hasan and Asim recited it with a fatha on the ta’, meaning that he is the last of the prophets, as they recited makhtum with a seal of musk, meaning: its last is musk.
Whoever recited it like that.

x: God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, remember God with your hearts, your tongues, and your limbs, often, and do not let your bodies be devoid of His remembrance in any state within your capacity.
And glorify Him in the morning and the evening. He says: Pray to Him in the morning with the dawn prayer, and in the evening with the afternoon prayer.
And His statement,
h
It is He who sends blessings upon you

, and His angels do, means, the Most High says: Your Lord, whom you remember often and glorify morning and evening, if you do that, who will have mercy on you, praise you, and supplicate for you with His angels. It was said that the meaning of His statement, He sends blessings upon you, and His angels do, is that He will spread the good remembrance of you among the servants of God. And His statement,
h
That He may bring you out from darknesses into the light

, means: God's angels will supplicate for you, and God will bring you out from misguidance to guidance, and from disbelief to Islam. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement, Remember God with much remembrance, he said: He does not impose an obligation on His servants except that He has set a known limit for it, then He excuses those who do it in a state of excuse, other than remembrance, for God has not set a limit for it to reach and He has not excused anyone for abandoning it except one who is overcome by his mind. He said, Remember God while standing, sitting, and [lying] on your sides
r
(An-Nisa’: 103)

, by night and by day, on land and at sea, while traveling and at home, in wealth and poverty, sickness and health, in secret and in public, and in every situation. He said, Glorify Him morning and evening, so if you do that, He and His angels will pray upon you. God, the Almighty, said,
h
It is He who sends blessings upon you
, and so do His angels.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, And glorify Him in the morning and the evening means the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer. His saying,
h
To bring you out from darkness into light means from misguidance to guidance

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
It is He who sends blessings upon you

, and His angels [ask Him to do so], that He may bring you out from darkness into the light, he said: From misguidance to guidance. He said: Misguidance means darkness, and light means guidance. And His statement,
h
And He was Merciful to the believers
, means, the Most High, the Majestic, says:
h
And He was Merciful to the believers
in Him and His Messenger, that He would not punish them while they were obedient to Him and followed His command.

x: h
Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be
, 'Peace.'" God Almighty says: The greeting of these believers on the Day of Resurrection in Paradise will be, 'Peace.'
Some of them will say to one another: 'It is a security for us and for you that we have entered this entrance from God that He will not torment us in the Fire forever.'

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, “
h
Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be
, ‘Peace,’” he said: The greeting of the people of Paradise will be, ‘Peace.’ And His statement,
h
And He has prepared for them a generous reward
, means: And He has prepared for these believers a generous reward for their obedience to Him in this world, and that is Paradise.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And He has prepared for them a noble reward, meaning Paradise.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, Indeed, We have sent you as a witness over your nation by conveying to them the message with which We sent you, and giving them good tidings of Paradise if they believe you and act upon what you have brought them from your Lord, and a warner of the Fire that they will enter and be tormented therein if they disbelieve you and disobey what you have brought them from God. And what we said about that was said by the people of interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness over your nation with the message, and a bringer of good tidings of Paradise, and a warner of the Fire.

x: And his saying,
h
And calling to God
, means: And calling to the oneness of God, and to single out divinity for Him alone, and to sincerely obey Him alone, without any other gods or idols.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
and calling to God

to testify that there is no god but God. His statement, By His permission, means: By His command to you to do so. And an illuminating lamp, means: And a light for His creation, illuminating the light that I have brought to them from God, His servants. An illuminating lamp, means: A light that illuminates for whoever is illuminated by its light and acts according to what He has commanded. What He means by that is: That He guides with it whoever follows him from his nation.

x: And His statement,
h
And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from God great bounty

, God Almighty says: And give good tidings to the people of faith in God, O Muhammad, that they will have from God great bounty. He says: That they will have from God’s reward for their obedience to Him a great multiplication, and that is the great bounty from God to them.
And His statement,
h
And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites

, means: Do not obey the words of a disbeliever or a hypocrite, lest you hear him calling you to fall short in conveying God’s messages to those of His creation to whom He sent you with them. And ignore their harm, means: Turn away from their harm to you, and be patient with it, and do not let that prevent you from carrying out God’s command with His servants, and carrying out whatever He has charged you with. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And turn away from their harm, he said: Turn away from them.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And leave their harm means be patient with their harm. His saying,
h
And put your trust in God

, means: Entrust your affairs to God, and trust in Him, for He will suffice you for everything besides Him, until His command and judgment come to you. And sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs, meaning: God is sufficient for you as a guardian of your affairs, and as your protector and trustee.

x: God the Most High says:
h
O you who have believed

in God and His Messenger, When you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them meaning before you have had intercourse with them, then you have no waiting period to count for them meaning: no counting of menstrual periods, nor months to count for them, so provide for them: meaning: give them what they enjoy of honor or money. And His statement, and release them with gracious release means: and set them free with kindness, which is a gracious release. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told us, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
O you who have believed

, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then you have no waiting period to count for them. This is about a man who marries a woman, then divorces her before he has touched her. If he divorces her once, she is separated from him, and there is no waiting period for her to marry whomever she wants. Then he recited, Then give them their due and release them with gracious freedom. He said: If he specified a dowry for her, then she is only entitled to half. If he did not specify a dowry for her, then he gives her his due according to his ease or difficulty, which is the gracious release.

x: Some of them said: The pleasure marriage in this place was abrogated by His saying then half of what you imposed (al-Baqarah 2:237).
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
O you who have believed

, when you marry believing women… to His statement, a gracious release. He said: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: Then this word abrogated the pleasure contract And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dowry, then give half of what you specified (al-Baqarah 2:237).

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us: Shu'bah told us:
m: I heard Qatada narrating on the authority of Sa'id ibn Al-Musayyab: This verse was abrogated:
h
O you who have believed

, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then you have no waiting period for them to count, so provide for them. He said: This verse in Al-Baqarah was abrogated.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you
h
your wives to whom you have given their dowries
. Meaning: those whom you married for a specified dowry.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Your wives to whom you have given their dowries
, he said: their dowries.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you
h
your wives to whom you have given their dowries
, he said: Every woman to whom he gave a dowry, God made her lawful to him.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you
h
your wives to whom you have given their dowries
... to His statement,
h
Purely for you

, apart from the believers, so he did whatever he wanted of this designation, whether much or little. And His statement, And what your right hand possesses from what God has bestowed upon you, means: And We have made lawful for you your female slaves whom you took captive and whom you owned through captivity, and they became yours through God’s victory over you from the spoils. And the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you, so God made lawful for him, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the daughters of his paternal uncles and his paternal aunts and his maternal uncle and his maternal aunts, the emigrating women with him from among them, but not those of them who did not emigrate with him.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abdullah bin Musa narrated to us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Umm Hani’, who said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, proposed to me, so I apologized to him with my excuse, then God revealed to him: Indeed, We have made lawful to you
h
your wives to whom you have given their dowries

... until His saying: those who emigrated with you. She said: So I was not made lawful to him, I did not emigrate with him, I was among those who were freed. It has been mentioned that in Ibn Masoud’s reading and your maternal aunts and those who emigrated with you with a waw, and even if it is like that in his reading, it is possible that it has the same meaning as our reading without the waw, and that is because the Arabs sometimes insert the waw in describing someone who has been mentioned before, as the poet said: Rashid and Ibn Marwan would not have done so until the order was issued by the source. Rashid is the son of Marwan, and Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim interpreted this reading of Abdullah as meaning that they were a type other than his maternal aunts’ daughters, and that they were every emigrant who emigrated with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The report about him mentioned that:

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say in the letter of Ibn Masʿud and those who emigrated with you meaning by that: everything that emigrated with him, not from the daughters of the paternal uncle and aunt, nor from the daughters of the maternal uncle and aunt. And his saying,
h
And a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet
, means: And We made a woman lawful for him if she gives herself to the Prophet without a dowry.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet without a dowry

, so he did not do that, and it was permissible for him specifically, not for the believers. He mentioned that this is in Abdullah’s reading and a believing woman who gave herself to the Prophet without in, and the meaning of that and the meaning of our reading in which in is one, and that is like what the speaker says in speech: There is nothing wrong with him having intercourse with a slave girl if he owns her, and a slave girl is his property. And his saying,
h
If the Prophet wants to marry her
, means: If he wants to marry her, it is permissible for him to marry her if she gives herself to him without a dowry.
h
Purely for you
, means: It is not permissible for anyone from your nation to approach a woman who gives herself to him. Rather, that is
h
purely for you
, O Muhammad. She is
h
purely for you
and not for the rest of your nation.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
Purely for you

, not for the believers, meaning: A woman is not to give herself to a man without the permission of a guardian or a dowry, except for the Prophet, she is exclusively for him, not for the people. And they claim that it was revealed about Maymunah bint al-Harith, that she was the one who gave herself to the Prophet.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement, O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives ... to His statement,
h
Purely for you

, not for the believers, he said: Every woman to whom he gave a dowry, God had made her lawful to him until these women gave themselves to him, so they were lawful to him, not for the believers, without a dowry,
h
purely for you
, not for the believers, except for a woman who had a husband.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Salih ibn Muslim, he said:
m: I asked Al-Sha’bi about a woman who gave herself to a man, he said: It is not permissible, it is not permissible for him, she only belonged to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The reciters differed in their reading of the statement, If she gives herself, so the majority of reciters in the regions read it as If she gives with a kasra on the alif as a condition, meaning: if she gives.

c: It was reported on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri
m: that he read If she gives with a fatha on the alif, meaning: and We made lawful for him to marry a believing woman, she gave herself to him. The reading that I do not permit to differ from is the breaking of the alif due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it. As for his saying,
h
Purely for you

, not for the believers, this is not for the believers. It was mentioned that before this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he could marry any women he wanted, but God restricted Surat al-Ahzab 33:50 O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you
h
your wives to whom you have given their dowries

, and those your right hand possesses from what God has given you as spoils of war, and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you
h
and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet
- if the Prophet desires to marry her - exclusively for you from Except for the believers.
h
We have already known what We have enjoined upon them concerning their wives

and those their right hands possess, so that there will be no difficulty for you. And ever is God Forgiving and Merciful. it to these, so he did not count them and restricted the rest of his nation to two, three, and four.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us:
m: I heard Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, on the authority of Ziyad, a man from the Ansar, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, that the women whom God made lawful for the Prophet were those whom God mentioned: O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you
h
your wives to whom you have given their dowries
… until His saying: in their wives. God only made lawful for the believers two, three, and four.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives… to the end of the verse, he said: God forbade him all other women, and before that he could marry any women he wanted, that was not forbidden to him, so his wives were very anxious about that to marry any people he liked, so when God revealed, Indeed, I have forbidden to you from mankind other than what I have related to you, his wives were pleased with that. Scholars differed regarding the believing woman who offered herself to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). Was there a woman like that with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him)?

x: Some of them said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) did not have any women with him except through a marriage contract or through possession. As for as a gift, he did not have any of them with him.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Yunus bin Bakir told us, on the authority of Anbasa bin Al-Azhar, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: There was no woman with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who gave herself as a gift.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja'far told us: Shu'bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, that he said
m: regarding this verse,
h
And a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet
, he said: That she gives. As for those who said that he had women with him, some of them said: It was Maymunah bint Al-Harith.

x: Some of them said: It was Umm Sharik.
Some of them said: It was Zaynab bint Khuzaymah.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: And a believing woman if she offers herself to the Prophet. He said: She is Maymunah bint al-Harith.

x: Some of them said: Zainab bint Khuzaymah, the mother of the poor, was a woman from the Ansar.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us: Al-Hakam told us:
m: ʿAbd Al-Malik wrote to the people of Medina asking them. He said: Ali wrote to him - Shuʿbah said: I think he was Ali bin Al-Husayn. He said: Aban bin Taghlib told me about it, on the authority of Al-Hakam, that it was Ali bin Al-Husayn who wrote to him - he said: She is a woman from the Asad tribe called Umm Sharik, who offered herself to the Prophet. He said: Shuʿbah told us, he said:

c: Abdullah bin Abi al-Safar told me, on the authority of al-Shaʿbi,
m: that she was a woman from the Ansar, who offered herself to the Prophet, and she was one of those who postponed marriage.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Saeed told me, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Khawlah bint Hakim ibn al-Awqas from Banu Salim,
m: she was one of those who offered themselves to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Saeed bin Abi Al-Zinad narrated to me, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwa, on the authority of his father, who said: We used to say that Umm Sharik had offered herself to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she was a righteous woman. And His statement,
h
We have already known what We have enjoined upon them concerning their wives

, means, the Most High says: We have already known what We have enjoined upon the believers concerning their wives if they wish to marry them, which We have not enjoined upon you, and what We have made specific to them in this regard, without you, which is that We have enjoined upon them that it is not permissible for them to contract a marriage with a free Muslim woman except with a guardian from the agnatic kin and just witnesses, and it is not permissible for them to have more than four of them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
b.via: Khawlah bint Hakim ibn al-Awqas from Banu Salim

x: Who said that?

c: Abdullah bin Ahmed bin Shabwa told me, he said: Mutahhar told us, he said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: My father told me, on the authority of Matar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding the statement of God,
h
We have already known what We have enjoined upon them concerning their wives
, he said: Among what God has enjoined upon them is that there is no marriage except with a guardian and two witnesses.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
We know what We have enjoined upon them concerning their wives
. He said: concerning the four.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
We know what We have enjoined upon them concerning their wives

, he said: Among the things that God enjoined upon them was that a woman should not be married except with a guardian and a dowry in the presence of two just witnesses, and that it was not permissible for them from among the women except four, and those whom their right hands possess. And His statement, and those whom their right hands possess, meaning, the Most High says: We have already made obligatory upon the believers concerning their wives, because it is not lawful for them to marry more than four of them. And those whom their right hands possess, if they are believers or People of the Book, are all lawful for them through captivity, concubinage, and other means of ownership. And His statement, "so that there will be no difficulty for you. And God is Forgiving and Merciful," meaning, the Most High says: Indeed, We have made lawful for you, O Muhammad, your wives whom We mentioned in this verse, and a believing woman if she offers herself to the Prophet, if the Prophet wishes to marry her, so that there will be no sin or hardship on you in marrying whomever you marry from these categories whom it is permissible for you to marry from those named in this verse. And God is Forgiving to you and to the people of faith in you, and Merciful to you and to them, that He does not punish them for a past sin of theirs after they have repented from it.

evidence.text: It has been mentioned that in Ibn Masoud’s reading and your maternal aunts and those who emigrated with you with a waw, and even if it is like that in his reading, it is possible that it has the same meaning as our reading without the waw, and that is because the Arabs sometimes insert the waw in describing someone who has been mentioned before, as the poet said: Rashid and Ibn Marwan would not have done so until the order was issued by the source.

Rashid is the son of Marwan, and Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim interpreted this reading of Abdullah as meaning that they were a type other than his maternal aunts’ daughters, and that they were every emigrant who emigrated with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

He mentioned that this is in Abdullah’s reading and a believing woman who gave herself to the Prophet without in, and the meaning of that and the meaning of our reading in which in is one, and that is like what the speaker says in speech: There is nothing wrong with him having intercourse with a slave girl if he owns her, and a slave girl is his property.

The reciters differed in their reading of the statement, If she gives herself, so the majority of reciters in the regions read it as If she gives with a kasra on the alif as a condition, meaning: if she gives.
The reading that I do not permit to differ from is the breaking of the alif due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.

x: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his statement,
h
You may postpone whomever you wish of them and take to yourself whomever you wish
Some of them said: By his statement,
h
You may postpone
, he meant,
h
You may take to yourself
, and by his statement,
h
You may take to yourself
, he meant, You may take in.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
You may postpone
whichever of them you wish, meaning:
h
you may postpone

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
You may postpone
any of them you wish, he said: You may remove from your wives whomever you wish without divorce, and take to yourself whomever you wish, he said: You may return her to you.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
You may defer from them whom you wish and take to yourself whom you wish
, he said: So God absolved him from that, that he may leave whomever he wishes of them, and come to whomever he wishes of them without dividing them, and the Prophet of God used to divide them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us: Amr told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin:
m: h
You may postpone whomever you wish of them and take to yourself whomever you wish

. He said: When they feared that he would divorce them, they said: O Prophet of God, give us whatever you wish of your wealth and yourself. Among those he postponed were Sawdah bint Zam’ah, Juwayriyyah, Safiyyah, Umm Habibah, and Maymuna. Among those he took to sheltering him were: Aisha, Umm Salamah, Hafsa, and Zaynab.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say, regarding His statement,
h
You may defer from them whom you wish and take to yourself whom you wish
, then whatever he wishes to do in dividing among the women, God has made it permissible for him to do so.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin,
m: regarding His statement,
h
You may defer from them whom you wish
, and
h
you may take to yourself

whom you wish. Among those whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave refuge were Aisha, Hafsa, Zainab, and Umm Salamah, and his share of himself with them was equal to his share. Among those whom he had the greatest hope of were Sawda, Juwayriyya, Safiyya, Umm Habiba, and Maymuna, and he would divide for them whatever he wished, and he had wanted to leave them, so they said: Divide for us from yourself whatever you wish, and leave us as we are.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: You may divorce and release whomever you wish of your wives, and keep whomever you wish of them but do not divorce them.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, You may Surat al-Ahzab 33:51
h
You may postpone
whomever you wish of them, and
h
you may take to yourself
whomever you wish.
h
And whoever you desire of those whom you have set aside
, there is no blame upon you. That is more suitable that their eyes may be comforted and they may not grieve and be satisfied with what you have given them, all of them.
h
And God knows what is in your hearts
