, and God is ever Knowing and Forbearing. postpone whomever you wish of them - the Mothers of the Believers - and
h
you may take to yourself

whomever you wish - meaning: the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. What is meant by postponement is: you may release whomever you wish of them, and what is meant by taking to yourself is: you may keep whomever you like of them.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: You can leave marrying whomever you want, and marry whomever you want from the women of your nation.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Al-Hasan said
m: regarding His statement, You may defer any of them you wish and take to yourself any you wish, he said: When the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, proposed to a woman, no man had the right to propose to her until he married her or left her. It was said: That is what God made for His Prophet when some of them were jealous of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and some of them asked for more maintenance than he used to give them, so God commanded him to give them the choice between this world and the Hereafter, and to release the one who chose this worldly life and its adornments, and to keep the one who chose God and His Messenger. So when they chose God and His Messenger, it was said to them: Now acknowledge your contentment with God and His Messenger, whether the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided among you, or did not divide, or divided among some of you and did not divide among others, and favored some of you over others in maintenance, or did not favor others, treated you equally, or did not treat you equally, then the matter in that is up to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and you have no part in that. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, according to what was mentioned, with what God made for him, treated them equally in the division except for one of them whom he wanted to divorce, so she agreed to leave the division to her. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told me, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin, he said:
m: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to divorce his wives, they said to him: Assign to us from yourself and your wealth whatever you wish, so God commanded him to take in four and to grant five. Sufyan ibn Wakee’ narrated:

c: Ubaidah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, that she said:
m: Isn’t a woman ashamed to give herself to a man? Until God revealed: You may defer to any of them you wish, and
h
you may take to yourself

whomever you wish. I said: Your Lord is quick to grant your desires. Ibn Wakee’ narrated: Muhammad ibn Bishr, meaning Al-Abdi, narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, that she used to taunt the women who had offered themselves to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she said: Isn’t a woman ashamed to offer herself without a dowry? Then this verse was revealed, or God revealed: You may defer to any of them you wish, and
h
you may take to yourself
any you wish, and whoever you desire of those you have set aside. So I said: I see that your Lord is hastening to fulfill your desires for you.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, You may defer to whomever you wish of them and take to yourself whomever you wish… the verse, he said: His wives had been jealous of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he had abandoned them for a month, then the choice was revealed from God to him concerning them, so he recited until he reached, And do not display yourselves like that of the times of the former ignorance, so he gave them the choice between choosing that he set them free and divorce them or that they stay if God and His Messenger wanted, on the condition that they were the mothers of the believers, never to be wedded, and that he would take to himself whomever he wished of those who had offered themselves to him until he could raise his head to her, and defer to whomever he wished, until he could raise his head to her. And whoever desires of those with whom he has been married and removes a wife, there is no blame upon him. That is more likely that their eyes may be comforted and he not grieve, and that they may be content when they know that it is My decree over them to prefer some of them over others. That is more likely that they will be content. He said, And whoever I desire of those I removed, whoever I desire He was afflicted with it, and he who was isolated was not afflicted with it. So he gave them the choice between being satisfied with this or he would leave them. They chose God and His Messenger, except for one Bedouin woman who went away. And he remained on that path, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and God had stipulated this condition for him. He continued to be just between them until he met God. The most correct of the sayings on this matter, in my opinion, is that it is said that God, the Exalted, made it possible for His Prophet to postpone from among the women whom He made lawful for him whomever he wished, and to take to himself from among them whomever he wished. This is because He did not limit the meaning of postponement and shelter to the married women who were under his care, when this verse was revealed, without others from whom shelter or postponement could be newly introduced. Since this is the case, the meaning of the statement is:
h
You may postpone

whomever you wish from among those who have offered themselves to you and made their marriage lawful for you, so do not accept them or marry them, or from those who are under your care, so do not remain with them, and
h
you may take to yourself

whomever you wish from among those who have offered themselves to you, or from among the women whom I have made lawful for you to marry, so accept them or marry them, and from those who are under your care, so have intercourse with them if you wish, and leave them if you wish without dividing them. And His statement,
h
And whoever you desire of those whom you have set aside
, there is no blame upon you.

x: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.

Some of them said: The meaning of that is: And whoever of your wives you have married and had intercourse with, of those whom you have not married and you have set aside from intercourse, there is no blame upon you.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, And if you desire among those whom you have set aside, there is no blame upon you, he said: All of these are regarding his wives. If he wishes, he may come to whomever he wishes among them, and there is no blame upon him.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And whoever you seek of those you have dismissed, he said: And whoever you seek will attain him, and whoever you dismiss will not attain him.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: And if you replace one of your wives whom you have put off, and you set him free, or if one of them dies among those whom you have made lawful for you, then there is no blame upon you.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding His statement, “And if you seek [for marriage] among those whom you have set aside, there is no blame upon you. That is more suitable that their eyes may be comforted and they will not grieve and be satisfied with what you have given them all,” meaning by that: the women whom God has made lawful for him from among the daughters of the paternal uncle, the paternal aunt, the maternal uncle, and the maternal aunt. who emigrated with you, meaning: If one of the women with you dies, or you release him, then it is lawful for you to replace the one of the women with you who died, or you released him, and it is not permissible for you to add anything to the waiting period of the women with you. The more correct of the two interpretations is the interpretation of the one who said: The meaning of that is: And from among your women whom you seek to have sexual intercourse with, from whom you have separated from them, there is no blame upon you, because his statement, That is more likely to please their eyes, indicates the correctness of that, because there is no meaning to their eyes being pleased if he, may God bless him and grant him peace, replaced the dead or divorced one among them, unless he meant by that: That is more likely to please the eyes of the married one among them, and that is something that is indicated by the apparent meaning of the revelation, which is far-fetched. And His saying, That is more likely that their eyes will be comforted and they will not grieve, means: This that I have given you, O Muhammad, of My permission for you to postpone whomever you wish from the women whom I have given you to postpone, and to take in whomever you wish from them, and My removing from you the difficulty in your seeking to have intercourse with whomever you wish to have intercourse with from your women, and your separating from that whomever you have secluded from them, is more likely for your women to have their eyes comforted by it and for them not to grieve and for them to be satisfied with what
h
I have given them

all of preferring whomever I have preferred of a portion or maintenance, and preferring whomever I have preferred from them over other women, if they know that it is from My pleasure with you in that, and My permission for you to do it, and a release from Me, not from you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: This is more likely to make their eyes happy and not grieve and to make them content with what
h
I have given them
all. If they know that this came from God as a concession, it is better for their souls and less likely to cause them grief.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement, something similar. The correct reading of His statement, because
h
I have given them
all is the nominative case. Nothing else is permissible according to us. This is because all of them is not an adjective for the ha in His statement,
h
I have given them
. Rather, the meaning of the statement is: and they are all satisfied. This is an emphasis on what is in they are satisfied of the mention of women. If it were made an emphasis on the ha in
h
I have given them

, it would have no meaning. The reading in the accusative case is not permissible for this reason, and because of the consensus of the hujjat among the reciters that the reciter is mistaken in this way. And His statement,
h
And God knows what is in your hearts

, means: God knows what is in the hearts of men of inclination towards some of the women he has over others, out of passion and love. He says: Therefore, He has removed from you the difficulty, O Surat al-Ahzab 33:51
h
You may postpone
whomever you wish of them, and
h
you may take to yourself
whomever you wish.
h
And whoever you desire of those whom you have set aside
, there is no blame upon you. That is more suitable that their eyes may be comforted and they may not grieve and be satisfied with what you have given them, all of them.
h
And God knows what is in your hearts

, and God is ever Knowing and Forbearing. Muhammad, in what has been removed from you regarding seeking whomever you desire from among those whom you have set aside, as a favor and honor from Him to you. And God is All-Knowing, means: God has knowledge of the deeds of His servants, and other than that of all things. Forbearing, means: He is forbearing towards His servants, that He does not hasten punishment from those who commit sins among them, but He is forbearing and patient with them, so that whoever repents among them may repent, and He may remove from his sins whoever turns back among them.

evidence.text: The correct reading of His statement, because I have given them all is the nominative case.
The reading in the accusative case is not permissible for this reason, and because of the consensus of the hujjat among the reciters that the reciter is mistaken in this way.

x: The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of the Almighty’s saying,
h
It is not lawful for you to take other women after
that.
Some of them said: The meaning of that is:
h
It is not lawful for you to take other women after
the women you gave a choice to, so they chose God, His Messenger, and the Hereafter.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
It is not lawful for you to marry other women after that… the verse to a watcher
. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade him from marrying any other women after his first wives.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
It is not lawful for you to take other women after
that... to his statement, except those your right hand possesses. He said: When he gave them the choice, and they chose God, His Messenger, and the Hereafter, he restricted it to them and said,
h
It is not lawful for you to take other women after
that, nor to exchange them for other wives. And they are the nine who chose God and His Messenger.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: It is not permissible for you to take women after those whom We have made lawful for you by saying, O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives... until His saying, those who emigrated with you and a believing woman
h
if she offers herself to the Prophet
. It is as if the speakers of this statement directed the speech to mean: It is not permissible for you to take women except those whom We have made lawful for you.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me: Abd al-Wahhab told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, on the authority of Ziyad, who said
m: to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: If all of the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had died, would it have been possible for him to marry again? He said: It would not have been forbidden to him. So I recited to him this verse: O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives 2:11. He said: He made lawful for him a variety of women and prohibited for him everything else. Lawful for him is every woman whose reward he has given her, and what his right hand possesses from what God has bestowed upon him, and the daughters of his paternal uncles and the daughters of his paternal aunts, and the daughters of his maternal uncles and the daughters of his maternal aunts, and every woman who offers herself to him if he wishes to marry her exclusively for him, not for the believers.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-A’la told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, on the authority of Ziyad Al-Ansari, who said:
m: I said to Ubayy ibn Ka’b: Tell me, if the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had died, would it be permissible for him to marry again? He said: What would make that forbidden to him? He said: I said: His statement,
h
It is not lawful for you to marry other women after
that. He said: God only made certain women permissible for him.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, he said: Muhammad ibn Abi Musa told me, on the authority of Ziyad,
m: a man from the Ansar, he said: I said to Ubayy ibn Ka’b: Tell me, if the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had died, would he not have been able to marry again? He said: What prevents him from that? And perhaps Dawud said: What forbids him from that? I said: His statement,
h
It is not lawful for you to marry other women after
that. He said: God only made lawful for him a certain type of women, and He said, O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives ... to His statement,
h
If she offers herself to the Prophet
. Then it was said to him,
h
It is not lawful for you to marry other women after
that.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam bin Salm told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of someone
m: who mentioned it, on the authority of Abu Salih: It is not permissible for you to marry women after that. He said: He was ordered not to marry a Bedouin woman or a foreign woman, and to marry after that from the women of Tihama, and whomever he wanted from the daughters of his paternal uncle and paternal aunt, and his maternal uncle and maternal aunt, if he wanted, three hundred. Surat al-Ahzab 33:52
h
It is not lawful for you to take other women after
this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty should please you, except those your right hand possesses. And ever is God, over all things, a Watcher.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: It is not lawful for you to have women after these except your paternal cousins... the verse.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh say: Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement,
h
It is not lawful for you to marry other women after

that, meaning: after the naming, he said: It is not lawful for you to marry any woman except a cousin or a aunt’s daughter, or a maternal uncle or a aunt’s daughter, or a woman who has offered herself to you, whoever of them migrated with the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And in the wording of Ibn Mas’ud and those who migrated with you, he means by that: everyone who migrated with him, not from the daughters of the paternal uncle or aunt, nor from the daughters of the maternal uncle or aunt.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: It is not permissible for you to have women who are not Muslims. As for Jewish, Christian, and polytheist women, they are forbidden to you.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
It is not lawful for you to marry women after

that, neither a Jewish woman, nor a Christian woman, nor an unbeliever. The first of the opinions that is most correct in my opinion is the opinion of the one who said: The meaning of this is: It is not permissible for you to marry women after those whom I made lawful for you by saying, Indeed, We have made lawful for you your wives to whom you have given their dowries... until His saying, And a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet. I said that this is more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse, because His statement,
h
It is not lawful for you to have other women

, follows His statement, Indeed, We have made lawful for you your wives, and it is not permissible for him to say, I have made these lawful for you, and they are not lawful for you except by one of them abrogating the other, and on the condition that the time for imposing one of the two verses is the implementation of the other of them. If this is the case, and there is no proof or indication that the ruling of one of the two verses abrogates the ruling of the other, and one of them was not revealed before the other, and it is not impossible for them to be valid, then it is not permissible to say that one of them abrogates the other. If this is the case, and the statement of those who said: The meaning of this is: It is not permissible after the Muslim women to be Jewish, Christian, or unbelieving, has no clear meaning, since his saying after only means: After the named women mentioned previously in the verse before this verse, and the verse in which the named women were mentioned as permissible for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not mention the permissibility of all Muslim women. Rather, it mentioned his wives and his right hand possessions that God bestowed upon him, and the daughters of his paternal uncles and the daughters of his paternal aunts, and the daughters of his maternal uncles and the daughters of his maternal aunts, who migrated with him, and a believing woman if she offered herself to the Prophet, so the unbelieving women are specifically prohibited, then what we said about that is correct, unlike the statement of those who disagreed with our statement about it. The reciters differed in their reading of the phrase It is not permissible for you to have women. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa read it as it is permissible for you with a ya, meaning: it is not permissible for you to have any women after that.

x: Some of the reciters of Basra read it as It is not permissible for you to have women with a ta, indicating that it is a verb for women, and women is the plural for many of them. The more correct of the two readings is the one that reads it with a ya’, for the reason I mentioned to them, and the consensus of the authoritative reciters on reading it with it, and the anomaly of those who disagreed with them on that. And His statement, nor that you exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty should please you, the people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.

Some of them said: The meaning of that is: It is not lawful for you to have women after the Muslim women, neither Jewish nor Christian nor disbelieving, nor that you exchange the Muslim women for other disbelieving women.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Nor that you exchange them for other wives and Nor that you exchange the Muslim women for other wives from among the Christians, Jews, and polytheists “even if their beauty pleases you, except those your right hand possesses.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibn Razin,
m: regarding his statement,
h
It is not lawful for you to marry other women after this

, nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty should please you, except those your right hand possesses, he said: It is not lawful for you to marry polytheist women except those you have captured and whom your right hand possesses.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Do not exchange your wives who are in your care for other wives, by divorcing them and marrying others.
Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, nor that you exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty should please you, meaning: It is not permissible for you to divorce any of your wives if you do not like them, so that was not permissible for him.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Nor should you exchange your wives for someone else, by giving him your wife and taking his wife.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, nor that you exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty should please you, he said: The Arabs in the Age of Ignorance used to exchange their wives, one would give his wife to another and another would take his wife. So He said,
h
It is not lawful for you to take other women after

this, nor that you exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty should please you, except those your right hand possesses, there is no problem with exchanging your female slave for whomever you wish, but not for free women. He said: And that was among their practices in the Age of Ignorance. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of this is: Nor that you divorce your wives and replace them with other wives. We said that this is more correct, because we have previously explained that the statement of the one who said that the meaning of his saying
h
it is not lawful for you to marry women after

that is that it is not lawful for you to marry a Jewish, Christian or infidel woman, is a statement that has no basis. If that is the case, then his statement, nor that you exchange them for a disbelieving woman is meaningless, since among the Muslim women were those who were forbidden to him by His statement,
h
It is not lawful for you to have other wives after

that, which we have previously indicated. As for what Ibn Zayd said about that, it is also meaningless, because if it had meant exchange, the reading and revelation would have been: nor that you exchange them for other wives, or nor that you exchange them with a damma on the ta’, but the agreed-upon reading, nor that you exchange them with a fatha on the ta’, means: nor that you exchange them, even though what Ibn Zayd mentioned of the actions of the Jahiliyyah is not known among any nation that we know of: that a man exchanges his free wife for another, so it is said: that was from their actions, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade doing something like it.

x: Was it not possible for the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) to marry another woman in addition to the other wives he had, so that the interpretation of his statement, nor that you exchange them for other wives, would be directed to what you interpreted it to be? Or he would say: Where is the mention of his wives who were with him in this place, so that the ha in his statement, nor that you exchange them for other wives, would be from the mention of them, and it would be assumed that the ha in this refers to the women, in his statement,
h
It is not lawful for you to take other wives after
that?

The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was allowed to marry whomever he wished from the women whom God had made lawful for him in addition to the other wives he had with him on the day this verse was revealed. Rather, he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was forbidden by this verse to separate from the one he had with by divorce, intending thereby to replace her with another woman, out of admiration for the beauty of the one he had replaced with, since God had made them the mothers of the believers and given them the choice between this worldly life and the Hereafter, and to be content with God and His Messenger. They chose God, His Messenger, and the Hereafter, and were thus forbidden to anyone else. He was forbidden from separating from them by divorce. As for marrying anyone other than them, he was not forbidden from that, rather God made that lawful for him as He has explained in His Book.

c: It was narrated from Aisha
m: that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not die until God had made the women of the earth lawful for him.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Aisha, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not die until women were made lawful for him, meaning the people of the earth.

c: Ubaid bin Ismail Al-Habbari told me: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Aisha, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not die until women were made lawful for him.

c: Al-Abbas bin Abi Talib told us, he said: Mu’alla told us, he said: Wahib told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ubayd bin Umair Al-Laythi, on the authority of Aisha, she said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not die until it was made permissible for him to marry as many women as he wished.

c: Abu Zaid Umar ibn Shabbah told me: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, who said: I think Ubayd ibn Umair told me,
m: Abu Zaid said, and Abu Asim said once, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not die until God made women lawful for him. He said: Abu al-Zubayr said: I witnessed a man speaking to Ata’.

c: Ahmad bin Mansour told us: Musa bin Ismail told us: Hammam told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ubayd bin Umair, on the authority of Aisha, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not die until women were made lawful for him.

x: If the matter is as you have described, that God forbade His Prophet in this verse from divorcing his wives whom he gave a choice to and they chose him, then what is the basis of the report narrated about him that he divorced Hafsa and Surat al-Ahzab 33:52
h
It is not lawful for you to take other women after

this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty should please you, except those your right hand possesses. And ever is God, over all things, a Watcher. then took her back, and that he wanted to divorce Sawda until she reconciled with him to refrain from divorcing her, and she gave her day to Aisha?

That was before this verse was revealed. The evidence for the correctness of what we have said, that this was before God forbade His Prophet from divorcing them, is the narration that was reported that Umar entered upon Hafsah to punish her when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had separated from his wives. He said to her: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had divorced you, so you spoke to him and he took you back. By God, if he divorced you, or had he divorced you, I would not have spoken to him about you. This was undoubtedly before the verse of choice was revealed, because the verse of choice was only revealed when the time for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to swear to separate from them had passed.

As for the evidence that Sawda’s affair was before the revelation of this verse, God only commanded His Prophet to give his wives the choice between separating from him and staying with him on the condition that they would not have a share, that he would defer to whomever he wished from them, and take in whomever he wished from them, and give preference to whomever he wished from them over whomever he wished. For this reason, God Almighty said to him, “And if you desire of those you have set aside, there is no blame upon you. That is more likely that their eyes will be comforted and they will not grieve and they will be satisfied with what you have given them all.” It is impossible that the reconciliation between her and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took place on her leaving Aisha that day in a situation where she had no day with him. It is not permissible for that to have happened from her except in a situation where she had a right from him on a day that was hers and it was obligatory for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to give it to her, and that was not for them after the choice, as I have described before in what has passed in this book of ours.

So the interpretation of the statement is: It is not lawful for you, O Muhammad, to take women after those whom I made lawful for you in the previous verse, nor to divorce your women whom God, His Messenger, and the Hereafter chose, and exchange them for other wives, even if the beauty of whomever you wish to exchange for them pleases you, except what your right hand inclines to. And in His statement, to exchange them there is a nominative case, because its meaning is: It is not lawful for you to take women after that, nor to exchange your wives. Otherwise, in His statement, except what your right hand possesses, there is an exception from women. And the meaning of that is: It is not lawful for you to take women after those whom I made lawful for you, except what your right hand possesses of female slaves, for you may take from any kind of female slaves you wish. And His statement,
h
And God is a Watcher over all things
, means: And God is a Guardian over all things, what He has made lawful for you, what He has forbidden you, and other than that of all things.
Nothing of that is hidden from Him, and preserving all of that does not burden Him.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And God is ever a Watcher over all things: meaning a Guardian, according to al-Hasan and Qatada.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of the phrase It is not permissible for you to have women.
The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa read it as it is permissible for you with a ya, meaning: it is not permissible for you to have any women after that.
Some of the reciters of Basra read it as It is not permissible for you to have women with a ta, indicating that it is a verb for women, and women is the plural for many of them.

The more correct of the two readings is the one that reads it with a ya’, for the reason I mentioned to them, and the consensus of the authoritative reciters on reading it with it, and the anomaly of those who disagreed with them on that.

As for what Ibn Zayd said about that, it is also meaningless, because if it had meant exchange, the reading and revelation would have been: nor that you exchange them for other wives, or nor that you exchange them with a damma on the ta’, but the agreed-upon reading, nor that you exchange them with a fatha on the ta’, means: nor that you exchange them, even though what Ibn Zayd mentioned of the actions of the Jahiliyyah is not known among any nation that we know of: that a man exchanges his free wife for another, so it is said: that was from their actions, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade doing something like it.

x: God Almighty says to the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O you who believe in God and His Messenger, do not enter the houses of the Prophet of God unless you are invited to food to feed him without waiting for its time meaning: without waiting for it to be reached or fulfilled, and it is a source from their saying: This thing has come, it comes, I, I, I, I, I. Al-Hutay’ah said: I brought the evening meal to Suhayl or Sirius, but the vessel became too long for me. There is another language for it, it is said: It is time for you, meaning it has become clear to you where, and he has attained for you and I will attain for you, and from it is the saying of Ru’bah ibn al-‘Ajaj: A dove like me has become excited and wants to sleep, a dove that has cooed And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, to food, not awaiting its preparation, he said: waiting for it to be cooked.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: not waiting for its preparation meaning: not waiting for the food to be prepared.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: not looking at his food, he said: not waiting for his food.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same. The accusative of ghair in his statement ghairin nazarinu is in the state of the kaf and meem in his statement except if permission is given to you because the kaf and meem are definite and ghair is indefinite, and it is from the description of the kaf and meem.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: It is not permissible for ghair to be in the genitive case with food, unless you say you", and he used to say: "Don't you see that if you said: Abdullah Ali showed a woman he hated her, then there would be nothing in it except the accusative case, unless you say he hated her, because if you made his description apply to it, and did not make clear the pronoun that indicates that the description belongs to him, then it would not be a statement. If you said: This is a man with a woman who is constantly with her, it would be a mistake, so you raise it, then say her constant, or you say her constant is he, then you make it in the genitive case.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: If you had made ghair in his saying ghairin nadhirinah a genitive, it would have been correct, because before it was the food, which is indefinite, so their action would have been made dependent on the food, because the mention of the food returned to its genitive, just as the Arabs say: I saw Zayd with a woman, treating her well and treating her well. So whoever said treating her well made it an attribute of Zayd, and whoever lowered it, it was as if he said: I saw him with the one to whom he treated well. So if the relative clause became indefinite, it would follow it even if it was a verb for a non-indefinite, just as al-A’sha said: I said to him: Bring this to us with the blood of her being led. So he made the led follow the i'rab of with blood because it is like your saying: with blood you lead it, so he lowered it because it is a conjunction to it.
He said: And it is recited: with blood you lead it with the blood lowered because it is added to the led. He said: And its meaning is: Bring it to me by the hand of the one who led it.
And if a matter is presented while there is a land barren and deserted, then it will be destroyed.

You have the right to respond to his voice and know that the meaning is successful It was narrated that some Arabs heard him chant: Have you seen that I gave you all my love, but I had no refusal if you refused? You surrendered to death, so you will die. Do the souls of those who surrender have any survival? Surat al-Ahzab 33:53 O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are given permission for a meal, without awaiting its preparation.
h
But when you are invited

, enter, and when you have eaten, disperse, and do not seek to listen to conversation. Indeed, that used to annoy the Prophet, and he would be shy of you. And God is not shy of the truth. And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a partition.
h
That is purer for your hearts and their hearts
h
And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God or to marry his wives after him
, ever. Indeed, that would be in the sight of God an enormity.

He did not say: Then I will die. Al-Kisa’i said: I heard the Arabs say: Your hand is extended, meaning you. This is common in speech. He said: Based on this, it is permissible to put ghair in the genitive case. The correct statement regarding this, in our view, is to permit the genitive case of ghair in nazireen in speech, not in recitation, based on what we mentioned from the verses that we narrated. As for recitation, it is not permissible for ghair except in the accusative case, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on putting it in the accusative case. And his statement,
h
But if you are invited

, then enter, means: But if the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, invites you, then enter the house which he has given you permission to enter. And when you have eaten, then disperse, means: When you have eaten the food which you have been invited to eat, then disperse, meaning, then disperse and leave his house.

Nor seeking comfort in conversation. So his statement, Nor seeking comfort in conversation is in the accusative case in apposition to watching, as is said in speech: You are neither silent nor speaking. It may be possible to say: Watching is in the accusative case in apposition to the meaning of watching, because its meaning is: Unless you are given permission to eat food, not looking at its preparation. So his statement, Nor seeking comfort is in the accusative case. The Arabs do that when they alternate between the first and the second, so they sometimes use the wording of the first, and sometimes its meaning. Al-Farra’ mentioned that Abu al-Qamqam recited to him: I find you are not a visionary of time, nor a wise person except that you are a sane person There is no elevator in the two elevators to turn you up or down, as long as I live on Shatib Hill An elevator is a single word that has a lowering ba in it, because the same thing that came between it and the elevator came between them in speech.
The meaning of his saying, nor to entertain one another with conversation is: nor to talk after you have finished eating, so that you may be entertained by it.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, nor seeking comfort in speech after you eat. Scholars differed about the reason for the revelation of this verse.

x: Some of them said: It was revealed because of some people who ate at the feast of Zaynab bint Jahsh, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then they sat talking in the house of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a need for his family, so shyness prevented him from ordering them to leave his house.
Who said that?

c: Imran bin Musa al-Qazzaz told me: Abdul-Warith told us: Abdul-Aziz bin Suhaib told us, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married Zaynab bint Jahsh. I sent someone to invite people to food, and I invited people to come, eat, and leave. Then the people would come, eat, and leave. I said: O Prophet of God, I have invited people until I find no one to invite. He said: Take away your food. Zaynab was sitting in a corner of the house, and she had been given camels. Three people remained talking in the house. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out towards Aisha’s room and said: Peace be upon you, people of the house. They said: And upon you be peace, O Messenger of God. How did you find your family? He said: So he went to the room of his wives, and they said the same as Aisha had said. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned, and there were three people talking in the house. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was very shy. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out towards Aisha’s room.

c: I do not know whether I told him,
m: or whether he told that the group…” They went out, so he returned until he placed his foot on a threshold inside the house, and the other outside, when he lowered the curtain between me and him, and the verse of the veil was revealed.
b.via: I do not know whether I

c: Abu Muawiyah Bishr bin Dihya told me: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said:
m: Ubayy bin Ka’b asked me about the veil, so I said: I am the most knowledgeable person about it. It was revealed concerning Zaynab, or the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, served her dates and barley gruel, so the verse was revealed: O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are permitted until His saying:
h
That is purer for your hearts and their hearts

c: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb told me: My paternal uncle told me: Yunus told me, on the authority of al-Zuhri: Anas ibn Malik told me that
m: he was ten years old when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) arrived in Medina. I was the most knowledgeable of people about the veil when it was revealed in the house of the Messenger of God with Zaynab bint Jahsh. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) became her bride. He called the people and they ate food until they left.

x: Some of them remained with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and they stayed for a long time. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) got up and went out, and I went out with him so that they would go out. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) walked and I walked with him until he came to the threshold of the room of Aisha, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) thought that they had gone out, so he went back and I went back with him until he entered upon Zaynab. They were sitting and had not gotten up. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went back and I went back with him. They had gone out. He put up a curtain between me and him and revealed the veil.
Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated:

c: Ibn Abi Uday narrated to us, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Anas, who said:
m: I invited the Muslims to the wedding feast of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the morning of his marriage to Zaynab bint Jahsh. He gave them a generous portion of bread and meat, then he returned as he usually did. He went to the room of his wives and greeted them, so they invited him. He returned to his house and I was with him. When we reached the door, there were two men talking in a corner of the house. When he saw them, he turned back. When they saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he turned away from his house and quickly turned away.

c: I do not know whether I told him, or he told me.
m: He returned to his house and lowered the curtain between me and him, and the verse of the veil was revealed.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: Umar bin Al-Khattab said:
m: “I said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you were to veil yourself from the Mothers of the Believers, then both the righteous and the wicked would enter upon you. So the verse of veiling was revealed.”

c: Al-Qasim bin Bishr bin Maruf told me: Sulayman bin Harb told us: Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said:
m: I am the most knowledgeable of people about this verse, the verse of hijab. (When Zaynab was presented to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he made food and invited the people. They came and entered, and Zaynab was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the house. They began to talk, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out and came back in while they were sitting. He said: Then this verse was revealed: O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet ... to Ask them from behind a partition. He said: So the people stood up and the partition was drawn.

c: Umar ibn Ismail ibn Mujalid told me: My father told us, on the authority of Bayan, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married one of his wives. He sent me to invite some people to eat. When they had eaten and left, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and went towards Aisha’s house. He saw two men sitting there, so he turned back. Then God revealed: O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are given permission.

c: Amr ibn Ali told us: Abu Dawud told us: Al-Mas’udi told us: Ibn Nahshal told us, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: Umar ordered the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to wear the veil. Zainab said: O Ibn al-Khattab, you are jealous of us, yet the revelation is being sent down to our homes! So God revealed: And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a partition.

c: Muhammad ibn Marzuq told me: Ashhal ibn Hatim told us: Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Saʿid, on the authority of Anas, who said:
m: “I was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was passing by his wives. He said: A bride was brought to him, then he came back and some people were with her. He went and relieved himself, and he stayed and came back and they had left. He said: Then he entered and there was a curtain between me and him. He said: So I told Abu Talha, and he said: If it is as you say, something will be revealed about this. He said: And the verse of the veil was revealed.”

x: Others said: It was in Umm Salamah’s house.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Thanayzid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, “
h
But when you are invited

, then enter. And when you have eaten, disperse and do not seek entertainment in conversation.” He said: This was in the house of Umm Salamah. He said: They ate, then they prolonged the conversation, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept entering and exiting and feeling shy of them, but God is not shy of the truth. He said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada: And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a partition. He said: We were informed that they were commanded to wear the veil at that time. And his saying,
h
That was hurting the Prophet

. He says: Your entering the houses of the Prophet without permission and your sitting in them, enjoying conversation after you have finished eating the food to which you were invited, would annoy the Prophet, so he would be too shy to expel you from them if you sat in them to talk after finishing the meal, or he would prevent you from entering if you entered without permission, even though he disliked that from you. And God is not shy of the truth to make it clear to you, and if your Prophet was shy, he did not explain to you his dislike of that out of shyness from you. And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a partition means: And when you ask the wives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believing women who are not your Surat al-Ahzab 33:53 O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are given permission for a meal, without awaiting its preparation.
h
But when you are invited

, enter, and when you have eaten, disperse, and do not seek to listen to conversation. Indeed, that used to annoy the Prophet, and he would be shy of you. And God is not shy of the truth. And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a partition.
h
That is purer for your hearts and their hearts
h
And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God or to marry his wives after him
, ever. Indeed, that would be in the sight of God an enormity. wives for something, ask them from behind a partition means: From behind a screen between you and them, and do not enter their houses.
h
That is purer for your hearts and their hearts

means: God Almighty says: Your asking them for something if you ask them for it from behind a partition is purer for your hearts and their hearts from the evil eye that appears in the hearts of men regarding women, and in the hearts of women regarding men. It is more likely that Satan will not have a way to you or them. It has been said that the reason God commanded women to wear the hijab was because a man was eating with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Aisha was with them, and her hand touched the man’s hand, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disliked that.

x: Who said that?

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was eating with some of his companions, and the hand of one of them touched the hand of Aisha, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disliked that, so the verse of hijab was revealed.” It was said: It was revealed regarding the issue of the age of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb and Yaqub told us: Hisham told us: Hamid al-Tawil told us, on the authority of Anas, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said:
m: “I said: O Messenger of God, your women are visited by both righteous and wicked men, so why don’t you order them to cover themselves? He said: Then the verse of hijab was revealed.”

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Hamid told us, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman told me: Amr ibn Abd God ibn Wahb told me: Yunus told me, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aishah, who said:
m: “The wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to go out at night when they wanted to defecate to the open plains, which were hot ground. Umar used to say: ‘O Messenger of God, veil your women,’ but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not do so. Then Sawdah bint Zam’ah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out, and she was a tall woman, and Umar called out to her in his loudest voice: ‘We recognize you, O Sawdah,’ out of eagerness for the veil to be revealed. So God revealed the veil.” Ibn Wakee’ narrated: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, who said: “Sawda went out to relieve herself after the veil had been imposed on us. She was a woman who used to make women look tall. Umar saw her and called out to her: ‘O Sawda, by God, you are not hidden from us. Look how you go out, or what you do.’ So she turned back and returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was eating dinner. She told him what had happened and what he had said to her, and there was a vein in his hand. Then a revelation was revealed to him and he was lifted from him, and the vein was still in his hand. He said: ‘You have been given permission to go out to relieve your needs.’”

c: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi told me: Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith told us: Hammam told us: Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib told us, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said:
m: “Umar ordered the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to wear the veil. Zaynab said: O son of al-Khattab, are you jealous of us while the revelation is being sent down to our homes? So God revealed: ‘And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a partition.’”

c: Abu Ayyub al-Nahrani Sulayman ibn Abd al-Hamid told me: Yazid ibn Abd Rabbah told us: Ibn Harb told us, on the authority of al-Zubaidi, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha,
m: “The wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would go out at night when they wanted to defecate to the open plains, which were hot ground. Umar ibn al-Khattab would say to the Messenger of God, ‘Veiling your women,’ but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not do so. One night, Sawdah bint Zam’ah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out at night in the evening. She was a tall woman, and Umar called out to her in his loudest voice, ‘We recognize you, O Sawdah,’ out of eagerness for the veil to be revealed. Aisha said: So God revealed the veil, and God said, ‘O you who have believed, do not enter…’… the verse.” And His statement,
h
And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God

, God Almighty says: And it is not appropriate for you to harm the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that is not appropriate for you. And it is not appropriate for you to marry his wives after him ever, He says: And it is not appropriate for you to marry his wives after him ever because they are your mothers, and it is not permissible for a man to marry his mother. It was mentioned that this was revealed about a man who used to enter before the veil was introduced. He said: If Muhammad dies, I will marry one of his wives, and he named her. So God Almighty revealed about this:
h
And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God or to marry his wives after him
, ever.

x: Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement, “
h
And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God or to marry his wives after him

, ever. Indeed, that would be in the sight of God an enormity,” he said: Sometimes the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would hear that a man would say, “If the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, were to die, I would marry so-and-so after him.” He said: That would harm the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the Qur’an was revealed,
h
And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God

… the verse. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated: Abd al-Wahhab narrated: Dawud narrated on the authority of Amir that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, died and he had married Qaylah bint al-Ash'ath. After that, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl married her, which caused great hardship for Abu Bakr. Umar said to him: O Caliph of the Messenger of God, she is not one of his wives. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not give her a choice or veil her, and he declared her innocent of him because of her apostasy with her people. Abu Bakr was reassured and calmed down.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-A’la told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer,
m: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died while he had married the daughter of Al-Ash’ath bin Qais, but he had not had intercourse with her, and he mentioned something similar. His statement, Indeed, that was a great sin in the sight of God, means that your harming the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and your marrying his wives after him is a great sin in the sight of God.

evidence.text: He said: And it is recited: with blood you lead it with the blood lowered because it is added to the led.
As for recitation, it is not permissible for ghair except in the accusative case, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on putting it in the accusative case.

x: God Almighty says: If you reveal with your tongues anything, O people, of watching women, or other things that he forbade you from, or of harming the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by saying: I will marry his wife after his death, or you conceal it - meaning: or you conceal it in yourselves, then God is All-Knowing of all things, meaning: God is All-Knowing of all of that and other things of your affairs and the affairs of others, and nothing is hidden from Him, and He will reward you for all of that.

God Almighty says: There is no blame upon the wives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their signs nor is there any sin. Then the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of what was removed from them in these cases.
Some of them said: The responsibility was removed from them in removing their cloaks in their presence.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Abdul Karim, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers
... the entire verse, he said: that she removes the jilbab.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God,
h
There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers
and those mentioned with him, that they see them.

x: Others said: He removed the blame from them for not covering themselves.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
There is no blame upon them

... to witnesses: He gave them permission not to veil themselves from them. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of those who said: That is to remove the blame from them in the case of these women who are not veiled from them, and that is because this verse follows the verse on the veil, and after the statement of God, And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a partition. So it is more appropriate and more appropriate for His statement,
h
There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers

, to be an exception from the group of those who were commanded to ask them for something from behind a partition if they asked them for it than it being the report of a subject with a meaning other than that. So the interpretation of this statement is: There is no sin on the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the mothers of the believers, in their permission for their fathers, and leaving the veil in front of them, nor for their sons, nor for their brothers, nor for the sons of their brothers. What is meant by their brothers and their brothers’ sons is their brothers and their brothers’ sons. And the plural of that is used with them in the same way as the plural of a young man when it is used in the plural of young men, and likewise the plural of brother when it is used in the plural of brothers. But when it is used in the plural of brothers, that is similar to the plural of a young man when it is used in the plural of young men, nor the sons of their brothers. And the paternal uncle was not mentioned in that, as Al-Sha’bi said, in order to avoid describing them to his sons. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated: Hajjaj ibn al-Munhal narrated: Hammad narrated: Dawud narrated: al-Sha'bi and Ikrimah, regarding the statement of God,
h
There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers

or their sons or their brothers or their brothers' sons or their sisters' sons or their women or those their right hands possess. I said, Why are the paternal uncle and maternal uncle not mentioned? He said, Because they describe her to their sons, and they disliked that she remove her veil in front of her maternal uncle and paternal uncle.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abu Al-Walid told us, he said: Hammad told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Sha’bi,
m: something similar, except that he did not mention how they describe it. And his saying, nor their women, means: There is no blame on them either if they do not veil themselves from the women of the believers.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, nor their women, he said: The free believing women, there is no blame for them to see that adornment. He said: All of this is about adornment. He said: It is not permissible for a woman to look at any of a woman’s private parts. He said: If a man were to look at a man’s thigh, I would not see anything wrong with it. He said: nor those their right hands possess, so it is not appropriate for a woman to uncover her earrings in front of a man. He said: As for kohl, a ring, and dyeing, there is nothing wrong with them. He said: The husband has preference, and the fathers after the man have preference. He said: And others are distinguished. He said: All of this is included in what appears of adornment. He said: The wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did not veil themselves from their slaves. His statement, nor those their right hands possess, of men and women.

x: Others said: of women. And His statement,
h
And fear God
, means:
h
And fear God

, O women, lest you transgress what God has set for you, and show of your adornment what you should not show, or abandon the hijab that God has commanded you to adhere to, except in what He has permitted you to leave, and the time is to obey Him. Indeed, God is ever, over all things, Witness, meaning, the Most High says: Indeed, God is a witness to what you do of your covering, and your leaving the hijab for whomever He has permitted you to leave that for, and other matters of yours. He says: So fear God in yourselves, lest you meet God while He is a witness over you with His disobedience, and opposition to His commands and prohibitions, and thus you perish, for He is a witness over all things.
God Almighty says: God and His angels bless the Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the statement of God, “Indeed, God and His angels send blessings on the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings on him,” meaning: They bless the Prophet. It could also be said that the meaning of this is that God has mercy on the Prophet, and His angels pray for him and seek forgiveness. This is because in the speech of the Arabs, praying for someone other than God is nothing but supplication. We have already explained this in the previous part of this book with its supporting evidence, so there is no need to repeat it. O you who have believed, pray upon him. God Almighty says: O you who have believed, pray for the Prophet of God Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And salute him with a worthy salutation. He says: And greet him with the greeting of Islam. In a similar manner to what we have said, there are reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Who said that? Ibn Humayd narrated: Harun narrated to us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Uthman ibn Wahb, on the authority of Musa ibn Talhah, on the authority of his father, who said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: I heard God say, ‘Indeed, God and His angels send blessings on the Prophet’... the verse. So how do we send blessings on you? He said: Say, ‘O God, send blessings on Muhammad and on the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings on Abraham. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious. And bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Abraham. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious.’”

c: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Kufi told me: Ya'la ibn al-Ajlah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, on the authority of Ka'b ibn Ujrah, who said:
m: When the verse, "Indeed, God and His angels send blessings on the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings on him and salute him with a worthy salutation," was revealed, I went to him and said: Peace be upon you, we know it, but how should we send blessings upon you, O Messenger of God? He said: Say: O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Abraham and the family of Abraham. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious. And bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Ismail narrated to us, saying: Abu Isra’il narrated to us, on the authority of Yunus ibn Khabbab, who said:
m: “He delivered a sermon to us in Persia and said: ‘Indeed, God and His angels…’ the verse. He said: Someone who heard Ibn Abbas say: ‘It was revealed thus.’ We said, or they said: ‘O Messenger of God, we have learned how to greet you, but how do we pray for you?’ He said: ‘O God, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious. And bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Abraham. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious.’”

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ziyad, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding His statement, Indeed, God and His angels… the verse, they said: O Messenger of God, we know this greeting, but how do we pray for you? He said: “Say: O God, bless Muhammad, Your servant and Messenger, and his family, as You blessed Abraham, for You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious.”

c: Yaqub al-Dawraqi told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Ayoub told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr ibn Masʿud al-Ansari, who said:
m: “When the verse, ‘Indeed, God and His angels send blessings on the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings on him and salute him with a worthy salutation,’ was revealed, they said: ‘O Messenger of God, we know this greeting, but how should we pray, since God has forgiven you your past and future sins?’ He said: ‘Say: O God, send blessings on Muhammad as You sent blessings on the family of Abraham. O God, bless Muhammad as You blessed the family of Abraham.’”
b.via: Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr ibn Masʿud al-Ansari

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, “Indeed, God and His angels send blessings on the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings on him and salute him with a worthy salutation.” He said: “When this verse was revealed, they said: O Messenger of God, we have learned how to greet you, but how do we send blessings on you? He said: Say: O God, send blessings on Muhammad as You sent blessings on Abraham, and bless Muhammad as You blessed Abraham. Al-Hasan said: O God, place Your blessings and blessings on the family of Muhammad as You placed them on Abraham. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy and Glorious.”

x: What is meant by the Almighty's statement, Indeed, those who harm God is that they harm their Lord by disobeying Him and committing what He has forbidden them. It has been said that what is meant by this are the image-makers, because they seek to create a creation like that of God.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad Al-Qurashi told me: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: Those who harm God and His Messenger are the people who make images.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding the statement of God, Indeed, those who abuse God and His Messenger - God has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment, he said: Glory be to God, there have been ignorant people among the children of Adam who have begun to abuse their Lord. As for their abuse of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, it is their slander of him for marrying Safiyyah bint Huyayy, as mentioned.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement, Indeed, those who abuse God and His Messenger - God has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment, he said: It was revealed regarding those who slandered the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he took Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab as his wife. And His saying,
h
May God curse them in this world and the Hereafter

, means that God Almighty says: God has distanced them from His mercy in this world and the Hereafter and has prepared for them in the Hereafter a punishment in which He will humiliate them by making them dwell in it forever.

x: And his saying, And those who harm the believers, Mujahid was directing the meaning of his saying, harm, to they stop.
He mentioned the narration about him:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And those who annoy he said: They stop. The meaning of the statement, according to what Mujahid said: And those who stand up to the believing men and women and criticize them, seeking to disgrace them, ‘for something other than what they have earned,’ means: for something other than what they have done.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, without what they have earned, he said: what they have done.

c: Nasr bin Ali told us: Othman bin Ali told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Ibn Umar recited: And those who harm believing men and women for [something] other than what they have earned have certainly borne upon themselves a slander and a manifest sin. He said: So how about if he is harmed for a good reason, for that is when the punishment is doubled for him?

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Uthman bin Ali told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Thawr, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: And those who harm believing men and women for no reason, he said: How about the one who does them good?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And those who harm believing men and believing women for [something] other than what they have earned have certainly borne upon themselves a slander and a manifest sin. So beware of harming a believer, for God will protect him and become angry on his behalf. His statement, They have borne the burden of slander and a manifest sin, means: they have borne falsehood, a lie, and a heinous slander. Slander is the most heinous lie. And a manifest sin, means: a sin that makes it clear to its listener that it is a sin and a falsehood.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers: Do not resemble the slave girls in their dress when they go out of their homes for their needs, uncovering their hair and faces, but let them draw their outer garments over themselves, lest an evildoer, if he knows that they are free, expose them to harmful speech. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the description of the approach that God commanded them to do.
Some of them said: It is that they cover their faces and heads, so that only one eye is visible.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, O Prophet,
h
tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments
. God commanded the women of the believers, when they went out of their homes for some need, to cover their faces from above their heads with their outer garments, and to show one eye.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Ubaydah,
m: regarding his statement, O Prophet,
h
tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments

. So Ibn Awn wore it with us, he said: And Muhammad wore it with us, Muhammad said: And Ubaydah wore it with me, Ibn Awn said: With his cloak, so he covered his nose and his left eye, and exposed his right eye, and he lowered his cloak from above until it was close to his eyebrow or over the eyebrow.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, he said:
m: I asked Ubaidah, about his statement:
h
Tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments
. He said: So he said with his garment, so he covered his head and face, and exposed his garment from one of his eyes.

x: Others said: Rather, they were ordered to tighten their robes over their foreheads.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, O Prophet,
h
tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments
... to His statement,
h
And God is Forgiving and Merciful

. He said: The free woman used to wear the clothing of the slave woman, so God commanded the women of the believers to bring down their outer garments, and bringing down the outer garment means that it covers and tightens it over the forehead.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers, God took a covenant from them when they went out that they should cover their eyebrows. That is more suitable that they will be known and not be abused. And if a female slave passed by, they would abuse her, so God forbade free women from imitating the female slaves.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, and to draw their veils over their bosoms means that they cover themselves so that it is known that they are free women, and no immoral person will harm them by word or suspicion.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Abu Salih, who said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina without a home. When night fell, the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and others would go out to take care of their needs, and some men would sit on the road spinning. Then God revealed: ‘O Prophet,
h
tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments
