. ’ They would cover themselves with the outer garment so that the slave woman would be distinguished from the free woman.” And His statement, That is more likely that they will be known and not be harmed, God Almighty says: Their drawing their outer garments close over themselves is more likely and more likely that they will be recognized by those they pass by, and they will know that they are not slaves, so they will refrain from harming them with unpleasant words or suspicious expressions. And God is Forgiving for what they did in the past of not drawing their outer garments close over themselves, Merciful to them, that He does not punish them after their repentance by drawing their outer garments close over themselves.

x: God Almighty says: If the hypocrites, who conceal their disbelief and show faith, and those in whose hearts is disease do not cease, meaning: suspicion of the desire for adultery and the love of immorality. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr bin Ali told me, he said: Abu Abd al-Samad told us, he said: Malik bin Dinar told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement,
h
If the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease do not desist
, he said: They are the adulterers.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And those in whose hearts is disease, he said: The desire for adultery. He said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, he said:

c: Abu Salih al-Tammar told us, he said:
m: I heard Ikrimah regarding his statement,
h
In their hearts is disease
, he said: The desire for adultery.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Abu Salih:
m: And those in whose hearts is disease, he said: the adulterers.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
If the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease do not cease… the verse

, he said: These are a category of hypocrites. And those in whose hearts is disease are the people of adultery. He said: The people of adultery are among the hypocrites who seek women and desire adultery. And he recited, So do not speak in a soft voice, lest he in whose heart is disease should covet (al-Ahzab 33:32). He said: The hypocrites are ten categories in Bara’ah. He said: Those in whose hearts is disease, one category of them has a disease related to women. His saying,
h
And the slanderers in the city
, means:
h
And the slanderers in the city
with lies and falsehood. Their rumours were as follows:

c: Bishr told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement,
h
If the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease and the agitators in the city do not cease… the verse

. The agitator is the lie that the hypocrites spread, and they used to say: A great number has come to you. And it was mentioned to us that the hypocrites wanted to reveal the hypocrisy in their hearts, so God threatened them with this verse, His statement,
h
If the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease do not cease… the verse
. So when God threatened them with this verse, they concealed it and kept it secret.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, and the slanderers in Medina, they are also the hypocrites who slander the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers. His saying,
h
We will tempt you with them
, means: We will give you power over them and incite you with them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement: We will tempt you against them means: We will give you power over them.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
We will tempt you with them
: meaning, we will force you to attack them, to incite you with them. His saying,
h
Then they will not live with you therein except for a little while
, means: Then We will banish them from your city, and they will not live with you therein except for a little while, until You banish them from it and expel them from it.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Then they will not be your neighbors therein except for a little while, meaning in Medina.

x: And His statement,
h
Cursed wherever they are found

, they will be seized and killed in a terrible slaughter, God Almighty says: Expelled and banished wherever they are found, meaning: wherever they are found on earth, they will be seized and killed in a terrible slaughter for their disbelief in God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Cursed in every case: Wherever they are found, they will be seized and killed with a slaying if they display hypocrisy. And the word cursed is in the accusative case as an insult. It may also be possible that few is an attribute of the cursed, so his word cursed is rejected as few, and its meaning is: Then none will live with you therein except a few cursed ones who will be killed wherever they are afflicted.

x: God Almighty says,
h
The way of God with those who passed on before

. These hypocrites who were in the city of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with him were of the same type as these hypocrites. If they showed their hypocrisy, he would kill them and curse them greatly. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
The way of God with those who passed on before
... the verse, he says: This is the way of God with them if they show hypocrisy. And His saying,
h
And you will not find any change in the way of God

, the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And you will not find, O Muhammad, any change in the way of God that He established for His creation, so be certain that He will not change His way in these hypocrites.

x: God Almighty says: “People ask you, O Muhammad, about the Hour. When will it come? Say to them: The knowledge of the Hour is only with God. No one knows the time of its coming except Him. “And what makes you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.” He says: What makes you feel, O Muhammad? Perhaps the time of its coming is near. The time of its coming is near, and the time of its arrival is near.

God Almighty says: God has distanced the unbelievers from all good, and has kept them away from it. And He has prepared for them a Blaze. He says: And He has prepared for them in the Hereafter a fire that will burn and blaze so that they may burn in it.

They will abide therein forever meaning: they will remain in the Blaze forever, without end. They will not find a protector to take care of them and rescue them from the Blaze into which God has cast them, nor a helper to aid them and save them from God’s punishment upon them.

God Almighty says: These disbelievers will not find any protector or helper on the Day when their faces will be turned over in the Fire, one state after another. They will say, and this is their state in the Fire, Oh, if only we had obeyed God in this world and obeyed His Messenger in what he brought us of His commands and prohibitions, so that we would be with the people of Paradise in Paradise. What a regret and remorse, how great and sublime it is.

God Almighty says: The disbelievers will say on the Day of Resurrection in Hell: Our Lord, we obeyed our leaders in misguidance and our elders in polytheism, and they led us astray from the path. He says: They led us astray from the path of truth, the path of guidance, faith in You, acknowledgment of Your Oneness, and sincere obedience to You in this world.
Our Lord, give them double the punishment meaning: punish them with a punishment double the punishment with which we were punished. And curse them with
h
a great curse
meaning: and end them with great disgrace. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, Our Lord, indeed we have obeyed our masters and our dignitaries, meaning our leaders in evil and polytheism.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Indeed, we obeyed our masters and our dignitaries, he said: They are the heads of the nations whom they led astray. He said: Our masters and our dignitaries are one. And the majority of the reciters of the regions read our masters. And it was narrated from Al-Hasan Al-Basri, our masters in the plural. And the unification in that is the reading according to us, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it. They differed in the reading of His statement,
h
A great curse
. The majority of the reciters of the regions read it with a tha’ katheer from abundance, except for Asim, who read it as
h
A great curse
from arrogance. The reading of that according to us is with a tha’ due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.

evidence.text: And the majority of the reciters of the regions read our masters.
And the unification in that is the reading according to us, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.
They differed in the reading of His statement, A great curse.
The majority of the reciters of the regions read it with a tha’ katheer from abundance, except for Asim, who read it as A great curse from arrogance.
The reading of that according to us is with a tha’ due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.

x: God Almighty says to the companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O you who believe in God and His Messenger, do not harm the Messenger of God with words that he dislikes from you, nor with actions that he does not like from you, and
h
do not be like those who harmed Moses

, the Prophet of God, by falsely and unjustly accusing him of a defect. So God cleared him of what they said about him of lies and falsehood by what He showed of proof of their lie. And he was held in high esteem with God. He says: Moses was an intercessor with God in what he asked, and he had a position and status with Him because of his obedience to Him. Then the scholars of interpretation differed regarding the harm that befell Moses, as mentioned by God in this passage.
Some of them said: They accused him of being a leper. A report on this was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Mention the narration that was narrated about him, and who said that:

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr and Abdullah bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Do not be like those who harmed Moses

, he said: His people said to him, You are a leper. He said: So one day he went out to wash himself and placed his clothes on a rock, and the rock came out, grabbing his clothes, and he went out following it naked until it reached the gathering of the Children of Israel. He said: They saw that he was not a leper. He said: So that is what His statement means, So God cleared him of what they said.

c: Yahya ibn Dawud al-Wasiti told me: Ishaq ibn Yusuf al-Azraq told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace:
h
Do not be like those who harmed Moses

. He said: “They said: He is a leper. Moses went to wash himself and placed his clothes on a stone. The stone passed by his clothes, so Moses followed him back and said: My clothes are a stone! He passed by a gathering of the Children of Israel and they saw him, so God cleared him of what they had said. “And he was held in high esteem by God.”

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
O you who have believed
h
do not be like those who harmed Moses

… to honorable. He said: Their harm to Moses was that they said: By God, nothing is preventing Moses from placing his clothes with us except that he is urinary. This harmed Moses, and while he was bathing one day and his clothes were on a rock, when Moses had finished washing and went to get his clothes, the rock started running with his clothes, and he started running after it until it passed by the assembly of the Children of Israel while he was looking for it. When they saw Moses, peace be upon him, naked, with no clothes on, they said: By God, we do not see anything wrong with Moses, and he is innocent of what we used to say about him. So God said: So God cleared him of what they said, and he was honorable in the sight of God.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
O you who have believed
h
do not be like those who harmed Moses

... the verse, he said: (Moses was a man who was very careful about his private parts and his clothes. He said: They used to say: What makes him do that is a defect in his private parts that he would hate to be seen. So one day he got up to wash himself in the desert and put his clothes on a rock, and they stuck to his clothes. He said: Then he came looking for it naked, until he looked out at them naked, and they saw that he was innocent of what they said, and he was honorable in the sight of God.) He said: Honorable in the speech of the Arabs: the beloved and accepted.

x: Others said: Rather, they described him as a leper.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told me: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid, who said: The Children of Israel said:
m: Moses was leprous, and a group said: He was a leper because of the severity of his concealment. He used to go to a spring every day, wash himself, and place his clothes on a rock near it. The rock carried his clothes until it reached the assembly of the Children of Israel. Moses came looking for them, and when they saw him naked, with nothing of what they had said about him, he put on his clothes and then went to the rock and struck it with his staff, and the staff left an impression on the rock.

c: Bahr ibn Habib ibn Arabi narrated to us, saying: Ruh ibn Ubadah narrated to us, saying: Auf narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah,
m: regarding this verse:
h
Do not be like those who harmed Moses

, but God cleared him of what they said… the verse. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Moses was a modest, discreet man. Hardly anything of his skin could be seen out of shyness. Those of the Children of Israel who harmed him harmed him and said: He only covered himself this way because of a defect in his skin, either leprosy, or a disease, or some other affliction. God wanted to clear him of what they said. One day, Moses was alone, and he placed his clothes on a stone, then washed himself. When he finished washing, he went to take his clothes, but the stone ran after his clothes. Moses took a staff and asked the stone, saying: My clothes are a stone, until he reached a group of the Children of Israel. They saw him naked, like the best of people in character, and God cleared him of what they said. The stone stood up and took his clothes.” He put it on and started hitting the stone with it. By God, there were scars on the stone from the marks of hitting it three, four, or five times.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: It reached me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Moses was a modest and discreet man, then he mentioned something similar.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Al-Hasan told us, on the authority of Abu Hurairah,
m: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Children of Israel used to bathe while they were naked, and the Prophet of God, Moses, was modest, so he used to cover himself when he bathed. Then they stabbed him in the private parts. He said: While the Prophet of God was bathing one day, he placed his clothes on a rock. The rock moved and the Prophet of God followed it, striking it with his staff, ‘My clothes, O rock!’ until it reached a group of the Children of Israel, or was in the middle of them. Then it stood up. The Prophet of God took his clothes and they saw the best of character and the most honorable of men. The group said: ‘May God kill the slanderer of the Children of Israel.’ So his innocence was proven, and God cleared him of it.”

x: Others said: Rather, their harm to him was their claim that he killed his brother Aaron.
Who said that?

c: Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi told me: Ibad told us: Sufyan ibn Habib told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib,
m: may God be pleased with him, regarding the statement of God,
h
Do not be like those who harmed Moses

… the verse, he said: Moses and Aaron went up the mountain, and Aaron died. The Children of Israel said: You killed him, and he loved us more than you did, and was kinder to us than you, so they harmed him because of that. Then God commanded the angels to carry him until they passed by the Children of Israel, and the angels spoke of his death, until the Children of Israel knew that he had died. Then God cleared him of that and they went and buried him. No one from God’s creation saw his grave except the marble, so God made him deaf and mute. The most correct of the sayings in this regard is to say: The Children of Israel harmed the Prophet of God in some ways that he would not have liked to be harmed with, so God absolved him of what they had harmed him with. It is possible that this was because they said that he was a leper. It is possible that this was because they claimed that he had killed his brother Aaron. It is possible that all of this was the case, because he mentioned all of that with which they harmed him. No statement in this regard is more true than what God said that they harmed Moses, so God absolved him of what they had said.

x: God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, fear God lest you disobey Him, lest you deserve His punishment. His saying, And say a sound word, means: Say a clear, impermissible, and true word about the Messenger of God and the believers.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: And speak a just word, meaning: a sound one.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Anbasa told us, on the authority of Al-Kalbi,
m: And speak a just word, he said: Truthfully.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, Fear God and speak words of appropriate justice, meaning just. Qatada said: He means by that in his speech and in all of his actions, and appropriate is truthfulness.

c: Saad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me: Hafs bin Omar told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding the statement of God, And say a word of appropriate justice, say: There is no god but God.

x: And His statement, He will rectify for you your deeds, meaning that the Almighty says to the believers: Fear God and say the right words, and He will guide you to righteous deeds, so He will rectify your deeds. And forgive you your sins, meaning: He will pardon you for your sins, so He will not punish you for them. And whoever obeys God and His Messenger, by doing what He commands him to do, and refraining from what He forbids, and saying the right, has certainly achieved a great victory, meaning: He has attained the greatest honor from God.
The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of that.

Some of them said: Its meaning is that God offered His obedience and His obligations to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains on the condition that if they did well, they would be rewarded and compensated, and if they neglected, they would be punished. But their patience refused, fearing that they would not fulfill their duty, and Adam made them bear it. He was unjust to himself, ignorant of what was in his favor.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding His statement, Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they declined to bear it and feared it. He said: The Trust: the obligations that God has imposed on the servants. He said: Hisham narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Awam, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they declined to bear it, he said: The Trust: the obligations that God has imposed on His servants. He said: Hisham narrated to us, he said:

c: Al-Awam bin Hawshab and Juwaybir informed us,
m: both on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Indeed, We offered the Trust ... to His statement, to ignorant people. He said: The Trust means the obligatory duties. Juwaybir said in his hadith: When it was presented to Adam, he said, O Lord, what is the Trust? He said, It was said, ‘If you fulfill it, you will be rewarded, and if you neglect it, you will be punished.’ He said, “O Lord, you carried it with what was in it. He said, So he did not remain in Paradise except for the amount of time between the afternoon prayer and sunset, until he committed a sin and was expelled from it.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saʿid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said
m: regarding this verse, Indeed, We offered the Trust, that it was offered to Adam, and he said: Take it for what it contains. If you obey, I will forgive you, and if you disobey, I will punish you. He said: I have accepted. And there was only an amount of time between the afternoon and nightfall of that day until he committed the sin.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement, Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, “If they fulfilled it, He would reward them, and if they neglected it, He would punish them.” They disliked that and were afraid, not because of disobedience, but out of respect for the religion of God, that they would not fulfill it. Then He offered it to Adam, and he accepted it with what was in it, which is His statement, “
h
And man bore it
. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant,” deceived by the command of God.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement, Indeed, We offered the Trust: obedience. He offered it to them before He offered it to Adam, but they could not bear it. So He said to Adam, “O Adam, I have offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they did not accept it. Will you take it? What is in it?” He said, O Lord, what is in it? He said, If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do wrong, you will be punished. So Adam took it and bore it, and that is what He said, “
h
And man bore it
. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.”

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak Ibn Muzahim,
m: regarding the statement of God, “Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they declined to bear it and feared it; but man bore it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.” Adam said: It was said to him: Take it with its due right. He said: What is its due right? It was said: If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do wrong, you will be punished. So, it was not long between the noon and the afternoon prayers until he was taken out of it.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding the verse: “Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they could not bear it. So, will you, O Adam, take what is in it?” Adam said: And what is in it, O Lord? He said: If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do evil, you will be punished. He said: I have taken it upon myself. God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: I have taken it upon myself. Adam did not remain there except for the time between the first and the afternoon prayers until Iblis, may God curse him, expelled him from Paradise. Trust means obedience.

c: Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told me: Baqiyah told us: Isa bin Ibrahim told me, on the authority of Musa bin Abi Habib, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Amr,
m: who was one of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Trustworthiness and loyalty were sent down to the son of Adam with the prophets, so they were sent with him, and among them was a Messenger of God, and among them was a Prophet, and among them was a Prophet who was a Messenger. The Qur’an was sent down, and it is the speech of God, and Arabic and non-Arabic were sent down, so they learned the matter of the Qur’an and learned the matter of the Sunnah in their tongues. God did not leave anything of His command, of what they do and what they avoid, which are the proofs against them, except that He made it clear to them. There are no people of a language except that they know the good from the bad. Then trustworthiness is the first thing to be removed, and its effect remains in the roots of people’s hearts. Then loyalty, covenants, and pledges are removed, and the books remain. There is a scholar who works and an ignorant person who knows them and denies them, until it reached me and my nation. No one perishes in the sight of God except one who perishes, and no one neglects Him except one who abandons Him. Beware, O people, and beware of the sneaking whisperer, for He tests you to see which of you is best in deeds.

c: Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani told me: Ubayd God ibn Abd al-Majid al-Hanafi told us: al-Awam al-Attar told us: Qatada and Abaan ibn Abi Ayyash told us, on the authority of Khalid al-Asri, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are five things, whoever does them on the Day of Resurrection with faith will enter Paradise: one who maintains the five daily prayers, with their ablutions, bowing, prostration, and timings; one who gives zakat from his wealth willingly - and he used to say: By God, no one does that except a believer - and one who fasts Ramadan; one who performs the Hajj if he is able to do so; and one who fulfills a trust.” They said: O Abu al-Darda’, what is a trust? He said: Ghusl from major ritual impurity, for God does not trust the son of Adam with regard to any aspect of his religion except that.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, who said:
m: It is part of trustworthiness that a woman is entrusted with her private parts.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they declined to bear it and feared it, he said: God offered them the Trust, that He would impose upon them the religion, and make for them a reward and a punishment, and entrust them with the religion, but they said: No, we are subject to your command, we do not want reward or punishment. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “And God offered it to Adam and said: Between my ear and my shoulder,” Ibn Zayd said, so God said to him: “As you bear this, I will help you. I will make a veil for your sight, so if you fear that you will see except what is not lawful for you, then lower its veil. I will make a door and a lock for your tongue, so if you fear, then close it. I will make a garment for your private parts, so do not uncover them except for what is lawful for you.”

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, meaning: the religion, the obligations, and the prescribed punishments. And they declined to bear it and feared it. It was said to them, Bear it and fulfill its due right. They said, We are not able to do that. “
h
And man bore it

. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.” It was said to him, Will you bear it? He said, Yes. It was said, Will you fulfill its due right? He said, Yes. God said, Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant of its due.

x: Others said: Rather, what is meant by trust in this context is: people’s trusts.
Who said that?
Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated:

c: Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Mas’ud, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Being killed in the cause of God expiates all sins, or he said: It expiates everything except trust. The possessor of the trust will be brought and it will be said to him: ‘Return your trust.’ He will say: ‘O Lord, the world has passed away,’ three times. Then it will be said: ‘Take him to the abyss.’ So he will be taken there and he will fall into it until he reaches its bottom, and he will find it there as it was. He will carry it and place it on his shoulders and ascend with it to the edge of Hell. When he sees that he has emerged, it will slip and he will fall in its wake forever and ever. They said: ‘Trustworthiness is in prayer, trustworthiness is in fasting, trustworthiness is in speech, and the worst of that is deposits.’ So I met al-Baraa’ and said: ‘Do you not listen to what your brother Abdullah is saying?’ He said: ‘He has spoken the truth.’” Sharik said, and Thani Ayash Al-Amiri said, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar, but he did not mention trustworthiness in prayer, or in everything.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Abu Hazim, he said:
m: “God offered the Trust to the lowest heaven, but it refused. Then to the one next to it, until He finished with it. Then to the earths, then to the mountains. Then Surat al-Ahzab 33:72 Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they declined to bear it and feared it; but man bore it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant. He offered it to Adam and said: ‘Yes, between my ears and my shoulders.’ So I command you to do three things, for they will help you: I have made for you a tongue between two jaws, so restrain it from everything I have forbidden you. I have made for you a private part and covered it, so do not uncover it to do what I have forbidden you.”

x: Others said: Rather, what is meant by it is Adam’s trust in his son Cain over his family and children, and Cain’s betrayal of his father by killing his brother.
Who said that?

c: Musa bin Harun told me: Amr bin Hammad told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi in a report he mentioned on the authority of Abu Malik, and on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and on the authority of Marra Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, on the authority of some of the companions of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “No child was born to Adam except that a girl was born with him. He would marry the boy of this womb to the girl of another womb, and he would marry the girl of this womb to the boy of another womb, until two were born to him, called Qabil and Abel. Qabil was a farmer, and Abel was a milk-producing woman. Qabil was the older of the two, and he had a sister who was more beautiful than Abel’s sister. Abel asked to marry Qabil’s sister, but he refused and said: She is my sister who was born with me, and she is more beautiful than your sister, and I am more worthy to marry her. So his father ordered him to marry her to Abel, but he refused. They both offered a sacrifice to God, which of them had more right to the girl. Adam was away from them at that time, that is, in Mecca, looking at her. God said: To Adam: O Adam, do you know that I have a house on earth? He said: No, by God. He said: I have a house in Mecca, so go to it. Adam said to the heaven: Keep my son in trust, but it refused. He said to the earth, but it refused. He said to the mountains, but they refused. He said to Cain, but it refused. He said to the jinn, but it refused. He said to Cain, and the jinn said: Yes, you can go and come back and find your wife as you please. When Adam set out and offered a sacrifice, Cain used to boast to him, saying: I have more right to her than you; she is my sister, I am older than you, and I am my father’s successor. When they offered it, Abel offered a fat, young palm tree, and Abel offered a bundle of ears of corn. He found a large ear of corn in it, so he rubbed it and ate it. Then the fire came down and consumed Abel’s sacrifice and left Cain’s sacrifice. Cain became angry and said: I will surely kill you so that you will not marry my sister. Abel said:
h
God accepts only from the righteous. If you should stretch out your hand against me to kill me - I will not stretch out my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds.

(al-Ma’idah 5:5) 27-28) ... to His saying So his soul prompted him to kill his brother (al-Ma’idah 5:30). So he sought him out to kill him. The boy finished with him on the mountaintops. One day, he came to him while he was herding his sheep on a mountain, and he was asleep. He lifted a rock and smashed his head open with it, so he died and was left in the open, not knowing how to bury him. So God sent two ravens, brothers, and they fought. One of them killed the other, so he dug a grave for him, then threw dirt on him. When he saw him, he said: Would that I could not be like this raven and cover my brother’s shame (al-Ma’idah 5:31). So this is the saying of God Almighty So God sent a raven scratching the ground to show him how to cover his brother’s shame (al-Ma’idah 5:31). So Adam returned and found that his son had killed his brother. That is when He says: “Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains” ... to the end of the verse. The most correct of the statements on this matter is what was said by those who said: What is meant by trust in this place is all the meanings of trusts in religion and the trusts of people. This is because God did not specify in His statement,
h
We offered the trust
, some of the meanings of trusts for what we have described. And similar to what we said, the people of interpretation said about the meaning of God’s statement, Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.
b.via: some of the companions of the Prophet

x: Who said that?

c: Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant, meaning Cain, when he was entrusted with the trust of Adam, he did not protect his family for him.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And man bore it
, Adam said, Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant. He said: Unjust to himself, ignorant of what he bore between himself and his Lord.

c: Ali told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant. He was deceived by the command of God.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant. He said: Unjust to it, meaning to the trust, ignorant of its right.

x: God Almighty says: And man was entrusted with the Trust so that God might punish the hypocrites therein who appear to be performing God’s obligations, believing in them, while they conceal their disbelief in them, and the hypocritical women and the polytheists who worship God in their worship of Him as gods and idols, “and the polytheistic women. And God will turn in mercy to the believing men and believing women” He returns them to His obedience and fulfilling the trusts that He has imposed upon them until they fulfill them. And God is Forgiving of the sins of the believing men and believing women, by covering them up and not punishing them for them, Merciful that He does not punish them for them after they have repented from them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Suwar bin Abdullah Al-Anbari told us: My father told us: Abu Al-Ashhab told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: that he used to recite this verse: Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains until he finished: That God may punish the hypocritical men and hypocritical women, and the polytheistic men and polytheistic women. Then he would say: The two who betrayed it, the two who wronged it: the hypocrite and the polytheist.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: That God may punish the hypocritical men and hypocritical women, and the polytheistic men and polytheistic women. These are the two who betrayed it, and God will accept the repentance of the believing men and believing women. These are the two who fulfilled it. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.

evidence.text: Suwar bin Abdullah Al-Anbari told us: My father told us: Abu Al-Ashhab told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that he used to recite this verse: Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains until he finished: That God may punish the hypocritical men and hypocritical women, and the polytheistic men and polytheistic women.

notes.en: T1 reads: “they do.” This is Abū ʿAmr’s sole reading; Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah, and al-Kisāʾī read it with tāʾ. The Seven Readings, p. 518; al-Kashf ʿan wujūh al-qirāʾāt 2/193.

notes.en: Ṣ reads: “God is sufficient for you regarding what He commands you, and He is a guardian over you”; M: “God is sufficient for you regarding what He commands you, as trustee and guardian over you”; T1: “God is sufficient as caretaker of what He commands you, and guardian over you”; T2 and T3: “God is sufficient as caretaker in commanding you, and guardian over you.” The adopted wording is required by the context and conveys the meaning the author gave earlier, 6/245 and 7/474, 580.

Al-Suyūṭī attributed this report in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/184 to the author, mentioning only its raised version; in 5/183 he attributed only its ending to the author and Ibn Abī Ḥātim. Ibn Saʿd transmitted the raised report in al-Ṭabaqāt 1/149; Abū Nuʿaym transmitted it in Dalāʾil al-nubuwwah (as cited in al-Bidāyah wa-l-nihāyah 3/535), through Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah. Ibn Abī Ḥātim (as cited in Ibn Kathīr’s Tafsīr 6/383), Tammām in his Fawāʾid (no. 1399, Rawḍ edition), and Abū Nuʿaym in Dalāʾil al-nubuwwah (no. 2) transmitted it as a raised report through Saʿīd ibn Bashīr, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan, from Abū Hurayrah.

notes.en: Ibn Hishām’s Sīrah 2/231–233. Aḥmad (5/392, Maymaniyyah edition) and the author in his History 2/579 transmitted it through Ibn Isḥāq.
notes.ar: سيرة ابن هشام 2/ 231 - 233، وأخرجه أحمد (5/ 392) (الميمنية)، والمصنف في التاريخ 2/ 579، من طريق ابن إسحاق به.

notes.en: Mujāhid’s Tafsīr, pp. 547–548. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/187 to al-Firyābī, Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 547، 548، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 187 إلى الفريابي وابن أبي شيبة وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: T1 reads: “he digs the trench.”
notes.ar: في ت 1: "يحفر الخندق".

notes.en: T2 reads: “with him.”
notes.ar: في ت 2: "معه".

notes.en: T1 reads: “at its environs.” ʿAqwat al-dār means around the house and nearby. Al-Nihāyah 3/283.
notes.ar: في ت 1: "بعقيرة"، وعقوة الدار: حولها وقريبا منها. النهاية 3/ 283.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted an abridged version in his Tafsīr 2/113 from Maʿmar, from Qatādah. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/187 to Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 113 عن معمر، عن قتادة مختصرا، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 187 إلى ابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Al-Bayhaqī transmitted it in al-Dalāʾil 3/433 through Muḥammad ibn Saʿd. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/185 to Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه البيهقى في الدلائل 3/ 433 من طريق محمد بن سعد به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 185 إلى ابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Ibn Hishām’s Sīrah 2/245.
notes.ar: سيرة ابن هشام 2/ 245.

notes.en: Mujāhid’s Tafsīr, p. 548. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/187 to al-Firyābī, Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 548، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 187 إلى الفريابي وابن أبي شيبة وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Shaybah transmitted it 14/416; al-Bukhārī (no. 4103), Muslim (no. 3020), al-Nasāʾī in al-Kubrā (no. 11398), and al-Bayhaqī in al-Dalāʾil 3/433 transmitted it through ʿAbdah. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/185 to Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 14/ 416، والبخارى (4103)، ومسلم (3020)، والنسائي في الكبرى (11398)، والبيهقى في الدلائل 3/ 433 من طريق عبدة به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 185 إلى ابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Omitted from the manuscripts; supplied from the source cited for the report.
notes.ar: سقط من النسخ، والمثبت من مصدر التخريج.

notes.en: The author’s History, al-Istīʿāb 3/1392, Usd al-ghābah 5/161, and al-Iṣābah 6/98 read: “Masʿūd.”
notes.ar: في تاريخ المصنف، والاستيعاب 3/ 1392، وأسد الغابة 5/ 161، والإصابة 6/ 98: "مسعود".

notes.en: This is how it appears in the manuscripts and the author’s History. Ibn Hishām’s Sīrah 2/219, Muʿjam mā istaʿjam 2/698, Muʿjam al-buldān 2/931, and Tāj al-ʿarūs, root z-gh-b, read: “Zughābah,” differing on whether the zāy has fatḥah or ḍammah, and whether the middle consonant is ʿayn or ghayn. See Sharḥ gharīb al-sīrah al-khushnī 3/5.
notes.ar: كذا في النسخ، وتاريخ المصنف، وورد في سيرة ابن هشام 2/ 219، ومعجم ما استعجم 2/ 698، ومعجم البلدان 2/ 931، وتاج العروس (ز غ ب): "زغابة"، على اختلاف في فتح الزاي وضمها، وهل هي بالعين المهملة أم بالغين المعجمة. وينظر شرح غريب السيرة للخشنى 3/ 5.

notes.en: The Aḥābīsh were Banū al-Muṣṭaliq and Banū al-Hawn ibn Khuzaymah. They gathered at a mountain below Mecca called Ḥubshī and allied with Quraysh, so they were called Quraysh’s Aḥābīsh. Lisān al-ʿArab, root ḥ-b-sh.
notes.ar: الأحابيش: هم بنو المصطلق وبنو الهون بن خزيمة، اجتمعوا عند جبل بأسفل مكة يُسمى: حُبشى، وتحالفوا مع قريش، فسمّوا: أحابيش قريش. اللسان (ح ب ش).

notes.en: Āṭām are palaces or fortresses; the singular is uṭum. Sharḥ gharīb al-sīrah 3/5.
notes.ar: الآطام: القصور، ويقال: الحصون، واحدها أُطُم. شرح غريب السيرة 3/ 5.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, and T2 read: “he shut.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2: "غلق".

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, and T2 read: “she shut.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2: "غلقت".

notes.en: M adds after it: “I became apprehensive.”
notes.ar: بعده في م: "تخوفت".

notes.en: Jashīshah is a food made from jashīsh, coarsely ground wheat. Common speech calls it dashīsh with dāl, but jīm is correct. Same source.
notes.ar: الجشيشة: طعام يُصنع من الجشيش، وهو البر يطحن غليظا، وهو الذي تقول له العامة: دَشيش، بالدال، والصواب فيه بالجيم. المصدر السابق.

notes.en: Aḥfaẓahu means “he angered him”; ḥafīẓah means anger. Same source.
notes.ar: أحفظه: أغضبه، والحفيظة الغضب. المصدر السابق

notes.en: The author’s History—the source for this report—and Ibn Hishām’s Sīrah read: “ṭāmm.” Ṭamma al-shayʾu yaṭimmu ṭumūman means “the thing became abundant until it grew great or spread everywhere.” One also says the sea or water ṭamma. Ṭāmm means something immense or abundant water; here it signifies abundance. Al-Wasīṭ, root ṭ-m-m.
notes.ar: في تاريخ المصنف - مصدر التخريج -، وسيرة ابن هشام: طامّ. وطمّ الشيء يطِم طمومًا: كثر حتى عظم أو عمّ. ويقال: طمّ البحر أو الماء. والطامّ: الشيء العظيم، والماء الكثير، وهو كناية عن الكثرة - الوسيط (ط م م).

notes.en: M reads: “its leaders and chiefs.”
notes.ar: في م: "قاداتها وساداتها".

notes.en: Jahām is a cloud that has emptied its rain. The meaning is: what you offer me has no good in it, like a rainless cloud. Al-Nihāyah 1/323.
notes.ar: الجهام: السحاب الذي فرغ ماؤه، والمعنى: أي الذي تعرضه عليَّ لا خير فيه، كالجهام الذي لا ماء فيه النهاية 1/ 323.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, and T2 read: “he accepts it.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2: "يقبله".

notes.en: Ghārib is the front of a camel’s hump; dhurwah is its top. “He handles him at the hump and shoulder” means he kept coaxing and deceiving him, as one calms a skittish camel by stroking its back until it becomes docile and accepts the halter. Same source.
notes.ar: الغارب: مقدم سِنام البعير، والذروة أعلاه. أما: يقتله في الذروة والغارب فأراد أنه لم يزل يخدعه كما يُخدع البعير إذا كان نافرًا فيُمسح باليد على ظهره حتى يستأنس فيجعل الخطام على رأسه. المصدر السابق.

notes.en: Samaḥa means “he was easygoing and gentle.” Al-Wasīṭ, root s-m-ḥ.
notes.ar: سمح: سهل ولان. الوسيط (س م ح).

notes.en: M reads: “He gave them.”
notes.ar: في م: "أعطاهم".

notes.en: Omitted in M.
notes.ar: سقط من: م.

notes.en: M reads: “Daylam, brother of.”
notes.ar: في م: "ديلم أخو".

notes.en: M reads: “I know him.” Laḥn is wording that differs from the apparent meaning. One says laḥantu lahu when one speaks so that a person understands while others do not. The meaning is: signal to me without speaking plainly, and allude to what you know. Sharḥ gharīb al-sīrah 3/5; al-Nihāyah 4/241.
notes.ar: في م: "أعرفه"، واللحن أن يخالف ظاهر الكلام معناه، ويقال: لحنت لفلان، إذا قلت له قولا يفهمه ويخفى على غيره، والمعنى: أشيروا إليَّ ولا تُفصِحوا، وعرِّضوا بما علمتم. شرح غريب السيرة 3/ 5، والنهاية 4/ 241.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, and T2 read: “Do not weaken people’s resolve.” One says fatta fī ʿaḍudihi when he weakens and undermines someone. Sharḥ gharīb al-sīrah 3/5.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2: "ولا تفتوا أعضاد الناس"، ويقال: فتَّ في عضده إذا ضعَّفه وأوهنه. شرح غريب السيرة 3/ 5.

notes.en: Arbā means “greater.” Same source.
notes.ar: أربى: أعظم. المصدر السابق.

notes.en: Najama al-shayʾ means “the thing emerged and appeared.” Lisān al-ʿArab, root n-j-m.
notes.ar: نجم الشيءُ: طلع وظهر. اللسان (ن ج م).

notes.en: Ibn Hishām’s Sīrah 2/214–223. The author transmitted it in his History 2/565–566, 570–572.
notes.ar: سيرة ابن هشام 2/ 214 - 223، وأخرجه المصنف في تاريخه 2/ 565، 566، 570 - 572.

notes.en: Ibn Hishām’s Sīrah 2/246. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/187 to Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: سيرة ابن هشام 2/ 246، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 187 إلى ابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: T1 reads: “I became clear”; T2: “I appeared.” Nabwah means estrangement, roughness, or elevation. Nabāt bī tilka al-arḍ means “I found no settled place there”; nabā janbī ʿan al-firāsh means “my side was not comfortable on the bed”; and nabā al-shayʾ ʿannī means “the thing became distant from me.” Lisān al-ʿArab, root n-b-y.
notes.ar: في ت 1: "بينت"، وفي ت 2: "بدت"، والنَّبْوَةُ: الجَفوة والارتفاع والعلو، ونبت بي تلك الأرض: لم أجد بها قرارا، ونبا جنبى عن الفراش: لم يطمئن عليه، ونبا الشيءُ عنى يَنبو: أي تجافي وتباعد. اللسان (ن ب ى).

notes.en: Omitted in T2.
notes.ar: سقط من: ت 2.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Shaybah transmitted it 13/571, and Abū Nuʿaym in Ḥilyat al-awliyāʾ 3/338, through Ḥammād. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/187 to Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 13/ 571، وأبو نعيم في الحلية 3/ 338 من طريق حماد به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 187 إلى ابن المنذر.

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, T1, and T2.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، ت 1، ت 2.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/187 to the author and Ibn Abī Ḥātim. See Ibn Kathīr’s Tafsīr 6/389.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 187 إلى المصنف وابن أبي حاتم. وينظر تفسير ابن كثير 6/ 389.

notes.en: Omitted in M.
notes.ar: سقط من: م.

notes.en: This is the reading of ʿĀṣim in Abū Bakr’s transmission, Nāfiʿ, and Ibn ʿĀmir. The Seven Readings, p. 519; al-Taysīr, p. 144.
notes.ar: هي قراءة عاصم في رواية أبي بكر، ونافع، وابن عامر. السبعة ص 519، والتيسير ص 144.

notes.en: This is the reading of Ibn Kathīr, al-Kisāʾī, and ʿĀṣim in Ḥafṣ’s transmission. See the preceding two references.
notes.ar: هي قراءة ابن كثير، والكسائي، وعاصم في رواية حفص. ينظر المصدران السابقان.

notes.en: This is the reading of Abū ʿAmr and Ḥamzah. See the preceding two references.
notes.ar: هي قراءة أبي عمرو، وحمزة، ينظر المصدران السابقان.

notes.en: All the readings are correct.
notes.ar: القراءات كلها صواب.

notes.en: M reads: “the alif.”
notes.ar: في م: "الألف".

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, T1, and T2.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، ت 1، ت 2.

notes.en: Mujāhid’s Tafsīr, p. 548. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/187 to al-Firyābī, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 548، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 187 إلى الفريابي وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: M reads: “He says.”
notes.ar: في م: "يقول".

notes.en: Ibn Hishām’s Sīrah 2/222, 246; al-Ṭūsī cited it in al-Tibyān 8/291. Al-Bayhaqī transmitted an extended version in al-Dalāʾil 3/435 through Ibn Isḥāq, from Yazīd ibn Rūmān, from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, as his statement. Al-Suyūṭī likewise attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/186 to Ibn Isḥāq and Ibn al-Mundhir from ʿUrwah. Ibn Hishām cited it in his Sīrah 2/245 from Ibn Isḥāq as his statement.
notes.ar: سيرة ابن هشام 2/ 222، 246، وذكره الطوسى في التبيان 8/ 291، وأخرجه البيهقي في الدلائل 3/ 435 من طريق ابن إسحاق، عن يزيد بن رومان، عن عروة بن الزبير من قوله مطولا، وكذلك عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 186 إلى ابن إسحاق وابن المنذر عن عروة، وذكره ابن هشام في السيرة 2/ 245 عن ابن إسحاق من قوله.

notes.en: Mujāhid’s Tafsīr, p. 548. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/187 to al-Firyābī, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 548، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 187 إلى الفريابي وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted a similar report in his Tafsīr 2/1103 from Maʿmar, from Qatādah. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/187 to Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 1103 عن معمر عن قتادة بنحوه، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 187 إلى ابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, and T2 add after it: “So-and-so said this; he said…”
notes.ar: بعده في ص، ت 1، ت 2: "قال هذا فلان قال".

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, and T2 read: “he says.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2: "يقول".

notes.en: M reads: “my mouth.”
notes.ar: في م: "فمي".

notes.en: M reads: “the two shaykhs’ redoubt.” Al-Ajumm is one of the ājām of Medina; it has the same meaning as uṭum. Medina’s ājām and āṭām were its fortresses and palaces; al-Shaykhān is a place in Medina. Muʿjam al-buldān 1/135–136 and 3/348.
notes.ar: في م: "أحمر الشيخين"، والأجم واحد آجام المدينة، وهو بمعنى الأُطُم، وآجامُ المدينة وآطامُها: حصونها وقصورها، والشيخان: موضع بالمدينة. معجم البلدان 1/ 135، 136، 3/ 348.

notes.en: Al-Midhād is a place in Medina. Muʿjam al-buldān 4/468.
notes.ar: المذاد: موضع بالمدينة. معجم البلدان 4/ 468.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, and T2 read: “he reached it”; the sources cited for the report read: “he cut it off.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2: "بلغه"، وفي مصادر التخريج: "قطعه".

notes.en: M reads: “so they differed”; T1 and T2: “so they disputed.” Iḥtaqqū means “they quarreled”; taḥāqquq is disputation; ḥāqqahu means “he disputed with him, each claiming the right.” Lisān al-ʿArab and Tāj al-ʿarūs, root ḥ-q-q.
notes.ar: في م: "فاختلف"، وفي ت 1، ت 2: "فاحتنق"، واحتق: تخاصم، والتَّحاقُّ: التخاصم، وحاقَّه: خاصمه وادعى كل واحد منهما الحقَّ. اللسان، والتاج (ح ق ق).

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, T1, and T2.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، ت 1، ت 2.

notes.en: The manuscripts read: “Dūbār”; the author’s History reads: “Dhūbāb”; al-Baghawī’s Tafsīr: “Dhī Nāb.” The adopted form is from Ibn Saʿd’s al-Ṭabaqāt. Dhubāb is a mountain in Medina mentioned in accounts of campaigns and historical reports. Muʿjam al-buldān 2/716.
notes.ar: في النسخ: "دوبار"، وفى تاريخ المصنف: "ذوباب"، وفي تفسير البغوي: "ذي ناب"، والمثبت من طبقات ابن سعد، وذباب: جبل بالمدينة له ذكر في المغازي والأخبار البلدان 2/ 716.

notes.en: M reads: “al-ṣarī.” Nadā al-arḍ means the ground’s moisture and dampness. Lisān al-ʿArab, roots ṣ-r-y and n-d-y.
notes.ar: في م: "الصرى"، ندى الأرض: نداوتها وبللها. اللسان (ص ر ي، ن د ى).

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, and T2 read: “with our iron.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2: "بحديدنا".

notes.en: M reads: “it comes”; T2: “you imagine.” Ḥāka fī kadhā means “it left an impression on it.” Al-Wasīṭ, root ḥ-y-k.
notes.ar: في م: "يجيء"، وفي ت 2: "تخيل"، وحاك في كذا: أثَّر فيه. الوسيط (ح ى ك).

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, T1, and T2.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، ت 1، ت 2.

notes.en: The manuscripts read: “it shone for me from it”; the author’s History is the source for the adopted wording.
notes.ar: في النسخ: "أضاء لى منه"، والمثبت من تاريخ المصنف.

notes.en: M reads: “so it covered.”
notes.ar: في م: "فطبقت".

notes.en: The author transmitted it in his History 2/567. Al-Bayhaqī in al-Dalāʾil 3/418 and al-Baghawī in his Tafsīr 6/323 transmitted it through Muḥammad ibn Khālid. Ibn Saʿd in al-Ṭabaqāt 4/82–83, al-Ṭabarānī (no. 6040), and al-Ḥākim 3/598 transmitted abridged versions through Kathīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/185–186 to Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abū Nuʿaym.
notes.ar: أخرجه المصنف في تاريخه 2/ 567، وأخرجه البيهقي في الدلائل 3/ 418، والبغوي في تفسيره 6/ 323 من طريق محمد بن خالد به، وأخرجه ابن سعد في طبقاته، 4/ 82، 83، والطبراني (6040)، والحاكم 3/ 598 - كلاهما مختصرًا - من طريق كثير بن عبد الله به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 185، 186 إلى ابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه وأبي نعيم.

notes.en: Its source was given above, 18/231.
notes.ar: تقدم تخريجه في 18/ 231.

notes.en: Ibn Hishām’s Sīrah 2/222, 246. The author transmitted an extended version in his History 2/570 from Ibn Ḥumayd, from Salamah, from Ibn Isḥāq, as his statement. Al-Qurṭubī cited it in his Tafsīr 14/148.

notes.en: This is the reading of Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim in Abū Bakr’s transmission, Ḥamzah, and al-Kisāʾī. The reading with ḍammah is ʿĀṣim’s reading in Ḥafṣ’s transmission and is mass-transmitted. See The Seven Readings, p. 520, and al-Taysīr, p. 145.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr cited it in his Tafsīr, 6/414, from the compiler. ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr, 2/116–117, and Ibn Saʿd in al-Ṭabaqāt, 8/199–200, through Maʿmar from Qatādah.

Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 5/200, to al-Firyābī, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and Ibn Mardawayh.

notes.en: M and T2 read “confluence.” The root (jamʿ) of anything is its point of gathering. It is said, “This chapter is the confluence of these chapters,” meaning the one that gathers and encompasses them. See al-Wasīṭ, root j-m-ʿ. Al-Zaylaʿī cited the report in Takhrīj al-Kashshāf, 3/110, from the compiler; Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 6/417; and al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 5/201, to Ibn Abī Ḥātim …

notes.en: The claim that the Prophet ﷺ admired Zaynab bint Jaḥsh while she was still married to Zayd, and was eager for Zayd to divorce her so that he could marry her himself, is considered incorrect by authoritative Qur’an commentators. See al-Qurṭubī’s Tafsīr, 14/189–191, and Aḍwāʾ al-bayān, 6/580 ff.
notes.ar: القول بأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقع منه استحسان لزينب بنت جحش وهى في عصمة زيد، وكان حريصًا على أن يطلقها زيد فيتزوجها هو. قول غير صحيح عند أهل التحقيق مِن المفسرين. ينظر في الرد عليه تفسير القرطبي 14/ 189 - 191، وأضواء البيان 6/ 580 وما بعدها.

notes.en: Al-Bukhārī (no. 4787) and al-Ṭabarānī, 24/43 (no. 116), transmitted it through Ḥammād ibn Zayd.
notes.ar: أخرجه البخارى (4787)، والطبراني 24/ 43 (116) من طريق حماد بن زيد به.

notes.en: Al-Bayhaqī transmitted it in Dalāʾil al-nubuwwah, 3/466, through Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah. Ibn Abī Ḥātim—as cited in al-Fatḥ, 8/523—transmitted it through ʿAlī ibn Zayd, with an addition at its end. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 5/203, to al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī.
notes.ar: أخرجه البيهقي في دلائل النبوة 3/ 466 مِن طريق سفيان بن عيينة به، وأخرجه ابن أبي حاتم - كما في الفتح 8/ 523 من طريق على بن زيد به، بزيادة في آخره. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 203 إلى الحكيم الترمذي.

notes.en: Al-Tirmidhī transmitted it at length (no. 3207) through Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind. Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr—as cited in al-Durr al-manthūr, 5/202—and through him al-Ṭabarānī, 24/41 (no. 111), Aḥmad, 6/241, 266 (al-Maymaniyyah edition), Muslim (no. 287/177), al-Tirmidhī (no. 3208), and al-Nasāʾī in al-Kubrā (no. 11408) transmitted it through Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, from ʿĀmir al-Shaʿbī, from Masrūq, from ʿĀʾishah. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and Ibn Mardawayh.

notes.en: Aḥmad transmitted it, 16/396 (no. 10678), through ʿAwf al-Aʿrābī. Al-Bukhārī (nos. 3404, 4799) and al-Tirmidhī (no. 3221) transmitted it through ʿAwf with a connected chain mentioning Abū Hurayrah. See al-Jarḥ wa-l-taʿdīl, 1/237.
notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد 16/ 396 (10678) من طريق عوف الأعرابي به، والبخارى (3404، 4799)، والترمذى (3221) من طريق عوف به موصولًا بذكر أبى هريرة، وينظر الجرح والتعديل 1/ 237.

notes.en: M reads “he was shy, so he would cover himself”; T1 reads “he would cover himself”; T2 reads “from it, and the covering, he would wash.” The established wording is that in Aḥmad’s Musnad.
notes.ar: في م: "حييًّا فكان يتستر"، وفى ت 1: "يستتر"، وفى ت 2: "منه والستر يغتسل". والمثبت من مسند أحمد.

notes.en: M and T2 read “or.”
notes.ar: في م، ت 2: "أو".

notes.en: M reads “their middle.”
notes.ar: في م: "توسطهم".

notes.en: M reads “manliness”; T1 reads “Marwah”; T2 reads “Farwah.” The established reading is that in Aḥmad’s Musnad.
notes.ar: في م: "مروءة"، وفى ت:1 "مروة"، وفى ت: "فروة"، والمثبت من مسند أحمد.

notes.en: T1 and T2 read “beware of you” (feminine).
notes.ar: في ت 1، ت 2: "اياكي".

notes.en: Aḥmad transmitted it, 15/44 (no. 9091), through Qatādah. Al-Bukhārī (nos. 4799, 3404) and al-Tirmidhī (no. 3221) transmitted it through al-Ḥasan.
notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد 15/ 44 (9091) من طريق قتادة به، وأخرجه البخارى (4799،3404)، والترمذي (3221) من طريق الحسن به.

notes.en: T1 and T2 read “call them by their fathers’ names.”
notes.ar: في ت 1، ت 2: "ادعاوهم".

notes.en: The manuscripts read “Ḥabīb,” a scribal corruption; the established reading is correct. See Tahdhīb al-Kamāl, 11/139.
notes.ar: في النسخ: "حبيب" وهو تصحيف، والمثبت هو الصواب ينظر تهذيب الكمال 11/ 139.

notes.en: Rukham: a well-known kind of bird; singular rakhmah. It is described as treacherous and vile, or as filthy. See al-Nihāyah, 2/212.
notes.ar: الرخم: نوع من الطير معروف، واحدته رَخَمة، وهو موصوف بالغدر والموق. وقيل بالقذر. النهاية 2/ 212.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 6/475, from the compiler. Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ—as cited in al-Maṭālib al-ʿāliyah (nos. 3819, 4066)—al-Ṭaḥāwī in Mushkil al-āthār, 1/68, Ibn Abī Ḥātim—as cited in Ibn Kathīr’s Tafsīr, 6/474–475—and al-Ḥākim, 2/579, transmitted it. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 5/223, to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 6/ 475 عن المصنف، وأخرجه أحمد بن منيع - كما في المطالب العالية (3819، 4066) - والطحاوى في مشكل الآثار 1/ 68، وابن أبي حاتم - كما في تفسير ابن كثير 6/ 474، 475، - والحاكم 2/ 579، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 223 إلى ابن المنذر وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Omitted in M and T1.

notes.ar: بعده في ت 2: "جميعا".

notes.en: Tafsīr Mujāhid, p. 552. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 5/224, to Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 552، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 224 إلى ابن أبي شيبة وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 5/224, to the compiler, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim, citing only its opening. See also al-Baghawī’s Tafsīr, 6/379.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 224 إلى المصنف وعبد بن حميد وابن أبي حاتم مقتصرًا على أوله، وينظر تفسير البغوي 6/ 379.

notes.en: Al-Baghawī mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 6/379; Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr, 6/476; and Abū Ḥayyān in al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ, 7/253.
notes.ar: ذكره البغوي في تفسيره 6/ 379، وابن كثير في تفسيره 6/ 476، وأبو حيان في البحر المحيط 7/ 253.

notes.en: Omitted in T2.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 5/225, to the compiler and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 225 إلى المصنف وعبد بن حميد.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 6/477, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 5/225, to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 6/ 477 عن الضحاك به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 225 إلى عبد بن حميد.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 6/477, from the compiler. Ibn al-Anbārī transmitted it in al-Aḍdād, pp. 388–389, and al-Ḥākim, 2/422, through Shuʿbah. Ibn al-Anbārī’s version has Mujāhid in place of Ibn Jubayr. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 5/225, to Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 6/ 477 عن المصنف، وأخرجه ابن الأنباري في الأضداد ص 388، 389، والحاكم 2/ 422 من طريق شعبة به، ووقع عند الأنباري عن مجاهد بدلًا من ابن جبير، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 225 إلى سعيد بن منصور وابن أبي شيبة وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Ibn al-Anbārī transmitted it in al-Aḍdād, pp. 389–390, through ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 5/224–225, to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: أخرجه الأنباري في الأضداد ص 389، 390 من طريق عبد الله بن صالح به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 224، 225 إلى ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.ar: في م: "عليها".

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 6/477, from al-ʿAwfī with this chain. Al-Ṭūsī also mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 8/333.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 6/ 477 عن العوفى به، والطوسى في تفسيره 8/ 333.

notes.en: T1 reads “al-Zuhrī.”
notes.ar: في ت 1: "الزهرى".

notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 125 عن الثورى عن غير واحد عن الضحاك، وعزاه السيوطي في =

notes.ar: = الدر المنثور 5/ 225 إلى عبد بن حميد.

notes.en: M reads “ʿAmr”; T1 and T2 read “ʿUmar.” See above, 1/136. Ibn Ḥajar said in al-Iṣābah, 2/108: “Perhaps his father’s name was ʿAmr, but it was shortened and he became known by that.”
notes.ar: في م: "عمرو"، وفى ت 1، ت 2: "عمر"، ينظر ما تقدم في 1/ 136، وقال ابن حجر في الإصابة 2/ 108: ولعل أباه كان اسمه عَمْرًا فصغر واشتهر بذلك.

notes.en: T1 reads “it will be, and what they bring”; T2 reads “it will be, and what they live.”
notes.ar: في ت 1: "يكون وما يجيبون"، وفى ت 2: "يكون وما يحيون".

notes.en: Omitted in M.
notes.ar: سقط من: م.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 6/479, from the compiler, saying: “This is a very unusual hadith, and it has corroborating reports through other routes.” Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 5/226, to the compiler and graded it weak.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 6/ 479 عن المصنف، وقال: هذا حديث غريب جدًّا، وله شواهد من وجوه أخرى، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 226 إلى المصنف وضعفه.

notes.en: M reads “al-ʿAwwām al-ʿAṭṭār”; T1 and T2 read “Abū al-ʿAwwām al-ʿAṭṭār.” Abū al-ʿAwwām al-Qaṭṭān is ʿImrān ibn Dāwar al-Aʿmā, Abū al-ʿAwwām al-Qaṭṭān al-Baṣrī. See Tahdhīb al-Kamāl, 22/328.
notes.ar: في م: "العوام العطار"، وفى ت 1، ت 2: "أبو العوام العطار"، وأبو العوام القطان، هو عمران بن دَاوَر العمى أبو العوام القطان البصري. ينظر تهذيب الكمال 22/ 328.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 6/479. Abū Dāwūd (no. 429), al-Ṭabarānī in al-Ṣaghīr, 2/5, and Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilyah, 2/234, transmitted it through ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Majīd. Al-Ṭabarānī does not include Abū al-Dardāʾ’s statement. Abū Nuʿaym transmitted it in Akhbār Iṣfahān, 2/189, through Abū al-ʿAwwām al-Qaṭṭān, without Abū al-Dardāʾ’s statement.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 6/ 479، وأخرجه أبو داود (429)، والطبراني في الصغير 2/ 5، وأبو نعيم في الحلية 2/ 234 من طريق عبيد الله بن عبد بن المجيد به، وقول أبي الدرداء لم يذكره الطبراني، وأخرجه أبو نعيم في أخبار أصبهان 2/ 189 من طريق أبى العوام القطان به، ولم يذكر قول أبي الدرداء.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr, 2/125, through al-Thawrī. Al-Ḥākim, 2/422, and al-Bayhaqī, 7/371, transmitted it through al-Aʿmash. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 5/226, to al-Firyābī, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 125 عن الثورى به، وأخرجه الحاكم 2/ 422، والبيهقى 7/ 371 من طريق الأعمش به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 226 إلى الفريابي وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 6/478–479, from the compiler.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 6/ 478، 479 عن المصنف.

notes.ar: أخرجه الطبراني (10527)، وعنه أبو نعيم في الحلية 4/ 201 من طريق تميم بن المنتصر به، وأخرجه أبو نعيم في الحلية 4/ 201 من طريق شريك به موقوفًا.

notes.en: Shufr: the edge of anything; the shufr of an eyelid is its edge where the eyelashes grow. See al-Wasīṭ, root sh-f-r.
notes.ar: الشُّفر: حرف كل شيء، وشفر الجفن حرفه الذي ينبت عليه الهدب. الوسيط (ش ف ر).
